title: Rust 1.98 clippy result_large_err fails CI on main
description:
Rust 1.98.0, released 2026-08-18, tightened `clippy::result_large_err`. Five private helpers return `Result<T, OperationResult>`, and `OperationSuccess` is at least 128 bytes, so `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` now fails on pristine main:

- crates/selfie/src/package/service/audit.rs:207
- crates/selfie/src/package/service/check.rs:77, :100, :127
- crates/selfie/src/package/service/install.rs:417

Confirmed by running clippy 1.98 against a clean `git archive` of origin/main: 5 errors, no local edits. Every open PR fails clippy as soon as it re-runs, so this blocks the whole queue.

The `Err` here is not a failure. It carries an `OperationResult` the caller returns as-is, so it is an early-return channel rather than an error. Six signatures carry it (the five above plus `steps::handle_missing_environment`), and none is public.

Boxing the `Err` variant is clippy's own recommendation and keeps the blast radius inside the crate.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #120

title: sudo selfie sync pull/push leaves root-owned git objects in the user's repo
description:
Not caught by selfie-tcu2's refusal. create_sync_service builds a DotfileServiceImpl that carries the gate, but SyncServiceImpl only ever calls check_drift, which is (correctly) ungated -- so nothing in the sync path consults it.

sudo selfie sync pull runs gix against the user's package/dotfiles repository as root, writing objects, refs and index entries owned by root:root inside a repo the user owns. The next ordinary git or selfie sync fails on them.

Worse than the deploy-state case selfie-tcu2 describes: deploy state self-heals, because the rename comes from a user-owned temp file in a user-owned directory. Root-owned git objects do not.

Fix is probably to gate SyncService's write paths (push, pull) the same way, reusing privilege::refuse_sudo. Decide whether the port belongs on SyncServiceImpl or whether sync should consult the dotfile service it already holds.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Steve Loveless
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-09 on fix/refuse-sudo-selfie-tcu2 (PR #102), alongside selfie-tcu2.

WHAT WAS GATED: prepare_push, execute_push, pull. NOT status -- it writes nothing, same reasoning as
check_drift. prepare_push is gated as well as execute_push for two independent reasons: the CLI
prompts per proposed commit between the two, so refusing only at execution walks the user through
every prompt and then discards the answers; and the MCP server calls them as separate tool
invocations, so nothing guarantees the query ran first.

SHAPE: rather than give SyncServiceImpl its own copy of the privilege port plus the allow_root flag
-- two gates that can drift onto two rules, which the code review had flagged -- the pair became one
value, privilege::RootPolicy. refuse_sudo is now private, so RootPolicy is the only way to apply the
rule. DotfileServiceImpl holds one too, and the CLI builds both services from a single
root_policy(config), so --allow-root cannot reach one service and miss the other.

Sync does NOT read the policy back out of the DotfileService it already holds: DotfileService is a
port about dotfiles, and giving it a "what privilege am I running with" accessor would put a question
there that has nothing to do with the port's job.

A DEFECT THIS INTRODUCED, AND HOW IT WAS FOUND: reusing SudoRefusal verbatim made `sudo selfie sync
push` refuse with "every dotfile in this run would be written as root, including the ones under your
home directory" -- on a command that writes no dotfile at all. No test caught it. Every test asserted
the refusal happened, which it did. It was found by running the binary under a real euid 0 in a
container, reading the output, and noticing the sentence was about the wrong thing.

SudoRefusal now carries a WriteScope so each path names its own damage. Its field is private, so
RootPolicy is the only thing that can mint a refusal -- an adapter cannot fabricate one, the way
BoundedText and GitMessage already work here.

MUTATIONS (same harness as selfie-tcu2's):
m5  prepare_push gate removed -> CAUGHT by prepare_push_is_refused_before_git_runs
m6  pull gate removed         -> CAUGHT by pull_is_refused_before_git_runs
m7  Repository message replaced with the Dotfiles one -> SURVIVED the whole suite. That is the
    defect above, reproduced as a mutation. Regression test added; re-run as m7b -> CAUGHT.

An earlier m5 attempt could not compile, because SudoRefusal's constructor is private outside the
privilege module. Reported as NEVER-RAN rather than counted, per the testing rules -- and it is
incidental evidence that the encapsulation holds.

The gate tests drive a GitSyncProvider that panics on every method, so a passing test proves the
refusal fired BEFORE git was reached rather than merely instead of reporting its result. A gate
placed after the git work returns the same error, so asserting on the error alone would not
distinguish them.

CONTAINER VERIFICATION: six cases under a real euid 0. sync push refused with 0 loose git objects
written; sync pull refused; sync status proceeded (read-only, correctly ungated).

title: A login profile that writes to stdout is spliced into resolved dotfile content
description:
Provider-sourced dotfile content is the command's ENTIRE stdout. When that command runs under a login shell, the login profile's own stdout is captured into the same stream and becomes part of the deployed file.

Mechanism, verified:
- ShellCommandRunner::login_shell (commands/shell.rs:77-92) sets login: true; build_command (:98-102) adds '-l', so the shell sources the user's login profile.
- run_capture (dotfile_service/resolve.rs) returns output.stdout() as the resolved content, byte for byte. Nothing separates profile output from command output -- they are the same fd.
- So a .zprofile / .bash_profile / config.fish containing an echo, a banner, a version-manager notice, or a 'motd'-style greeting produces content like 'banner\n<secret>' written into the target.

Why this matters more than a cosmetic corruption: the target is frequently a credentials file. A ~/.netrc, an ~/.aws/credentials, a token file with a leading banner line is silently malformed. The failure is quiet -- the deploy reports success, the file exists, and the breakage shows up later in whatever consumes it.

Existing gates do NOT catch it: the empty check (resolve.rs:175-179) passes because the content is non-empty, and MAX_CONTENT_BYTES (:180-182) passes because a banner makes it larger, not smaller, and only by a few bytes. There is no format validation -- by design, since selfie does not know what the target's format is.

ALREADY LIVE, not hypothetical: the MCP server has run provider commands under login_shell since 31bf6bc (mcp-server/src/server.rs:228), and install/check/audit have since 9e918a7. selfie-w8gd (U3) will extend it to CLI apply, which is where the bytes actually land in a credentials file -- so the exposure grows, but it is pre-existing and NOT introduced by that unit.

Nothing in the code or docs warns about it. docs/package-files.md says only that provider commands 'run through a shell'.

Fix directions, none obviously right:
- run the login shell so profile stdout is discarded and only the command's own output is captured (hard -- there is no clean fd separation through 'sh -l -c')
- warn when resolved provider content changes after a no-op command, or when a control run of ':' produces non-empty stdout -- a cheap heuristic that catches the common case
- document it as a sharp edge and tell users to keep profiles silent, which is the weakest option but honest

Found by the selfie-w8gd/selfie-fbwo plan author (U3 of the command-execution batch); mechanism verified independently by the lead against shell.rs and resolve.rs.
notes:
CORRECTIONS TO THE DESCRIPTION ABOVE, from the U3 plan reviewer, each verified independently by the lead. RAISED TO P1.

1. PROVENANCE WAS WRONG. The description says the MCP server has run provider commands under login_shell 'since 31bf6bc'. It has not. git show 31bf6bc (2026-03-17, 'Use login shell in MCP server for full user PATH') touches only crates/mcp-server/src/main.rs and crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs -- it gave the PACKAGE service a login shell. The DOTFILE service's login-shell runner in crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs came from f888761 (2026-07-27), 'feat(dotfiles): resolve secret-bearing content at apply time'. Verified with git log -S login_shell -- crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs.

So this is three days old, not four months. Still pre-existing, still not introduced by selfie-w8gd -- but 'long-standing and unremarked' was the wrong framing.

2. BLAST RADIUS WAS OVERSTATED. The description says the hazard is live on 'install/check/audit'. It is not. resolve_content has exactly ONE production caller -- SecretApply::resolve at dotfile_service/service.rs:719 (the only other hit is a test at resolve.rs:463). Dotfile apply is the sole path where a command's stdout becomes FILE CONTENT. install/check/audit do run a login shell, but their stdout goes to status and events, never into a credentials file.

Corrected scope: exposed on exactly ONE surface today -- the MCP tool selfie_apply_dotfiles. selfie-w8gd adds a second: CLI 'selfie apply'.

3. RAISED P2 -> P1. Fewer surfaces than first filed, but the reviewer's argument holds: this silently corrupts credential files, the deploy reports success, and no gate catches it. A quiet wrong-bytes-on-disk defect on the credential path outranks a loud failure.

4. ONE ASYMMETRY WORTH KNOWING, and it points at the fix. The Template/vars path DOES have a partial detector -- a binding value containing a newline emits 'dotfile var X contains a line break; it will be substituted as-is'. The whole-file Provider path, which is exactly where a spliced banner lands, has no equivalent. Filed separately.

NOT A REASON TO BLOCK selfie-w8gd. Same defect, correct fix, and the mitigation has to be made for the MCP path regardless. That unit is required to disclose it in docs/package-files.md instead.
close_reason: Closed

title: run_buffered discards pipe read errors and returns a partial buffer as complete
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:154 and :161 read a command's stdout and stderr with 'let _ = read_to_end(&mut out, &mut buf).await;'. An IO error part-way through the read is discarded and whatever was buffered so far is returned as if it were the command's complete output.

Consequences differ by path and the check path is the worst:
- check: a truncated stdout can flip a check result. A command whose output would have said 'installed' can be read as not installed, or the reverse, with no error surfaced.
- dotfile resolve: MAX_CONTENT_BYTES is checked against the truncated buffer, so a partial credential can pass the size cap and be written to the target. Same shape as the truncation hazard identified while evaluating selfie-mxo.
- audit and install: a partial log, reported as the whole.

Nothing distinguishes 'the command produced this' from 'the pipe failed and this is what we got'. run_buffered is the primitive behind execute, execute_with_timeout and execute_in_dir, so every non-streaming command path inherits it.

Fix: propagate the read error rather than discarding it. Note both reads happen in detached tokio tasks specifically to avoid the ~64KB pipe-buffer deadlock, so the error has to be carried back across the join rather than returned directly.

Found while planning selfie-mxo.
acceptance_criteria: A pipe read error surfaces as a command failure rather than a silently truncated buffer.
notes:
SEVERITY RAISED TO P1 after the selfie-mxo plan review enumerated the consumers. The bead as filed described a truncated buffer returned as complete. The four production consumers of that buffer make it worse than that framing:

1. crates/selfie/src/package/service/install.rs:268-269 uses stdout_str().trim() as an EXECUTABLE PATH. A partial read yields a truncated path — which either fails, or resolves to a DIFFERENT binary than the command reported. That is the worst of the four and was not in the original filing.
2. crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/resolve.rs:268 is the only production consumer of raw stdout(). A partial read writes a TRUNCATED CREDENTIAL to the target: bytes.len() > MAX_CONTENT_BYTES is then false, so the size cap at resolve.rs:181 — the only gate — does not fire. Verified by the reviewer against the code.
3. check.rs:261/271 — a truncated stdout can flip a check result.
4. audit.rs:266 — a partial source list reported as complete.

Exact sites: crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:157 and :164, both 'let _ = tokio::io::AsyncReadExt::read_to_end(&mut out, &mut buf).await;'. (Earlier note said 154/161; corrected against the tree.)

Note this is the SAME hazard that made selfie-mxo's proposed fix dangerous: pre-emptive truncation would defeat the post-hoc size cap on the credential path. mxo concluded truncation must never be introduced for that reason — and this bead is that failure already reachable without it.

Fix: propagate the read error rather than discarding it. Both reads happen in detached tokio tasks to avoid the ~64KB pipe-buffer deadlock, so the error must be carried back across the join rather than returned directly.
close_reason: Closed

title: dotfiles track accepts a symlinked target silently, deferring the refusal to a later apply
description:
After selfie-4m9, 'selfie apply' REFUSES to deploy to a symlinked target. But 'selfie dotfiles track' still accepts one without comment and records it as tracked.

The user therefore learns nothing at the moment they could act cheaply — when they are standing at the target, know why the symlink is there, and could 'rm' it in seconds — and instead gets a refusal at the next apply, possibly weeks later, with the context gone.

Verified by probe during selfie-4m9 implementation.

track already knows the target path and can stat it. It should say at track time that the target is a symlink and that apply will refuse it, ideally naming the destination. Whether it should refuse to track outright, or track with a warning, is the substance of this issue: refusing is more consistent, warning is friendlier if the user intends to remove the link before applying.

Related: selfie-paa5 would add an opt-in to follow symlinks, which changes what track should say.
acceptance_criteria: Tracking a symlinked target tells the user at track time that apply will refuse it.
notes:
RAISED P2 -> P1 (2026-07-31). Track does more than fail to warn: it silently copies the SYMLINK DESTINATION's content into the dotfiles repository, which sync push commits to a git remote. Chain verified independently, link by link, by the unit's plan author and again by its reviewer:

1. Track reads THROUGH the link. handle_track_standalone (service.rs:1626) and handle_track_for_package (service.rs:1755) both call filesystem.read_file(&expanded_target); RealFileSystem::read_file (fs/real.rs:33) is fs::read_to_string, which follows symlinks.
2. It copies the destination's content into the repo. Measured: target config.toml -> symlink -> real_secrets containing DESTINATION_CONTENT_TOKEN=abc123; after track, dotfiles/myapp/config.toml holds that content. Same for track_for_package.
3. Silently. Success(DotfileTracked{was_already_tracked:false}), ZERO warnings, both handlers.
4. It writes a spec -- dotfiles/myapp.yml, plain source/target entry.
5. It records deploy state for a deploy THAT NEVER HAPPENED: source_checksum == deployed_checksum == checksum of the link destination, with a deployed_at timestamp. The target is still a symlink; nothing was ever written to it.
6. sync push commits it. push discovers the repo by walking up from package_directory (sync_service/service.rs:284-287). track_for_package writes inside that repo unconditionally and is grouped by infer_package_name (service.rs:816-834), so no --include-ungrouped is needed. track_standalone writes into dotfiles_directory, which docs/sync.md:139 makes MANDATORY to be in the same repository.

So: another tool symlinks a credential-adjacent file into place (stow, yadm, Syncthing), the user tracks it, and its contents are copied into a repo that gets pushed. No warning at any step.

IT ALSO MANUFACTURES selfie-qvwq. The full timeline was reproduced: track (silent) -> drift reports drift_count=0 'in sync' -> apply silently skips -> user edits the repo file -> 'repo changed' FOREVER, apply refusing every round. The entire failure timeline in qvwq is created by the one track that said nothing.

DECIDED: REFUSE, not warn. The deciding argument, from the reviewer: there is NO configuration in which a tracked symlinked target does what the user asked. It is either permanently inert (destination content matches, nothing ever happens) or permanently broken (the moment the repo file is edited, apply refuses forever). Refusing removes an option that never worked. A warning cannot repair it either -- all three side effects are wrong independently, and there is no correct answer to 'which content' for a target that can never be deployed.

Also fixed by placing the refusal before the existence check: track on a DANGLING symlink today fails with 'Target file does not exist', which is misleading -- the named path does exist, it is a link, and path_exists follows.

Being fixed now as unit A of the target-semantics batch, alongside selfie-qvwq and selfie-86o.
close_reason: Closed

title: deny_unknown_fields on DotfileEntry reintroduces the YAML anchor bug 826e854 fixed
description:
Commit 826e854 ('fix: allow YAML anchors while still catching unknown fields') removed #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] from Package, EnvironmentConfig and DotfileEntry, replacing detection with a flatten-into-HashMap plus a validation pass that permits underscore-prefixed anchor keys and reports anything else as a field-level error. Provider-sourced dotfiles re-added the attribute to DotfileEntry to catch a 'var:' for 'vars:' typo, which reintroduces the bug that commit fixed.

Verified empirically against the merged tree:
  _anchor: &a hello  inside a dotfiles entry  ->  REJECTED, 'unknown field _anchor'
That is the exact '_brew: &brew' case named in 826e854's message.

Second consequence: a typo inside a dotfiles entry now fails the WHOLE package file to parse, so it drops out of valid_packages, taking that package's other dotfiles and all its install and check commands with it. The user gets 'skipping unparsable package file' rather than a field-level diagnostic naming the key, and none of the package's other issues are checked.

The typo-catching goal is right and the regression test for it should stay. The mechanism is the one already tried and deliberately backed out. Fix by extending the existing flatten-plus-validate mechanism down to DotfileEntry rather than by the attribute, so anchors keep working and a typo produces a field-level error.
acceptance_criteria: A YAML anchor inside a dotfiles entry parses; a misspelled key produces a field-level validation error rather than failing the whole file.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #71 (merged 6786b48). deny_unknown_fields replaced with a hand-written Deserialize for DotfileEntry that records unrecognized keys into unknown_keys and skips _-prefixed ones, so YAML anchors parse again and a misspelled key produces a field-level error instead of failing the whole package file. content_source() returns the existing ContentSource::Invalid so apply refuses the entry — fail-closed.

Two fail-open paths were found by review and closed in the same PR:
1. Removing deny_unknown_fields alone made apply report Success/deployed_count:1 while writing an unrendered '{{ api_key }}' over a credentials target. Found at the plan gate.
2. save_package re-serializes from the struct, so any load-mutate-save silently deleted the offending key and the NEXT apply deployed the credentials file. Guard placed inside save_package rather than at its callers — there are five production call sites, two of which (spec create, standalone dotfiles track) were on nobody's list. Found at final review.

serde(flatten) was deliberately avoided: it forecloses Spanned<T> on these fields, which d96b82c had to back out of Package for, and would block selfie-2wb.

Residual documented and tracked: selfie-kj5y (a _-prefixed key shadowing a real field, e.g. _vars:, deploys unrendered with no diagnostic).

title: Dotfile deploys write through symlinked targets
description:
expand_user_path (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:226) calls FileSystem::expand_path, which canonicalizes (crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:43). Canonicalization resolves symlinks, so perform_deploy receives a symlink-resolved target and writes through any symlink at the target path, silently overwriting the link's destination rather than replacing the link.

Security-relevant on its own: a symlink planted at a dotfile target redirects written content to a path the planter chose. It also nullifies the symlink protection of write_file_private for any caller that canonicalizes first, which constrains how secret-bearing dotfiles must resolve their target.

Deciding the right behavior is the work here: replacing a symlinked target is a behavior change for users who deliberately symlink their dotfiles, so this is not simply 'stop canonicalizing'.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy either refuses to write through a symlinked target or does so only by explicit opt-in; behavior is documented and tested.
notes:
Provider-sourced dotfiles (selfie-doh) deliberately does NOT route secret targets through expand_user_path. It uses its own expand_secret_target, which expands ~ and normalizes . and .. but never canonicalizes, so the final path component reaches write_file_private unresolved and its symlink guarantee actually holds for credential writes.

That divergence is intentional and load-bearing, not an oversight. Whoever fixes this issue must UNIFY the two expansions by bringing the repo-file path up to the secret path's behavior — not by deleting the secret path's expansion in the name of removing duplication, which would silently reintroduce the vulnerability for credentials.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #72 (merged 78ae893). Deploy now REFUSES a symlinked target via libc::O_NOFOLLOW rather than writing through it; the link and its destination are left untouched, a warning names both paths, and the entry is counted as skipped.

The bead's diagnosis was incomplete. Canonicalization in expand_user_path was half of it — fs::write follows a final-component symlink regardless — but fixing only the write leaves the main case broken, because the expansion hands the write site an already-resolved destination. Measured: each half alone produces IDENTICAL wrong behavior (destination overwritten, counted as deployed, no warning), which is why neither can be dropped as cleanup.

Three layers: expand_target_path no longer canonicalizes (the former expand_secret_target, body unchanged — the repository path was brought UP to the credential path's behavior, never the reverse); a check hoisted into handle_apply so dry-run does not preview a refused deploy and the conflict resolver is never asked an unanswerable question; and O_NOFOLLOW at the write as the only TOCTOU protection, pinned by the_writer_refuses_even_when_the_check_is_blinded (a decorator test with an AtomicUsize control).

REPLACE-the-symlink was considered and rejected: measured, it destroys a deliberate symlink on the unprompted RepoChanged path on the first ordinary apply after any repo edit. Opt-in to follow symlinks deliberately is selfie-paa5.

Ten attacks verified refused including the dangling-link case the bead predicted was already safe; TOCTOU confirmed kernel-enforced over 200 plant-then-write rounds.

title: Re-enable CI and cut Actions minute burn
description:
CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) was disabled_manually ~2026-03-25 because Actions minutes were being exhausted on this private repo. Result: ~4 months of pushes to main with zero automated verification. All four gates (typos, dprint, fmt, clippy, tests) pass locally on main today, so the workflow should go green once re-enabled.

Re-enable it, and reduce per-run cost so the credit problem does not recur:
- Skip runs for beads-only commits (9 of last 19 commits touched only .beads/issues.jsonl, each firing a full 5-job run).
- Consolidate 5 jobs into 2 to stop paying per-job minute rounding and a duplicated Rust compile across the clippy and build-and-test runners.
acceptance_criteria: CI workflow is enabled; a run on main completes green; per-run billable minutes reduced; beads-only commits do not trigger a run.
close_reason: CI re-enabled and green on PR #64; beads-only commits now skipped

title: MCP apply defaults auto_accept=true — silently overwrites divergent configs (data loss)
description: selfie_apply_dotfiles (MCP) defaults auto_accept=true, which auto-accepts DeployDecision::Conflict and overwrites the target (service.rs:661). A Conflict happens when a target exists, has no local deploy-state (NotTracked), and its content DIFFERS from the repo source — exactly the fresh-second-machine case (e.g. deploying home's configs onto the work machine, which has its own unpushed edits). Result: the other machine's config is silently clobbered with NO prompt. This violates the 'no silent failures / no data loss' principle and is worst on the AI-native path (the primary use case). Fix: when there is no interactive resolver (MCP/headless), the SAFE default must be to SKIP conflicts and report them (auto_accept=false), requiring explicit opt-in to overwrite. Consider also surfacing the diff in the conflict event so an AI/user can decide. Surfaced 2026-07-23 reasoning through cross-machine deploy safety.
close_reason: MCP apply now defaults auto_accept=false; conflicts skipped+reported with diff. Fixed in 3238cd6, test apply_param_defaults_auto_accept_to_false

title: Phase 1: Add recommends (soft deps) and login shell execution
description: Add 'recommends' field to package YAML for soft dependencies that install but don't cascade failure. Add --no-recommends flag. Switch CLI to login shell for install/check/audit (matching MCP server). See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-18-environment-manager-design.md
close_reason: Phase 1 shipped in PR #28

title: Standardize symbols — remove rogue emoji
description: P1: Several commands use emoji outside the canonical symbol system (✓ ✗ ⚠ ℹ ✨). Rogue emoji: 📋 in check.rs and validate.rs (results headers), 💡 in common.rs (suggestions — should use print_suggestion/✨), ⚠️ with variation selector U+FE0F in check.rs (renders as color emoji, looks different from text ⚠ used elsewhere). Fix: replace 📋 with a DisplayManager section header method, replace 💡 with print_suggestion, replace ⚠️ with ⚠.
close_reason: Implemented in commit a8ac5ff on feat/cli-display-consistency branch

title: Route all output through DisplayManager
description: P1: Half the commands bypass DisplayManager with bare println!(). This breaks MultiProgress coordination (will corrupt spinner output in Phase 2) and causes inconsistent stdout/stderr routing. Affected: check.rs, validate.rs, info.rs, list.rs summary, common.rs display_environment_summary/display_generic_environment_suggestion. Every user-facing output line should go through DisplayManager methods.
close_reason: Implemented in commit a8ac5ff on feat/cli-display-consistency branch

close_reason: Fixed: ran dprint fmt on 6 markdown files, added dprint fmt to PostToolUse hook, pushed to uat

title: Add dependency chain integration tests
description: The install handler resolves dependencies recursively, but tests don't exercise this path. Need tests for: single dependency, chain dependencies (A->B->C), missing dependency, and circular dependency (once detection is implemented). Use mock repo returning packages with dependency chains.
close_reason: Implemented circular dependency detection with DFS topological sort in deps.rs, restructured install handler for dependency chains, added 8 unit tests and 5 integration tests

title: Implement PackageService::create properly
description: PackageService::create returns a placeholder 'Create operation not yet implemented'. The CLI's create.rs bypasses PackageService entirely and directly uses PackageRepository -- constructing Package objects and GetPackage structs with pub fields. This breaks the hexagonal pattern. Implement the service method and have the CLI call it instead of going direct to the repository.
close_reason: Encapsulated GetPackage fields and implemented PackageService::create

title: Add circular dependency detection
description: The dependency resolution in install.rs follows dependencies linearly without cycle detection. If a user creates a cycle (A depends on B, B depends on A), installation would likely recurse infinitely or deadlock. Add cycle detection using a visited set to PackageService::install and/or validate.
close_reason: Implemented circular dependency detection with DFS topological sort in deps.rs, restructured install handler for dependency chains, added 8 unit tests and 5 integration tests

title: An unreadable file hiding environments: can deploy shared content over an override
description:
When a package file's top level cannot be re-parsed, apply warns and deploys anyway. That is the right default -- refusing would stop legal files over a check that did not run -- but the bound on its risk is wider than believed.

If the hidden key is 'environments:' itself (written '_environments:', or misspelled 'enviroments:'), the environment mapping is invisible. 'dotfiles_for_environment' then finds no override for a target, and the SHARED entry deploys onto the target the override was written for.

Reproduced with the built binary:

  name: myapp
  extra:
    ? [a, b]          <- makes the re-read fail
    : v
  dotfiles:
    - source: myapp/shared.conf
      target: T
  _environments:      <- hides the real mapping
    work:
      dotfiles:
        - source: myapp/work.conf
          target: T
  environments:
    work: { install: "true" }

  -> warns, '1 deployed, 0 refused', and T contains SHARED, not WORK.

This is the harm 'shadows_package_field' documents for the environment-level case, arriving by a route the top-level check cannot see because the check itself could not run.

Not a regression: on main the same file deployed the same bytes with no warning at all. The current behavior is strictly better and should not be reverted on this account.

The question is whether an extra condition is warranted -- for instance refusing an Unchecked package that has no 'environments' key at all, since a package with zero environments and shared dotfiles is the exact signature of a hidden mapping. Weigh against the false-positive cost that made warn-and-deploy right in the first place.

Found by independent final review of the selfie-5j5j / selfie-vhw4 / selfie-jt6m unit, which blocked that PR until its comment and commit message stopped claiming content safety they cannot deliver.

title: selfie apply is silent about a plainly misspelled top-level key
description:
A top-level key that is simply misspelled -- no underscore, no exotic YAML -- makes 'selfie apply' deploy nothing and exit 0 with no message.

Measured on main:

  configs:            <- instead of dotfiles:
    - source: ...
      target: ...

  $ selfie apply -y
  Dotfiles applied: 0 deployed, 0 skipped, 0 conflict(s), 0 refused
  exit 0

  $ selfie spec validate myapp
  ERROR InvalidValue configs  unknown field 'configs'; expected one of: name, homepage, ...

That is the same validate-speaks-apply-stays-quiet divergence as selfie-5j5j, for what is probably the commoner user error. Package carries no deny_unknown_fields on purpose (YAML anchors), so the key parses and 'dotfiles' defaults to empty.

The work on selfie-5j5j / selfie-vhw4 gives 'Package' a TopLevelKeys value at load time, but it carries only the SHADOWING subset (keys whose '_' prefix hides a real field). So after that lands, apply refuses '_dotfiles:' and refuses a file it could not re-read that deploys nothing, and stays silent on 'configs:'.

The coherent rule is probably: apply refuses what 'spec validate' calls an error at the top level -- i.e. every key 'unknown_key::<PackageField>' returns Some for, not just those where 'shadows' is true. The wording already exists in 'describe_unknown_key_in'.

Cost to weigh: a user whose file has a typo today gets a silent no-op; afterwards they get a refusal and exit 1. That is a machine that was already broken, but it is a user-visible change.

Found by review during the selfie-5j5j / selfie-vhw4 unit.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #134

title: save_package can drop an unknown environment key on rewrite
description:
`save_package` (package/repository/yaml.rs) guards against laundering unknown *dotfile-entry* keys by calling `validate_unknown_dotfile_fields()`, but nothing covers keys inside `environments.<env>`.

A package carrying `environments.work.audt: "brew audit myapp"` is serialized from the struct by `selfie spec edit`, `selfie package track-dotfile` and the `selfie_spec_update` MCP tool. `audt` is not modeled, so the user's command text is deleted with no diagnostic.

Same class as the `var:`/`_vars:` guard three lines above, one level down. PR #121 made the key detectable; this is the write-side half.

Found by review of PR #121.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #124

title: selfie apply does not refuse an environment-level _dotfiles key
description:
`spec validate` reports an unknown or shadowing key inside `environments.<env>`, but `selfie apply` does not refuse it, so the run deploys the wrong content and exits zero.

Given `environments.work._dotfiles:`, `EnvironmentConfig::dotfiles` reads empty. `Package::dotfiles_for_environment` (package.rs:879) then finds no environment entry to override the shared one and returns the shared entry, so the work machine gets the shared file instead of its own.

`handle_apply` consults only `shadowing_top_level_keys` (dotfile_service/service.rs:1275), which is top-level by construction. The top-level analogue refuses the whole package and the entry-level one refuses per entry; this level has neither.

Confirmed against origin/main: one `shadowing_top_level_keys` call site in the service, and the fallback in `dotfiles_for_environment` is unconditional on an empty environment list.

Found by review of PR #121, which added the validate-time half.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #124

title: Config docs contradict flags-only operation, and config validate reports flag values
description:
Three statements in docs/configuration.md describe behavior main no longer has, and one command contradicts its own documentation.

1. Line 56 says a run without a config file 'fails with No configuration file found in locations: …, and command-line flags do not substitute for the file'. Line 311 of the same file says 'A configuration file is optional, but two settings are not.' PR #112 (selfie-zse) changed the behavior and updated the second passage only.

2. Line 358 says a missing dotfiles directory 'is dropped without a message'. crates/cli/src/commands/common.rs warns whenever the directory was named by flag or file, which PR #110 added.

3. Line 363 says 'selfie config validate reads what is on disk and applies no overrides, so that a flag cannot hide a problem in the file'. crates/cli/src/commands/config.rs reports environment, package_directory, command_timeout, max_concurrency and stop_on_error from the reloaded file, but verbose and use_colors from the flag-merged config. 'selfie --no-color config validate' prints 'use_colors: false' against a file saying true.

The comment above those two lines still reads 'verbose and use_colors are CLI-only settings, not in the on-disk config', which stopped being true when the cli: section landed in PR #111.

Found by a code review that ran against a stale branch; each was then confirmed against origin/main.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #122

title: A fifo at the config file path hangs every selfie command
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr plan reviewer; verified by the team lead.

crates/selfie/src/config/yaml.rs:74 reads the config file with no irregular-file guard:

    let file_contents = self.fs.read_file(config_path)?;

crates/cli/src/config.rs:182 does the same for the cli: section:

    let Ok(contents) = fs.read_file(&config_path) else { return CliSection::default(); };

Reading a fifo blocks until a writer arrives, so the else arm never runs.

BLAST RADIUS IS WORSE THAN selfie-h2kr, which is P2. crates/cli/src/main.rs:99 applies ? to load_config(), so EVERY command loads the config file before doing anything else. A fifo at ~/.config/selfie/config.yaml therefore wedges the entire CLI, not just the spec-enumerating commands. It also hangs before any guard selfie-h2kr adds can run.

SAME CLASS as the closed selfie-lwv5 and selfie-qwj3, and as selfie-h2kr. The guard already exists and is reusable: irregular_kind (crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:43) classifies without opening (stat never blocks, only open does), irregular_refusal (real.rs:103) wraps it, and FileSystem::irregular_target_refusal (fs/filesystem.rs:175) exposes it on the port. Do NOT write a second guard.

Note the config path is one selfie composes from SELFIE_CONFIG_DIR or the XDG strategy, so repository_path (crates/selfie/src/fs/target.rs:166) is the right way to mint the TargetPath.

Wording needs its own frame: 'the configuration file is a {kind}, not a regular file'. Unlike a spec file, there is nothing to continue with — this refusal is fatal, and it must not be swallowed into CliSection::default() the way a read error currently is.

ASSIGNED TO the config unit of the specs-and-config batch rather than the spec-load unit, because it touches config/yaml.rs and cli/config.rs, which that unit already owns.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #111

title: create_dotfile_service silently drops the dotfiles repository when the directory is missing
notes:
CORRECTION (U3 plan author, verified by team lead 2026-08-12): this bead named the wrong mechanism for one of its symptoms.

There are THREE copies of the dotfiles-directory existence check, not one:
- crates/cli/src/commands/common.rs:80  — if dotfiles_dir.is_dir() { ...attach repo... }  SILENT
- crates/cli/src/commands/dotfiles/list.rs:100 — if dotfiles_dir.is_dir() { ... }          SILENT
- crates/cli/src/commands/common.rs:163 — if !dotfiles_dir.is_dir() { error + suggestion + return 1 }  CORRECT

'dotfiles list' does NOT go through create_dotfile_service at all — it calls create_package_repository directly (list.rs:91). So the claim in this bead that standalone dotfiles vanish from 'list' is true, but by way of list.rs:100, not common.rs:80.

Fixing only common.rs:80 would leave the bead half-closed while appearing done. Both silent sites must be covered, and the messages must come from one shared helper so the warning and the existing refusal cannot drift apart.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #111

title: Drop test-common's [lib] doctest = false so its examples are checked
description:
`crates/test-common/Cargo.toml` sets `[lib] doctest = false`, so no gate ever compiles examples in that crate's public API docs. Neither `just check` nor CI catches it: both run bare `cargo test`, which honors the setting.

That let 12 examples rot unnoticed across events.rs and fixtures.rs. Forcing them showed all 12 failing:

    cargo test -p test-common --doc
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 12 failed

They were fenced ```rust, promising runnable code, but written as illustrative snippets referencing variables that were never declared -- `service`, `stream`, `events`, `temp_dir` -- with no imports.

PR #104 deleted all 12 rather than fixing them, because each also restated its own signature: `let events = collect_events(stream).await;` below `pub async fn collect_events(mut stream: EventStream) -> Vec<PackageEvent>` shows a reader nothing. `cargo test -p test-common --doc` now reports 0 tests.

REMAINING WORK: drop `doctest = false`. It costs nothing now -- there are no examples left to fix first -- and without it, the next example someone adds to test-common is unchecked again. test-common is the crate whose whole audience is people writing tests, so its examples are the ones most likely to be copied.

Consider also whether any example is worth adding back. The helpers are mostly self-explanatory since the '# Arguments' boilerplate was removed, so this may be no work at all beyond the one-line Cargo.toml change plus confirming the suite still passes.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #107.

`[lib] doctest = false` removed from crates/test-common/Cargo.toml. PR #104 had already deleted the 12 rotted examples, so dropping the flag cost nothing: the crate has no code fences left and `cargo test -p test-common --doc` reports 0 tests and passes.

Mutation-tested rather than assumed, since a suite reporting zero doctests is indistinguishable from one that is not running: planting a broken example in events.rs turned the run red (0 passed, 1 failed) where the flag had hidden it entirely. Reverted after.

Any example added to test-common from now on is compiled by `cargo test`, and its links are checked by the new `docs` CI job from selfie-udyh.

comments.author: Steve Loveless
comments.text:
PR #104 deletes all 12 examples rather than fixing them (option 3). `cargo test -p test-common --doc` now reports 0 tests instead of 12 failures.

They were broken twice over: fenced ```rust while referencing undeclared variables, and redundant -- `let events = collect_events(stream).await;` sat below `pub async fn collect_events(mut stream: EventStream) -> Vec<PackageEvent>`.

What remains of this bead is narrower: `[lib] doctest = false` is still set, so any example added to test-common later is still unchecked. Dropping the setting now costs nothing, since there are no examples left to fix first.

title: Gate rustdoc with -D warnings in CI; fix 11 pre-existing doc-link errors
description:
`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p selfie -p selfie-cli` fails with 11 errors on main (verified identical at c640646 and on the doc-paring branch, so none were introduced by that work).

Nine are `rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links` — a public doc comment linking to a private item, which renders as plain text for every reader of the published docs:

  bound -> BOUNDED_END_BYTES
  GitMessage -> redact_credentials
  dotfile_service -> resolve, template
  event -> EventSender
  template_dotfiles -> Self::validate_dotfile_entry
  unknown_keys -> shadows_dotfile_field
  shadowing_top_level_keys -> shadows_package_field
  <unknown> -> classify

Two are `rustdoc::redundant_explicit_links`.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs fmt, clippy -D warnings, typos, build, test and cargo hack, but never builds the docs — so nothing catches a broken doc link. Add a rustdoc step with -D warnings and fix the existing errors.

Each private link needs a per-site decision: make the item pub, drop the link and name the thing in prose, or move the sentence to a body comment where the link is not needed at all.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #107.

CI now has a `docs` job running `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features`, the same command a developer can run locally, and CLAUDE.md points at it.

All 12 doc-link errors fixed by dropping the link and keeping the name in backticks rather than widening visibility -- making an internal pub to satisfy a doc link would add API surface for no caller. The three WINDOW references in assert_secret_free's doc state the number outright instead, since that paragraph exists to tell someone how to build a leak-test secret; WINDOW gained the change-both-together note.

--all-features is load-bearing: without it rustdoc never reaches the with_mocks items, so MockFileSystem's helpers and their links go unchecked.

Known and documented in the job: cargo reports an output filename collision on selfie/index.html because selfie is documented both as a workspace member and as test-common's dependency. It is a cargo warning, not a rustdoc one, so -D warnings does not promote it. Verified present in the CI log and harmless.

title: the sudo gate does not catch 'sudo -u <other-user> selfie apply'
description:
selfie-tcu2's classify maps (is_root=false, _) to Unprivileged, so a non-root sudo target is allowed. A test asserts this, so it is a scope decision rather than an oversight -- but it leaves the same class of damage open.

'sudo -u alice selfie apply' with HOME preserved: euid is alice's, SUDO_UID is set, the run proceeds, and it writes alice-owned files throughout YOUR home directory. Deploy state lands alice:alice 0600, which your next ordinary run cannot read. Under env_reset it writes into /home/alice and reports success -- the wrong-target failure mode again.

Candidate rule: refuse when SUDO_UID is set AND SUDO_UID != euid. That catches both root-via-sudo and user-via-sudo, while still permitting the case the current comment defends -- a process that merely inherited SUDO_UID and is running as the same user.

Not privilege-tool detection, which selfie-tcu2 rules out. It is the same SUDO_UID signal read more precisely. Needs a decision from the user, since selfie-tcu2's rule was decided deliberately.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Steve Loveless
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-09 on fix/refuse-sudo-selfie-tcu2 (PR #102).

THE RULE NOW: refuse when SUDO_UID is set AND differs from the effective uid. That catches `sudo
selfie` (euid 0, SUDO_UID 501) and `sudo -u alice selfie` (euid 1001, SUDO_UID 501) alike, while
still permitting what presence-alone was defending -- a process that merely inherited the variable
and is running as the user who set it. An unparseable value is refused: it cannot be compared, and a
real sudo always writes a decimal uid, so anything else was not written by the thing being detected.
A non-UTF-8 value reaches classify as None and is allowed, which is the one permissive lean and is
documented on the impl.

`Elevation::Root` still means euid 0 reached without sudo, and is still allowed -- containers, CI,
root managing root's own dotfiles.

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: widening the rule made the refusal wording wrong again. It said "written
as root", which is false for `sudo -u alice`. That is the THIRD wording defect on SudoRefusal:
1. "selfie does not deploy to system paths yet" -- false, caught by code review.
2. the dotfile message reused on the sync path -- caught by reading container output.
3. "as root" after this change -- caught by reading container output.
None was caught by a test, because every test asserted the refusal HAPPENED, which it always did.
each_scope_describes_its_own_damage now asserts no wording names root, over BOTH message() and
suggestion(); checking only message() is what let #3 through, since the suggestion was the surviving
half.

MUTATIONS: m8 (revert to presence-only) -> CAUGHT. m9 (refuse any parseable SUDO_UID, dropping the
comparison) -> CAUGHT by an_inherited_sudo_uid_matching_the_current_user_is_not_elevation. An earlier
m8 attempt reported ANCHOR-MISSING because rustfmt had reformatted the expression -- the harness's
anchor assertion working as intended.

CONTAINER: `sudo -u alice` refused, nothing deployed. Inherited SUDO_UID matching euid proceeds and
deploys.

title: sudo track commands do their CLI work before the refusal can fire
description:
Two CLI paths evaluate the sudo refusal too late, because it lives in DotfileServiceImpl and the handlers do work before constructing one.

1. handle_track_standalone (cli/src/commands/common.rs) checks that dotfiles_directory exists before building the service. Under 'sudo selfie dotfiles track' on a machine whose sudoers policy resets HOME, dotfiles_directory resolves under /root, is_dir() is false, and the user gets 'Dotfiles directory does not exist: /root/...' with 'mkdir -p /root/...' as the suggestion -- advice that would create the root-owned directory the refusal exists to prevent. This is exactly the env_reset case privilege.rs's module doc names as the reason to refuse rather than warn.

2. 'selfie track' (cli/src/commands/track.rs) runs the whole interactive prompt -- fuzzy package selector, namespace validation -- and only then refuses with exit 1, discarding all of it.

The policy must stay library-owned; only the timing moves. Calling privilege::refuse_sudo in the handler ahead of the precheck keeps the rule in one place. Weigh that against adding a second call site that can drift from the port's.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Steve Loveless
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-09 on fix/refuse-sudo-selfie-tcu2 (PR #102).

Both track paths now call commands::common::refuse_under_sudo before doing anything of their own.

That helper is an EARLY EXIT, not the gate. The library still refuses whatever the CLI does; both
read the same root_policy(config), so they cannot disagree about whether to refuse -- only about how
far the run gets first. Stated that way in its doc comment so a later reader does not take the CLI
check for the authority.

COVERAGE LIMIT, recorded rather than papered over: there is no unit test for the ORDERING. Both the
helper and root_policy are hardcoded to RealPrivilege, so a CLI test cannot simulate sudo without
injecting a privilege port through create_dotfile_service and its callers -- a testability refactor
well beyond these two beads. The ordering is verified by the container run instead: `dotfiles track`
under sudo with a missing dotfiles directory emits the refusal and NOT the `mkdir -p /root/...`
suggestion. Anyone changing these handlers should re-run that check; the suite will not catch a
regression here.

title: Pare doc comments back to what a caller needs, repo-wide
description:
Raised by the user 2026-08-03: "it's tiring reading all of the what ifs and alternatives and such in a method doc ... Working in this repo is becoming a downer due to all the longwinded docs."

WHAT A DOC COMMENT SHOULD CONTAIN, per the user, and nothing else:

  - what the method does
  - why you should or should not use it
  - side effects, if any
  - return explanation -- often the type already says it
  - param explanation -- same
  - # Errors
  - # Panics

WHAT DOES NOT BELONG THERE: rationale for the design, alternatives that were rejected, what-if scenarios, the history of how it came to be this way, or descriptions of callers. That material is for whoever maintains the function, so it belongs in ORDINARY // COMMENTS IN THE BODY, beside the code it constrains -- where someone about to change that code will actually see it.

The split that makes this easy: a doc comment answers the CALLER, a body comment answers the NEXT MAINTAINER. "Do not call this before X" is a caller's business. "We did not use fsync here because it would widen the window" is a maintainer's.

SCALE: 5,798 doc-comment lines across crates/*/src as of cc5606c. Worst blocks, none of which the current PR stack touches:

  77 + 44 + 39 + 32   crates/selfie/src/git/message.rs   (four blocks, 192 lines total)
  54                  crates/test-common/src/secrets.rs
  48                  crates/cli/src/commands/completion.rs
  45                  crates/selfie/src/commands/runner.rs
  32 + 27             crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs
  28                  crates/cli/src/main.rs
  24                  crates/cli/src/commands/apply.rs

ALREADY DONE, for reference on the target shape: dotfile_service/service.rs went from 267 doc-comment lines to 214 in cc5606c -- save_deploy_state 29 to 10, unmanaged_symlink_reason 20 to 5, load_deploy_state 18 to 9. fs/filesystem.rs had its trait docs split from RealFileSystem's mechanism at the same time.

DO NOT DELETE THE REASONING, RELOCATE IT. Several of these blocks record a trap someone will otherwise re-introduce -- the fsync direction, the 0o300 directory case, why two guards use different stats. Those must survive as body comments. A pass that only shortens will lose them.

Deliberately not folded into the current stack: these files are untouched by it, and a doc sweep across the whole crate would bury the fixes those PRs exist for.
acceptance_criteria: No doc comment carries rationale, rejected alternatives or what-ifs; that reasoning sits in body comments where it constrains the code. Worst offenders (git/message.rs, commands/runner.rs, commands/shell.rs, completion.rs) are done.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #104 (4ac0378).

Repo-wide doc-comment lines 6,076 -> 4,514. The four named worst offenders are done:

  git/message.rs             233 ->  82
  commands/runner.rs         365 -> 256
  commands/shell.rs          343 -> 111
  cli/commands/completion.rs  74 ->   8

Every doc block over 16 lines in the repo was reviewed. What survives is contract rather than commentary -- the FileSystem writers' guarantee strength, redact_credentials' coverage list, TargetPath's three doctests, privilege.rs on why sudo is refused rather than warned about. Rationale that was worth keeping moved to body comments beside the code it constrains; nine traps in message.rs alone were relocated and each verified still present.

.claude/rules/comments.md now states the rule, so this does not have to be re-derived: the caller/maintainer split, the trait-versus-impl division, prose to cut on sight, and which comment marker belongs where -- including two facts verified against rustc, that a private item's doctest runs and a doctest inside cfg(test) never does.

Found and fixed along the way: five CLI commands documented that do not exist, nine sentences left dangling by an earlier reference-stripping pass, a redaction doc claiming test coverage for a gap that has none, and a --help promise apply does not keep.

Filed rather than fixed: selfie-udyh (rustdoc -D warnings fails; CI never builds docs) and selfie-izce (test-common's doctest = false). Both have follow-up in PR #105.

title: A fifo in the package directory hangs every command that enumerates specs
description:
REPRODUCED by the PR #94 code reviewer against that branch, not inferred.

  mkfifo <package_dir>/ghost.yml
  selfie -e test -p <package_dir> spec list

prints "Loading specs..." and wedges. Killed at a 20s alarm, rc=142.

YamlPackageRepository::load_package_from_file and get_file_size (crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs, around :103 and :112) call read_file on every matching .yml with no irregular-file guard. Reading a fifo blocks until a writer arrives, and command_timeout governs provider commands rather than filesystem calls.

BLAST RADIUS is wider than the other beads in this family, which is why this is P2 where they are P3: anything that enumerates specs hangs. spec list, spec info, package list, package status, spec validate --all. A single stray fifo in the package directory takes out most of the CLI.

SAME CLASS as selfie-lwv5 (the dotfiles repository), different reader. Unit 4 (PR #94) guards the dotfile source reads and, per the review, the template read behind read_referenced_file. This is the package-YAML read path, which that unit does not touch.

The primitive already exists after #94: a free irregular_refusal(&Path) in fs/real.rs using a FOLLOWING fs::metadata, plus FileSystemError::IrregularTarget, plus pub(crate) repository_path(&Path) to call the trait method with. Reuse them; do not write another classifier.

Wording needs a third frame. This is neither a deploy target nor a dotfile source -- it is a package spec. repository_read_refusal is worded for a repository file the user syncs; a spec file wants its own sentence naming the package directory.

Guard both call sites, and note get_file_size is a stat-then-read pair -- check whether the guard belongs once, ahead of both.
acceptance_criteria: A fifo, socket or device node among the package YAML files is refused with a diagnostic rather than hanging spec list, spec info, package list/status and validate --all.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #110

title: sudo selfie apply writes every dotfile as root, including the ones under $HOME
description:
There is no privilege handling anywhere in production code: grep for sudo/setuid/geteuid/privilege across crates/selfie/src and crates/cli/src returns nothing. selfie writes as whatever user invoked it.

That is fine until a user targets a system path. An absolute target is legal (in fact expand_target_path plus the is_absolute guards at dotfile_service/service.rs:587,1126,1419 REQUIRE the expanded target to be absolute -- '~/' is only a portable way of writing one), and docs/package-files.md offers /etc/nginx.conf as an example. Deploying it fails with EACCES for a normal user.

The failure itself is clean. The WORKAROUND is the hazard: the obvious next move is 'sudo selfie apply', and apply has no per-entry privilege scope. Every dotfile in that run is then written as root -- including every ~/ entry, which lands root-owned inside the user's own home directory. The user gets a home directory they cannot rewrite without sudo, from a command whose only intended effect was one file in /etc.

Compounding it: write_file_no_follow sets no explicit mode (only O_NOFOLLOW custom_flags), so files land at 0666 & ~umask, typically 0644. Under sudo that is root:root 0644 on files that should be user-owned.

Pre-existing; not introduced by PR #89, which changes only what track records and leaves the is_absolute guards byte-identical.

Options, roughly in order of cost:
1. Refuse to run at all when euid is 0 unless an explicit opt-in flag is passed. Cheapest, and probably correct for a personal dotfile manager.
2. Warn when euid is 0 and any entry targets a path under $HOME -- the mixed case is the actually-dangerous one.
3. Per-entry privilege escalation (a requires_sudo on the dotfile entry, cf. selfie-cdj for install commands) so only the system entry escalates. Most correct, most work, and needs a decision about how selfie obtains the privilege.

Related: selfie-5nk (deployed file mode is not specifiable, so even a correct escalation cannot set root:root 0600), selfie-cdj (requires_sudo per environment, for install commands rather than dotfiles).
design:
DECIDED 2026-08-04 with the user. Implement option 1, refined: the gate is not "am I root" but "am I root VIA SUDO".

THE RULE

  euid == 0 AND SUDO_UID is set  -> refuse, exit non-zero
  euid == 0 AND no SUDO_UID      -> allow (real root: containers, CI, root managing root's own dotfiles)
  euid != 0                      -> allow

  Escape hatch: --allow-root for the deliberate case.

Refusing at ANY euid 0 was considered and rejected: it blocks legitimate root-owned machine, container and CI use behind a flag, to prevent an accident that is not happening there. SUDO_UID is what distinguishes "someone reached for sudo to get past an EACCES" from "this process is root because that is the design".

Known and accepted hole: doas, su and pkexec do not set SUDO_UID, so they are not caught. That is fine -- sudo is what the EACCES workaround reaches for, and an allowlist that covered every escalation tool would still miss one. Do not expand this into privilege-tool detection.

WHY NOT THE ALTERNATIVES

  Warn-only (bead option 2) cannot work. See the ~ finding below: on a machine where sudo resets HOME the paths LOOK correct and are simply the wrong home, so there is nothing for a warning to key on. It also leaves every root-owned artifact in place.

  Per-entry requires_sudo (bead option 3) stays the right end state for the /etc use case, but it is blocked on selfie-5nk: escalating without being able to say root:root 0600 relocates the problem rather than solving it. It also needs a design for how selfie OBTAINS privilege (re-exec? sudo per write? helper binary?), which is real security surface and its own unit.

TWO FINDINGS FROM THE 2026-08-04 PASS, NEITHER IN THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION

1. ~ DOES NOT RESOLVE TO A FIXED PLACE UNDER SUDO. Verified through the chain: fs/real.rs expand_path -> shellexpand::tilde -> dirs::home_dir -> dirs-sys-0.5.0/src/lib.rs:34, which reads $HOME FIRST and only falls back to getpwuid. Sudo's HOME handling is a sudoers policy that differs by platform (preserved on some, reset to /root by env_reset on Debian-family, flipped again by sudo -E).

   So there are TWO failure modes, not one:
     HOME preserved -> dotfiles land in the user's home, root-owned  (the case this bead describes)
     HOME -> /root  -> dotfiles land in /root instead, and apply REPORTS SUCCESS

   The second is a wrong-target bug, not a permissions bug. It is the strongest single argument for refusing rather than warning.

2. THE DAMAGE OUTLIVES THE BAD RUN. save_deploy_state uses write_file_private (service.rs:322, mode 0600), as do both secret-bearing target writes (:825, :944). Under sudo all three land root:root 0600.

   Consequence chain, and it now interacts with shipped work: the next non-sudo apply cannot read the state file, so post-selfie-y8ub it warns and proceeds with an EMPTY state -- meaning a full round of conflict prompts on every subsequent run. Worse, if state_directory did not exist beforehand, the sudo run creates it root-owned and the user cannot write into it at all. That one does not self-heal; the file case does, since the rename comes from a user-owned temp file in a user-owned directory.

   This is the argument for treating it as a footgun to close rather than a mess to warn about.

SCOPE: WHICH COMMANDS

  Gate apply and BOTH track handlers. Verified by grepping save_deploy_state in dotfile_service/service.rs -- the three call sites are handle_apply (:1665), handle_track_standalone (:2030) and handle_track_for_package (:2204). Those are exactly the commands that write dotfiles, the state file, or into the dotfiles repository.

  Do NOT gate the read-only commands (drift, list, status, spec *). They write nothing and gating them is friction for no gain.

  Do NOT gate package install. It runs user-authored commands that may legitimately need sudo -- that is selfie-cdj's territory, and refusing there would break a real use.

WHERE THE CHECK LIVES

  Follow the HomeDir precedent at fs/target.rs:18 -- a trait with one method, injected, so the policy is library-owned and mockable. Do not sniff the environment inline in the CLI: the MCP server is a second driving adapter and needs the same refusal, and a test must be able to simulate "running under sudo" without actually being root.

  The refusal is a normal typed error surfaced as an event, per the boundary rule that selfie never writes to stdout.

HOW TO READ THE EUID (corrected 2026-08-09). The earlier "NO NEW DEPENDENCIES" note here was wrong twice over and has been struck. Factually: nix is a DEV dependency (crates/selfie/Cargo.toml, [target.'cfg(unix)'.dev-dependencies]), which is exactly why the three is_root() calls in fs/real.rs (:618, :938, :1243) sit inside #[cfg(test)]. Production code cannot reach nix today. As policy: minimizing the dependency count is not a project goal and contradicts CLAUDE.md ("Lean towards using third party libraries ... so we can keep the codebase small"). DECIDED: promote nix = { version = "0.31", features = ["user"] } into [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies], keeping the dev entry for its "fs" feature. The argument is that it is the maintained wrapper and avoids the crate's first unsafe block (libc::geteuid is unsafe, and Cargo.toml's own comment records declining that cost once already) -- NOT that it happens to add no crate to Cargo.lock.

MCP SERVER: no flag mechanism and no reason for an AI assistant to be driving selfie under sudo. Refuse unconditionally there rather than exposing an allow_root parameter.

DOCS (revised 2026-08-09 -- the tree moved since the original note). docs/package-files.md no longer "offers /etc/nginx.conf as a target example": every YAML example there already uses ~/, and the absolute path survives only as prose explaining when one is appropriate, already carrying "selfie deploys as whoever runs it and never elevates, so a target like that one needs write access you may not have." Remaining work is therefore additive, not a rewrite: say that running under sudo is refused, name --allow-root, and say system paths are not supported yet. Also add --allow-root to the Command-Line Overrides section of docs/configuration.md, with a note that it is flag-only and deliberately has no config-file key -- that section opens "All configuration options can be overridden via command-line flags", so the inverse case needs saying or someone will add the key.

TESTING: mock the privilege port; never shell out and never require the suite to run as root. Cover both euid-0 branches (SUDO_UID set and unset) and the --allow-root override. Per .claude/rules/testing.md, mutate the SUDO_UID condition and confirm a named test fails -- a gate that always allows is exactly the shape of bug a green suite hides.

EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS UNIT: per-entry requires_sudo (this bead's option 3), selfie-5nk (deployed file mode), selfie-cdj (requires_sudo for install commands), and any mechanism for selfie to obtain privilege.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Steve Loveless
comments.text:
MUTATION RESULTS (2026-08-09, per the repo's testing rules). One mutation per invocation, each in a `git archive` copy with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR; `could not compile` / `error[E` checked before the `Compiling|Checking selfie v` line, so a mutation that never built could not be scored as caught.

m1  refuse_sudo returns Ok(()) for Elevation::Sudo
    -> CAUGHT by privilege::tests::a_sudo_run_is_refused
m1b same mutation, integration suite
    -> CAUGHT by running_under_sudo::apply_all_is_refused_and_writes_nothing
m2  classify maps (true, true) to Root, ignoring SUDO_UID
    -> CAUGHT by privilege::tests::sudo_is_root_plus_sudo_uid_and_nothing_less
m3  apply_all runs handle_apply first and overrides the result with the refusal afterwards
    -> CAUGHT, and by the right assertion: "the target was written before the run was refused".
       The event assertion PASSED under this mutation -- the refusal is still reported correctly --
       so the "nothing was written" assertions are the load-bearing ones, not decoration.
m4  check_drift gated, reporting OperationFailure::Generic
    -> SURVIVED. A real gap, not in the code but in the control test: drift_is_not_gated asserted
       only "the failure is not the Privilege variant", which a Generic-reporting gate satisfies
       while stopping drift dead. Exactly the shape the testing rules warn about -- a test written
       from the same mental model as the code.
    -> FIXED: the control now asserts drift SUCCEEDED.
m4b same mutation, after the fix -> CAUGHT
m4c faithful variant (check_drift gated, reporting OperationFailure::Privilege) -> CAUGHT

Not mutated, and worth knowing why: RealPrivilege's two-line body is not covered by any test. It
reads the real euid and the real SUDO_UID, so covering it means either running the suite as root or
mutating the environment (unsafe in edition 2024, and racy). `classify` exists precisely to hold the
rule where a test can reach it; what is untested is the two argument expressions feeding it.

comments.author: Steve Loveless
comments.text:
CONTAINER VERIFICATION (2026-08-09). Closes the gap noted in the mutation comment: RealPrivilege's
two-line body -- the actual geteuid and SUDO_UID reads -- is unreachable from the suite, because
covering it needs a real euid 0. Run in rust:latest as root, workspace mounted, three cases against
a real package fixture and a real deploy target.

A  euid 0, SUDO_UID=1000            -> exit 1, nothing deployed, message is the refusal + suggestion
B  euid 0, SUDO_UID unset           -> exit 0, file deployed  (the container/CI case the rule protects)
C  euid 0, SUDO_UID=1000, --allow-root -> exit 0, file deployed

All three as designed.

TWO NOTES ON THE HARNESS, both worth keeping:

1. The first run was a FALSE PASS on case A. selfie requires a config file even when every path is
   passed as a flag, so all three cases died at "No configuration file found" -- and case A's
   assertion was only "exit non-zero AND target absent", which that satisfies. It reported PASS
   having never reached the gate. Fixed by writing a config file, and by additionally requiring the
   output to contain the refusal text. A non-zero exit proves nothing on its own here; nearly every
   failure mode produces one.

2. Case B has to prove SUDO_UID is genuinely absent, not merely unmentioned. The script asserts it
   is unset before running, because SUDO_UID was being set per-command elsewhere in the same shell
   and a leak would have made case B silently test case A's condition.

Script kept at scratchpad/verify-sudo.sh for the session; re-creatable from the plan file.

title: A ~user target passes spec validate and is then silently skipped by apply
description:
Two rules about what a dotfile target may be, and they disagree. The gap hides between them.

  crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:815 -- TEXTUAL: accepts anything starting with '/' or '~'. So '~alice/.gemrc' passes 'selfie spec validate'.
  service.rs:690, :1234, :1530 -- POST-EXPANSION is_absolute(). shellexpand::tilde leaves '~user' UNCHANGED (expand_target_path's own doc comment says so), so '~alice/.gemrc' expands to the literal relative path '~alice/.gemrc', fails is_absolute(), and the entry is SKIPPED.

Net effect: the user writes '~alice/.gemrc', validate says the spec is fine, and apply silently does not deploy it. No error, no warning that names the reason -- the guards emit a skip.

Neither rule is wrong on its own; they are enforcing different things at different times and nobody reconciled them. A textual check cannot know what shellexpand will do, and the runtime check runs too late to be a validation error.

Fix directions: teach the validator that '~user/' is not supported (narrowest, and honest -- selfie does not resolve other users' homes); or make the runtime guard emit a diagnostic naming the '~user' form rather than a generic skip; or support it, which means resolving another user's home and is almost certainly not wanted.

Note the interaction with selfie-zv4b: that unit gives selfie ONE constructor for target paths instead of three scattered guards, which is where a reconciled rule would live. Consider doing this after it lands.

Found by the selfie-h15 plan author while surveying the enforcement sites; it also corrected the count -- selfie-1xg9 says three enforcement sites, there are three runtime guards PLUS the validator.
close_reason: Closed by PR #90 (merge a6c5baa, commit 14daa1a). One target rule, expressed once in crates/selfie/src/fs/target.rs as TargetRejection + deploy_target, enforced at five call sites plus the validator.

title: Investigate whether CLI path flags actually override the config file
description:
OBSERVED, NOT DIAGNOSED -- needs confirming before it is treated as a bug.

While attempting an end-to-end CLI run inside a temporary fixture, an agent reported that the selfie binary picked up the USER'S REAL config and package directory despite being passed -p / --dotfiles-directory / --state-directory, and enumerated the user's actual dotfiles. It reported '0 deployed, 8 skipped', so nothing was written and no harm was done, and the agent aborted rather than retrying.

If that reproduces, it means CLI path flags do not take precedence over the config file, which is both a usability bug and a testing hazard: any attempt to exercise the real binary against a fixture would silently operate on the developer's own configuration instead. The '8 skipped' suggests it read the real dotfiles directory.

TO INVESTIGATE:
- Do -p / --dotfiles-directory / --state-directory actually override ~/.config/selfie/config.yml, or are they merged the other way round?
- Is the precedence documented in docs/configuration.md, and does the documentation match the code?
- Does an env var or a default path win over an explicit flag anywhere?
- Check crates/cli/src/config.rs and wherever CliConfig is assembled from clap matches plus the config file.

If flags do win and the agent's run was misconfigured, close this and record what actually happened -- a false alarm here is worth the same write-up as a real bug, because the next person to try an end-to-end CLI test will hit the same question.

Reported by the selfie-ywvs code reviewer as a process note; explicitly NOT claimed by it as a finding, and not investigated.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #108

title: Fold credential redaction into BoundedText and retire GitMessage's git framing
description:
GitMessage (crates/selfie/src/git/message.rs), added by PR #83 for selfie-cvpm, is:

    BoundedText::bound(redact_credentials(text))

redact_credentials is NOT git-specific. It is RFC 3986 userinfo redaction over whitespace-delimited tokens: any scheme, scp-style user@host:path, IPv6 authorities, query parameters, insteadOf-style config values. Nothing in it knows what git is. The only git-specific things in that file are the type name, the module path, some test names, and a doc line about git's stderr not being UTF-8.

BoundedText truncates and does NOT redact. So the redaction currently sits behind a git-shaped door while FIVE non-git sites forward untrusted text through the bound-only path:

  resolve.rs:292  provider command stderr   <- THE CREDENTIAL PATH
  resolve.rs:283  provider command error
  event.rs:894 and :1739  CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed.stderr -> CLI and MCP JSON
  audit.rs:317   audit command stderr
  audit.rs:340   audit command error

A user's command that fails while contacting https://user:token@api.example.com therefore has that URL bounded and forwarded verbatim to the terminal and to an AI assistant's transcript. That is precisely the class selfie-cvpm closed, left open everywhere except git.

DECIDED (maintainer, 2026-07-31): fold the redaction INTO BoundedText so bound() redacts-then-truncates. All five sites are then fixed by construction with no call-site changes, and there is no second type anyone can reach for by mistake -- the failure mode this codebase keeps hitting. Rename the type accordingly; 'Bounded' undersells it once it sanitizes.

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: redact THEN truncate. Truncating first can cut a URL mid-string, leaving 'https://user:TOK' with no '@' to anchor on, so the bound would manufacture a leak the redactor can no longer see. PR #83 has a test pinning this (the fixture arithmetic is spelled out because it was vacuous on the first attempt); carry that test over.

GitMessage then collapses to a thin alias or disappears. Check what remains genuinely git-specific -- from_stderr's lossy decode is generic, and the git/ module keeps only the error types.

COSTS TO STATE:
- Over-redaction spreads: git@github.com becomes ***@github.com, and identity-error emails go, at five more sites. Deliberate everywhere else already; the reasoning is that deciding a username is safe is an allowlist that fails open.
- Five sites change behavior. Each needs a test that a credential in that path's text is redacted, with a positive control that non-credential text survives byte-identical.
- PR #83's 14 mutations cover the redactor; re-run them after the move rather than assuming they survive it.

Also fold in the rename of the redaction's residual documentation: the covered/uncovered lists in message.rs and docs/sync.md are written as git-specific and would become general.

Raised by the maintainer reviewing PR #83: 'is it really just for dealing with git? ...if it's used to handle strings that could have nothing to do with git, i think it could/should be renamed.' Verified: it is generic, and five non-git sites are currently walking past it.

title: tcsh and csh users cannot run any login-shell command path
description:
ShellCommandRunner::login_shell (crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:83-93) is std::env::var("SHELL").unwrap_or_else(|_| Self::default_shell()) with login: true, and build_command (:104-108) adds -l unconditionally. There is no shell-family handling anywhere.

tcsh and csh REJECT -l alongside another flag. Measured on both:

  tcsh -l -c 'printf %s hello'  ->  Unknown option: `-l'   rc=1
  csh  -l -c 'printf %s hello'  ->  Unknown option: `-l'   rc=1
  tcsh    -c 'printf %s hello'  ->  hello                  rc=0

Their usage lines confirm -l is accepted only as the sole argument.

So for a user whose $SHELL is /bin/tcsh or /bin/csh, EVERY login-runner path fails: install, check, audit and apply, in BOTH the CLI (create_command_runner, cli/src/commands/common.rs:64-65) and the MCP server (server.rs:229, main.rs:65). Not a degraded experience -- rc=1 on every command that runs anything.

Pre-existing and unrelated to selfie-evf9; found while measuring shell behavior for that unit's fence design, and confirmed independently by its plan reviewer.

Fix direction: drop -l for the csh family. Their login profiles (.login, .cshrc) are not usable through -l -c anyway, so the flag buys nothing there -- csh sources .cshrc for non-interactive shells regardless. Detect by the shell's basename rather than by probing, and note that selfie-evf9's stdout fence uses POSIX 'trap ... EXIT' and 'printf', neither of which csh has, so a csh-family path needs its own decision about content commands or an explicit refusal.

Consider whether an unsupported $SHELL should fail with a clear message naming the shell rather than surfacing the shell's own 'Unknown option' text.

title: apply records a deployment for a symlinked target it never wrote to
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1337: when drift == NotTracked and !options.dry_run, apply calls record_deployment(...) -- including for a target it has just REFUSED to write because the target is a symlink.

Measured: symlinked target, no prior state, destination content equal to the repo file. apply emits deployed_count=0, skipped_count=1 and writes nothing to the target, then records a deploy-state entry with source_checksum == deployed_checksum and a deployed_at timestamp. The state now asserts a deployment that did not occur.

SAME CLASS AS selfie-13bq -- 'the state file carries data implying a guarantee it does not provide' -- and the same lie that selfie-ywvs (P1) produces via track. Unit A of the target-semantics batch refuses track for exactly this reason, but leaves apply doing it by a different door.

CONSEQUENCE: it is the second manufacturer of the state that makes selfie-qvwq's diagnosis meaningless. Once that entry exists, drift compares live checksums against a recorded deployment that never happened, so the next edit to the repo file produces 'repo changed' forever with the target never updated.

There is an existing 25-line comment at service.rs:1286-1291 acknowledging this record and arguing it costs nothing. That argument predates the exfiltration chain in selfie-ywvs being understood and is worth re-examining: a state entry claiming a symlinked target was deployed is not free, it is what makes every later drift report wrong.

Fix direction: do not record a deployment for an entry that was refused. Check the interaction with selfie-13bq (which may remove the field the record relies on) and with the deliberate Skip-branch exclusion at service.rs:1305 before changing the condition.

Found by the unit-A plan reviewer while checking the plan's drift/apply parity claim.
notes:
