The MCP half of provider-sourced dotfiles inherited it (crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:228, with a comment noting that op and teller live on the user's PATH). The CLI half did not: crates/cli/src/commands/apply.rs:221 uses ShellCommandRunner::default_shell().

default_shell() is /bin/sh on Unix, while install and check run under the user's shell with -l. Two consequences. Provider commands do not get the login profile, so anything the profile sets rather than exports — SSH_AUTH_SOCK, OP_ variables, PATH entries — is missing. And a command written in fish or zsh syntax works in 'selfie package install' and fails in 'selfie apply', while the same package behaves differently through the CLI and the MCP server.

docs/package-files.md says only that provider commands 'run through a shell', which does not distinguish them.
acceptance_criteria: A provider command sees the same shell and environment through CLI apply as it does through install and through the MCP server, or the difference is documented.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ctrl+C cannot cancel a provider command during selfie apply
description:
Commit 568c528 threaded a CancellationToken from the CLI signal handler through the service and runner layers so Ctrl+C kills in-flight subprocesses, adding a token parameter to every CommandRunner method.

The dotfile apply path does not participate. SecretApply::resolve (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:705) passes &CancellationToken::new() — a fresh token nothing holds. DotfileServiceImpl::new takes no token, unlike PackageServiceImpl::new. And crates/cli/src/commands.rs never passes the token to handle_apply, though the Spec and Package arms beside it do.

Harmless before this feature, because apply executed nothing. Now Ctrl+C during 'selfie apply' cannot kill an 'op read' blocked on a biometric or password prompt; command_timeout still bounds it, so it is not unbounded, but the interactive escape hatch 568c528 exists to provide is absent and no cancellation event is emitted.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+C during selfie apply cancels an in-flight provider command, as it does during install and check.
close_reason: Closed

title: Deploy state file is written world-readable
description:
save_deploy_state (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:232) writes ~/.local/state/selfie/deploy-state.yml with FileSystem::write_file, so it lands at the process umask default, typically 0644. Secret-bearing dotfile targets are written owner-only at 0600, which makes the state file the weaker of the two.

Its contents are not credentials, but they are a complete map of every target path selfie manages on the machine, plus checksums of repository files. That is a reconnaissance aid on a shared host, and it is readable by anyone when the things it describes are not.

FileSystem::write_file_private already exists and does exactly what is needed — owner-only at creation, atomic replace. The change is the call site plus a test asserting the mode.

This also underpins ADR-0003's refusal to store checksums of secrets. That argument turns on the state file being easier to read than the secret itself; make the file owner-only and the asymmetry disappears, which is a precondition for selfie-0ei5 to even be worth considering.
acceptance_criteria: The deploy state file is readable only by its owner, with a test asserting it.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #72 (merged 78ae893). save_deploy_state now uses write_file_private, so ~/.local/state/selfie/deploy-state.yml is created owner-only (0600) and a pre-existing 0644 file is tightened on the next write.

Tests assert mode & 0o077 == 0, not & 0o007 — verified by mutation: writing the file 0640 fails both tests, while a world-bits-only check would have passed. The umask-vacuity guard panics when CI is set and skips only locally, so it cannot silently prove nothing on a runner (CI is ubuntu-latest, default umask 022, so it does not fire there).

title: Apply never runs validation, so every consumer must refuse invalid entries by hand
description:
handle_apply iterates ListPackagesOutput::valid_packages(), which is filter_map over PARSE results (crates/selfie/src/package/port.rs). Package::validate() is never called on the apply path — selfie validate is a separate, advisory command. So a package that parses but fails validation is applied.

The consequence is ContentSource::Invalid, a variant that exists only because an invalid entry can reach code that must act on it. Its own doc comment states the rule: apply does not run validation, so every consumer has to refuse it explicitly rather than guess. That is a comment, not a mechanism, and it was not honored for templates — a templated source could escape the package directory because the containment guard the repository-file path already had was not applied to the new call site. Two reviewers found it independently, one of them by noticing the same guard had been established in this repository twice before.

The specific gap is fixed: the guard and its normalization moved to crate::paths, where all three call sites reach it, with a regression test on the repository-file path so relocating it cannot quietly drop it. What is not fixed is the shape. The next consumer of content_source() can forget in exactly the same way, and nothing will fail to compile or fail a test.

Two directions, and the choice is the substance of this issue:

Gate apply on validation, refusing packages with validation errors. Simple and closes it outright, but it is a behavior change: packages that apply today would stop, including ones whose only defect is unrelated to the entry being deployed. Needs a decision about partial application and about which validation levels block.

Or make the invalid state unrepresentable where it is consumed — have apply take a type that can only be constructed from a validated package, so a consumer cannot reach an entry without having refused the invalid case. That converts a rule everyone must remember into a compile error, which is the form that actually holds. Larger change, and it is the direction this codebase has repeatedly found to be the one that sticks.
acceptance_criteria: An invalid dotfile entry cannot reach a consumer that has not explicitly handled it, enforced by the compiler or by apply refusing to run on an invalid package — not by a doc comment.
notes: Raised from the provider-sourced dotfiles PR (#67), whose description calls this out as the most uncomfortable detail of that work: the reasoning was written down correctly in a doc comment and the code still did not do it.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #75 (merged 97ff4ad).

Both options the bead named were measured and rejected — a whole-package validation gate fails 7 tests including one asserting a bad entry is skipped WHILE the package's other dotfiles still deploy, and a ValidatedPackage type would be constructed at one internal site (apply_all takes no packages) so it is that gate wearing a type.

title: Allow a dotfile entry to specify the deployed file mode
description:
A dotfile entry cannot say what permissions its target should have. Repository-file entries land at the process umask default, typically 0644, and only secret-bearing entries get 0600, automatically and inexpressibly.

Two failures this causes today: a deployed ~/.ssh/config at 0644 makes ssh warn or refuse, and a deployed script is not executable, so ~/.local/bin entries do not work. Both are ordinary daily-driver cases rather than edge cases.

Proposed shape: an optional per-entry mode, written as an octal string (mode: "0755") so YAML does not coerce it to a decimal integer. Absent, behavior is unchanged: umask default for repository files, 0600 for secret-bearing entries.

The constraint that matters: an explicit mode on a secret-bearing entry must not be permitted to loosen it below owner-only. ADR-0003 requires credentials be readable only by their owner, and a mode field that can express 0644 on a provider-sourced entry turns the spec into a way to defeat that. A group- or world-readable mode on a secret-bearing entry should be a validation error, not a warning — the same reasoning that made auto_accept not apply to those entries.

Also decide: whether mode applies on every apply or only at creation (it should apply on every apply, consistent with the in-sync permission tightening already implemented); and Unix-only semantics with a documented no-op elsewhere, matching write_file_private's existing platform note.
acceptance_criteria: A dotfile entry can set its target's mode; a mode that would make a secret-bearing target readable beyond its owner is rejected at validation.

title: CLI prints command stdout verbatim in the multi-error summary
description:
crates/cli/src/display_manager.rs:91-99 prints a failed command's collected stdout verbatim, line by line, in the multi-error summary. The value arrives via impl From<CommandError> for OperationFailure (crates/selfie/src/package/event.rs:1259-1273), which moves stdout into CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed, from where it reaches PackageEvent::Completed and is also serialized by the MCP server.

This is a general secret-egress surface, independent of any one feature: any user-defined command whose stdout contains something sensitive will have it printed to the terminal and sent to an MCP client when that command fails. selfie's whole model is running user-defined commands, so 'the command's stdout is sensitive' is not an exotic case — an install or check command that echoes a token would do it today.

Provider-sourced dotfiles handle their own resolve path specifically to avoid this, but that is a local fix for one caller and does not address the general surface.
acceptance_criteria: A failing command's stdout is not surfaced verbatim by default, or the risk is documented and the value is redactable.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #74 (merged 445788b).

selfie-ppp: stdout removed from CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed entirely, so the leak is unwritable rather than merely unreached; stderr kept, truncated to 2000 bytes in the library at construction, with truncate_stderr moved to commands/runner.rs so one bound serves both the general failure path and the dotfile resolve path.

title: cargo test -p selfie does not compile without --features with_mocks
description:
CLAUDE.md documents 'cargo test -p selfie   # Test library only' as a working command, but it fails to compile with unresolved imports for MockFileSystem, MockPackageRepository, MockCommandRunner and others — the mocks are gated behind the with_mocks feature.

It appears to work only because a workspace-wide 'cargo test' unifies the feature in from selfie-cli's dev-dependencies, so the failure is invisible unless the crate is tested alone. Reproduced on a clean tree, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to any current feature work.

Fix by either enabling with_mocks for the crate's own test builds or correcting the documented command in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: The command documented in CLAUDE.md for testing the library alone actually compiles and runs.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #70 (merged 19caf87). The compile failure was real when filed and was fixed incidentally by PR #67, which added features=[with_mocks] to test-common's dependency on selfie; test-common is a dev-dependency of selfie, so Cargo unifies the feature into selfie's own test build. What remained broken was CLAUDE.md, which documented the fixed trap as current fact and prescribed an unnecessary flag, contradicting Justfile:31. PR #70 corrects CLAUDE.md and architecture.md, and adds a CI step running the library crate alone, since every workspace-wide command unifies the feature in and so cannot catch this class of break.

NOTE: this bead's acceptance criteria named AGENTS.md, which no longer exists - deleted in cf1efe9 the same day this bead was filed. Only CLAUDE.md needed correcting.

A planned cfg_attr any(test, ...) change was cut and refiled as selfie-gh2v: it is dead code at HEAD, took the no-feature failure from 16 to 55 errors as scoped, and the complete version runs 379 lib tests instead of 393 while exiting 0.

title: Validate environment-specific dotfiles + surface overrides in spec validation
description: ADR-0001 requires: 'Validation must surface environment overrides and missing sources rather than applying them silently.' validate_dotfiles currently only checks top-level (shared) dotfiles. Extend it to also structurally validate each environments.<name>.dotfiles entry (empty/traversal/relative-source/absolute-target checks — extract a per-entry helper), and emit a warning when an environment entry overrides a shared entry's target so the override is not silent. TDD. Follow-up to per-environment dotfiles core (34558ef).
close_reason: Env-specific dotfiles now structurally validated + overrides surfaced as warnings. Implemented in feat(validate) with 3 TDD tests.

title: Secret provider integration point for dotfiles (shell out to 1Password/teller, don't reinvent)
description: ADR-0001 Problem B. selfie must NOT build its own secret store/encryption/templating. Instead provide an integration point that resolves a dotfile's content by running a user-configured provider command at apply time (e.g. 'op read op://vault/item/field', teller). Fits selfie's command-runner identity. DotfileEntry content source becomes: repo file (source) OR provider command (secret/from ref). At apply, run the provider, write result to target; never commit or persist the secret value; drift/state must NOT store the secret's checksum/value (needs distinct semantics - part of this design). Use case: private RubyGems server creds on work machine. User standardizes on 1Password (personal+work) and teller (work GCP/dotenv). Detailed design deferred; depends on selfie-7sv (per-env dotfiles) landing the content-source abstraction. Relates to selfie-t2d (multiple package dirs / private overlay).
close_reason: Provider-sourced and templated dotfiles shipped in PR #67

title: Dotfiles are single-source, not per-environment — no machine-specific config variants (YADM alt-file parity)
description: The 'dotfiles' field is top-level (one 'source' per mapping, deployed to all environments). If home and work legitimately need DIFFERENT versions of a config (e.g. ghostty font size, work-specific proxy settings), selfie cannot represent both — there is a single canonical source. YADM handles this via alt-files (##os.Linux, ##hostname) and templates. For selfie's home+work cross-machine goal this is a structural gap: today the user must unify configs across machines or they'll conflict on deploy. Options to design: per-environment dotfile overrides/variants, templating, or an explicit 'shared vs machine-specific' split. Relates to selfie-522 (environment inheritance). Surfaced 2026-07-23.
design: Per-environment dotfiles (ADR-0001, Problem A). Add optional 'dotfiles: Vec<DotfileEntry>' to EnvironmentConfig. Effective set for current env = top-level shared dotfiles, with any entry whose resolved target matches an env-specific entry REPLACED by it, unioned with env-specific entries introducing new targets. Env-specific overrides shared keyed on target; otherwise added (presence). No exclusion (YAGNI). Source resolution unchanged (relative to package YAML dir). git identity is out of scope (use git-native includeIf). DotfileEntry to gain a content-source abstraction so it composes with secret providers (selfie-B). No backward compat (pre-release).
notes: Core per-environment dotfiles (model + effective-set + apply/drift wiring + tests + docs) landed in 34558ef. Remaining per ADR-0001 tracked as blockers: selfie-chi (validation + override surfacing), selfie-2m1 (list/track/remove consistency).
close_reason: Per-environment dotfiles delivered in 34558ef (EnvironmentConfig.dotfiles + effective-set override/presence + apply/drift wiring + tests + docs; ADR-0001). Single-source limitation resolved. Refinements tracked independently: selfie-chi (env-dotfile validation + override surfacing), selfie-2m1 (list/track/remove consistency).

title: track_dotfile records target as expanded absolute path, breaking cross-machine portability
description: selfie_package_track_dotfile (MCP) and 'selfie track' (CLI) record the dotfile 'target' as a fully-expanded absolute path containing the literal home dir, e.g. 'target: /Users/sloveless/.config/ghostty/config', instead of a portable '~/.config/ghostty/config'. This breaks the core cross-machine value prop: on a machine with a different username (macos-work uses 'steve.loveless') or OS (Linux /home/...), the target resolves to the wrong/nonexistent path. Hand-written specs correctly use '~'. Fix: when tracking, store the target relative to $HOME using '~' (collapse the home prefix) rather than the expanded absolute path. Surfaced 2026-07-23 migrating ghostty/fastfetch/marksman/yamllint/zed via MCP; topgrade had the same issue from earlier tracking.
close_reason: Closed

title: Config loader warns on unknown/ignored keys instead of silently dropping them
description: When selfie loads a config with unknown or stale keys (e.g. the pre-rename 'configs_directory'), it silently ignores them. 'selfie config validate' even reports 'valid'. This hid a broken dotfiles setup for the user. Per user principle: selfie must NOT fail silently — if it can proceed with a funky-but-usable config, it should, but it must emit a warning about ignored/unknown keys (via the event system, not stdout, per the library boundary rules). Applies to both CLI and MCP frontends.

title: Rename max_parallel_installations to max_concurrency and apply everywhere
description:
Two problems:

1. **Misleading name**: `max_parallel_installations` is not used for installations at all — only for concurrent checks in `list` and dep status checks in `status`.

2. **Inconsistent usage**: Several operations that do concurrent work don't honor it — notably `install` (which the name implies it should) and any future bulk operations.

Fix both: rename to `max_concurrency` and apply the semaphore/chunking pattern to all concurrent operations including install. No backward compatibility needed (no releases yet). Affects: config structs, YAML deserialization, CLI config display, install handler, docs, CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Renamed max_parallel_installations to max_concurrency, applied concurrency to audit_all and install_recommends, dropped num_cpus dep. PR #41.

title: Show dependency satisfaction status in package info
description:
When displaying package info (info, list, check commands), indicate whether the package's declared dependencies are actually installed. Currently dependencies are listed in the info command but there's no indication of whether they're satisfied.

This would run the check command for each dependency and show a per-dep status (installed/not installed/unknown). Helps users catch broken dependency chains before attempting an install.

Implementation considerations:
- This is essentially running check on each dep, so it should reuse the existing check logic via PackageService.
- For the list command, this could be expensive if every package's deps are checked — consider making it opt-in (e.g., --check-deps flag) or only showing it in info/verbose modes.
- Emit dependency status via PackageEvent so CLI and MCP can render it.
- Handle missing deps gracefully (dep package file doesn't exist vs dep not installed).
close_reason: Implemented dependency satisfaction status in the status command. Added DependencyStatus struct, concurrent dep checking via execute_check_command_quiet, CLI rendering with colored status, and MCP JSON serialization. 5 new tests covering all edge cases.

title: Show git-dirty indicator on package info commands
description:
Commands that display package information (info, list, check, validate, audit) should also indicate whether the local package YAML file has uncommitted git changes. This helps users notice when their package specs have been modified locally but not yet committed, which matters for keeping configs in sync across machines.

Scope: Add a git-status indicator (e.g., 'modified', 'untracked', 'staged') to package output in commands that report package details. The indicator should appear alongside existing package metadata.

Implementation considerations:
- The selfie library has no git functionality today — this is net-new.
- Following hexagonal architecture, git operations should go behind a trait/port (e.g., GitStatusProvider) so the CLI can use a real implementation and tests can mock it.
- The library should emit git status info via PackageEvent so each frontend (CLI, MCP) can render it appropriately.
- Need to handle: file is untracked, file has staged changes, file has unstaged changes. Also handle gracefully when the package directory is not a git repo.
- Skip unpushed detection — committed is sufficient. This avoids complexity around missing upstream tracking branches.
- Performance: for the list command, checking git status for many files should be efficient (e.g., one 'git status --porcelain' call for the whole directory, not one per file).
close_reason: Implemented and merged in PR #28

title: YAML merge keys (<<: *anchor) not supported by serde_yaml 0.9
description: serde_yaml 0.9 dropped support for YAML merge keys (<<: *anchor) that existed in 0.8. The error is now visible thanks to the ParseError display fix, but the underlying issue remains. title: Remove async-trait — use native async traits + upgrade mockall to 0.14.0
description:
Remove async-trait crate; use Rust's native async fn in traits (stable since 1.75). Upgrade mockall from 0.13.1 to 0.14.0 which supports native async trait mocking.

Files using #[async_trait]: commands/runner.rs, commands/shell.rs, package/service.rs (×2), config/loader.rs. Note: ConfigLoader uses #[async_trait] but has no async methods — can just remove it.

Mocked async traits: CommandRunner (4 async methods), PackageService (7 async methods). Both use #[automock] + #[async_trait] together.

Benefit: Removes heap allocation per async trait call, removes a dependency, uses idiomatic modern Rust.

Risk: mockall 0.14.0 is a major version bump — may have breaking API changes beyond async trait support. Run full test suite after upgrade.
close_reason: Removed async-trait, upgraded mockall to 0.14, native RPITIT async traits, fixed mock visibility and hardcoded shell path

title: OperationFailure duplicates PackageError types field-for-field
description: OperationFailure has variants like PackageFailure::NotFound that mirror PackageError::PackageNotFound field-for-field, creating a parallel error hierarchy. When an error occurs, the same information exists in both PackageError and OperationFailure. OperationFailure should reference or wrap PackageError rather than duplicating its structure. Related to selfie-mqq (double event emission).
close_reason: Merged EnvironmentFailure and PackageFailure enums into OperationFailure::Package(PackageError) wrapper. Deleted ~130 lines of duplicate type definitions and field-copying conversion code.

title: Implement PackageService::create or remove from trait
description: PackageService::create is declared in the trait but the implementation is a stub that returns a placeholder success. The CLI's create.rs bypasses the service entirely and uses PackageRepository directly — the most significant hexagonal architecture boundary violation. Either implement create properly in the service (with event streaming, validation, etc.) or remove it from the trait until ready.
close_reason: PackageService::create is now fully implemented with service handler, event variants, and CLI integration

title: Add tests for ConfigLoader and YamlLoader
description: config/loader.rs (ConfigLoader trait, ConfigLoadError) and config/yaml.rs (YamlLoader) have zero tests. This is the component responsible for finding and reading the config file on disk — a critical path with several error variants (NotFound, MultipleFound, ConfigError) that are never exercised in isolation. config/validate.rs also lacks unit tests (only tested through CLI integration tests).

title: Fix double event emission for errors
description: When an error occurs, the library emits it twice: once as PackageEvent::Error and again inside PackageEvent::Completed { result: Failure } with a re-serialized copy in OperationFailure. This forces the CLI to implement PackageNotFoundTracker as a suppression workaround in common.rs. The Completed event should reference the error, not duplicate it. Additionally, OperationFailure duplicates error types field-for-field (e.g., PackageFailure::NotFound mirrors PackageError::PackageNotFound).
close_reason: Fixed in db33934: eliminated double event emission and removed PackageNotFoundTracker workaround

title: Unify PackageService return types across all methods

All methods should use the same pattern. Either all return EventStream (encoding early-exit errors as the first event in the stream) or all return Result<EventStream>. The inconsistency forces callers to handle two different patterns.

This prevents injecting MockPackageService for unit testing. Commands should accept Box<dyn PackageService> (dynamic dispatch) so mock services can be used in tests. MockPackageService and MockCommandRunner are defined but never used because of this.
close_reason: Refactored all 6 CLI command handlers to accept &dyn PackageService parameter instead of creating service internally. Service creation now happens at the dispatch_package_command level in commands.rs.

title: Fix event_processor tests using real filesystem
description: event_processor.rs tests (lines 328-418) create real ShellCommandRunner and RealFileSystem instances pointing at /tmp/nonexistent. These tests depend on filesystem state and could behave differently in CI. Replace with mock-based tests for deterministic behavior.
close_reason: Already fixed: tests now use stream::iter(vec![...]) to construct EventStream directly, with no real filesystem or command runner dependencies.

These are terminal UI crates that don't appear to be used in the library's production code. Verify usage and move to [dev-dependencies] or remove entirely -- these belong only in the CLI crate.

title: An unreadable install-only package passes sync push but fails apply
description:
After selfie-5j5j lands, the two surfaces disagree in severity for the same bytes.

An install-only package whose top level cannot be re-parsed into serde_json::Value:

- 'validate_unknown_fields' reports ValidationIssue::info(Advisory, ...). sync_service/service.rs filters to Error | Warning, so 'selfie sync push' succeeds.
- 'selfie apply' on the receiving machine hits the new arm, finds nothing to deploy, counts a refusal and exits 1.

So a user is told the file is fine when pushing and that the run failed when applying. The advisory level was chosen deliberately in PR #121 so an unrun check would not block a push, and the apply refusal was chosen deliberately so an unrun check would not produce a silent no-op. Both are defensible alone; together they are inconsistent.

Not necessarily a bug in either decision -- it may be that push should also refuse, or that the two are correctly different because only one of them deploys. Wants a decision.

Note the agreement test added in the selfie-5j5j unit fixtures only the has-dotfiles case, so it cannot see this split.

Found by review during that unit.

title: dotfiles drift reports clean for packages apply refuses
description:
'handle_check_drift' has no top-level unknown-key guard, so 'selfie dotfiles drift' -- and 'sync status', which reads its counts -- says a package is clean while 'selfie apply' refuses it.

Measured on main with a '_dotfiles:' package:

  $ selfie apply -y      -> refuses, names the key, counts a refusal
  $ selfie dotfiles drift -> 'Dotfile drift check: 0 drifted out of 0'  (with a check mark)

drift iterates 'package.dotfiles_for_environment(...)', sees zero entries because the anchor emptied the list, and reports nothing wrong.

The convention is already stated repeatedly in dotfile_service/service.rs ('Same guard, same position -- worded identically'), so this is a gap against the file's own rule rather than a new idea. The selfie-5j5j / selfie-vhw4 unit widens it by adding two more apply-only refusal paths.

Found by review during that unit.

title: save_package can rewrite a file whose top-level check did not run
description:
`unknown_top_level_field_issues` (package/validate.rs) returns `vec![]` when the YAML fails to re-parse into `HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>`, and `save_package` (package/repository/yaml.rs:340) gates the rewrite on it. So a file selfie cannot re-read is rewritten from the struct, dropping the very top-level keys that guard exists to protect -- a `_dotfiles:` block and everything under it.

Third instance of the silent pass PR #121 closed in `validate_unknown_fields`. The other two are being closed together (selfie-5j5j at apply, selfie-vhw4's pairing).

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT of that unit because the tradeoff inverts. On the apply path, refusing over an unrun check stops a deploy on a working machine, so it warns and proceeds. On the write path the cost of refusing is a declined save, which the user can act on, against the cost of silently deleting their keys -- so refusing is arguably correct here even though it is wrong there.

That asymmetry is the decision this bead is for. The current `return vec![]` carries a comment saying a writer must not refuse over a check that did not run; that reasoning was borrowed from the validation path and should be re-argued on its own terms rather than inherited.

Found while planning selfie-5j5j / selfie-vhw4.

title: Replace the three KNOWN_*_FIELDS lists with strum enums
description:
The known-key lists at all three levels are `&[&str]`, so nothing stops a call site pairing a key with the wrong level's list.

`describe_unknown_key_in(key, KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS)` inside `unknown_environment_keys` compiles, produces an issue with the same field path, and tells the user an environment accepts `name, homepage, description, dotfiles, post_install_note, environments`. PR #121's review caught this and pinned it with a test asserting the message, which is the weaker of the two available fixes: three distinct types make the same mistake a compile error.

Sketch, matching the `ValidationErrorCategory` pattern already in validation.rs:

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq,
             strum::Display, strum::EnumString, strum::IntoStaticStr, strum::VariantArray)]
    #[strum(serialize_all = "snake_case")]
    pub(crate) enum EnvironmentField { Install, Check, Audit, Dependencies, Recommends, Dotfiles }

`contains(&k.as_str())` becomes `from_str(k).is_ok()`; the 'expected one of' list comes from `VariantArray` rather than a hand-typed array, so a variant cannot be spelled wrong or left out of the message.

strum 0.28 is already a workspace dependency and crates/selfie already uses it. No field carries `#[serde(rename)]`, so `serialize_all = "snake_case"` reproduces every current string.

SCOPE: KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS, KNOWN_ENVIRONMENT_FIELDS and KNOWN_DOTFILE_FIELDS, plus `describe_unknown_key_in`, `shadows_field` and their callers in package.rs, package/validate.rs and dotfile_service/service.rs.

DOES NOT REPLACE THE GUARD TESTS. The drift that matters is between a struct's serde field names and the list, and the enum is still a parallel declaration; serde exposes no field names at runtime. The serialize-and-compare tests stay. What the enum removes is the wrong-list class, not the incomplete-list class.

Sequenced after PR #121 merges, so a mechanical retype does not ride in the same diff as that PR's behavior changes.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #123

title: shadowing_top_level_keys stays silent when its re-parse fails
description:
`shadowing_top_level_keys` (package.rs:278) returns `Vec::new()` when the YAML fails to re-parse into `HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>`. That is the same silent pass PR #121 closed in `validate_unknown_fields`, on the path that decides whether `selfie apply` refuses the package.

Both call the same parse on the same string, so after #121 the two disagree: validation reports that the check could not run, while `set_source` records zero shadowing keys and apply proceeds. A file that also carries `_dotfiles:` is then deployed with nothing to deploy and a success exit.

Sharing one parse between the two would fix the divergence at the source.

Found by review of PR #121.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #134

title: Local dprint and CI dprint disagree, so just check can pass while check-dprint fails
description:
Hit while fixing review comments on PR #110.

docs/package-files.md passed "dprint check" locally with exit 0 and no output, and CI failed check-dprint on the same commit with a one-word line-wrap difference:

    719|-`selfie spec remove ghost` is in that second group, so it will not delete the file for you. Remove it
    720|-with `rm`.
    719|+`selfie spec remove ghost` is in that second group, so it will not delete the file for you. Remove
    720|+it with `rm`.

The markdown PLUGIN is pinned in dprint.jsonc (markdown-0.17.8.wasm) and CI compiles that same version, so the plugin is not the difference. The dprint CLI is not pinned: locally it is 0.55.2, and .github/workflows/ci.yml uses dprint/check@v2.3, which installs whatever the action defaults to.

CONSEQUENCE: "just check" runs "dprint fmt" and can produce output that CI then rejects. That makes the local gate unable to tell you the formatting is wrong, which is the same class as three other divergences this batch hit — the rustdoc job not being in just check, typos not being in just check, and a stale rlib making just check report a missing pub function.

FIX OPTIONS: pin the dprint CLI version in the CI action (dprint/check accepts a version input) so both sides run the same binary; or pin it in a tool manifest the local environment also reads. Either way the two should be the same version, not the same plugin with different hosts.

Worked around on PR #110 by shortening the sentence clear of the wrap boundary, which is not a fix.

title: --state-directory creates its directory while every other path setting requires one to exist
description:
Raised by the maintainer reviewing PR #108: "If other commands that rely on directories/files (ex config), state-directory should not be creating a directory."

selfie is inconsistent about whether a configured directory must exist:

- package_directory: must exist. A missing one is a hard error with a suggestion to create it.
- the config file path: must exist. A missing file is fatal; a fifo or dangling symlink is refused.
- dotfiles_directory: must exist. Missing means the standalone repository is dropped (see selfie-3kpg for the diagnostics side).
- state_directory: CREATED IMPLICITLY. The deploy-state write calls create_dir_all on the parent (crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:139 and :192), so whatever path was configured is brought into being on first write.

That asymmetry is what turns selfie-hlsp from a loud failure into a silent one. A tilde in a flag value is not expanded, so:

    selfie --package-directory=~/packages package list   -> error, exit 1
    selfie --state-directory=~/state apply -y            -> exit 0, creates ./~/state/

The second reports success having written deploy state into a directory literally named ~ in the current working directory. Nobody will look there, and the next run finds no state and re-deploys everything.

DECIDE THE RULE, do not just patch the symptom. Either every configured directory must exist and be reported when it does not, or selfie creates them consistently and says so. The current split means a user cannot predict which of their settings will be validated.

Note docs/configuration.md (added by PR #108) currently DOCUMENTS the creating behavior. If the behavior changes, that paragraph goes with it — it was written to describe what selfie does, not to endorse it.

Related: selfie-hlsp is the same defect seen from the tilde-expansion side; fixing either one alone leaves the other reachable. selfie-f7nx covers config validate not checking dotfiles_directory or state_directory for absoluteness, which is the third face of it.

title: CLI flags cannot fill gaps in a config file that exists but omits a required setting
description:
Found by the selfie-zse unit's code reviewer; scoped out by that unit's author with an argument the team lead accepted.

docs/configuration.md documents precedence as 'flags, then file, then defaults'. That is only true when the file is ABSENT.

    ~/.config/selfie/config.yaml containing only:
        cli:
          verbose: true

    selfie --environment macos --package-directory ~/pkgs package list
    -> aborts with a missing-field error, despite both required flags being supplied

Mechanism: SelfieConfig has no serde default for environment or package_directory, so try_deserialize fails inside serde. crates/cli/src/main.rs falls back to flags only on ConfigLoadError::NotFound, so an existing-but-partial file takes the Err(other) arm and aborts. A cli:-only config file is a legitimate thing to write, and the docs now say so.

WHY THIS IS NOT A PATCH. Making the documented precedence real requires config loading to return something PARTIAL — environment and package_directory as Option — with resolution happening after the merge. Today load_config deserializes straight to a final SelfieConfig, so a file missing a required key fails before any flag is in scope. That changes load_config's contract for BOTH frontends (the MCP server has no flags, so it resolves to 'missing, and nothing to fill it from') and rewrites every test that loads a partial config.

The selfie-zse unit's config_from_flags is an all-or-nothing emulation bolted onto main's error match, which is why it cannot fill gaps.

INTERIM SHIPPED: docs/configuration.md states that flags apply when there is no config file, and that a file which exists must carry both required settings. The gap is documented rather than silent.

This is a different problem from the four beads that unit carried — 'make precedence real', not 'report what selfie ignored' or 'run with no config file'.

title: find_existing_tracker and find_dependent_packages give false answers when a spec is unreadable
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr final code reviewer. Both need a warning channel added to their signatures, so neither was fixable inside that unit.

Two functions answer a question by enumerating specs, and both silently exclude any spec they could not read — so the answer is wrong rather than incomplete, and the caller acts on it.

1. crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:206-217 — find_existing_tracker

   'if let Ok(output)' with no else, then valid_packages() only. Returns Option<(String, String)> — no channel to report anything.

   An unreadable spec makes this answer a false 'not already tracked'. So 'dotfiles track' can create a DUPLICATE entry for a target some other package already tracks.

2. crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:429 — find_dependent_packages

   Same shape. A dependent package whose spec is unreadable is invisible, so 'spec remove' reports a false 'no dependents' clearance and then deletes.

Both are the pattern selfie-h2kr's unit removed from five other enumerating sites by introducing skipped_spec_warning. These two could not join that set because they have no EventSender or DisplayManager in scope — the fix is a signature change, which is why they are their own work.

Note the failure mode is worse than the ones already fixed. Elsewhere a dropped spec means a missing row in a listing. Here it means a guard returns the safe-looking answer: 'nothing already tracks this' and 'nothing depends on this'. Both precede a write.

Widens with every refusal class added — selfie-h2kr's irregular-file refusal is the newest way for a spec to become unreadable.

Related: selfie-t5sw (spec search), and the bead covering available_packages and four other valid_packages()-only consumers.

title: The MCP server drops the dotfiles repository silently at four sites
A truncated or empty deploy-state file is read as 'nothing deployed' with no warning
description:
Found by the selfie-flka review-only pass; verified on that branch.

crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:304 — content of "", "# nothing\n", and "~\n" all parse SUCCESSFULLY and return (empty state, None). No warning, no diagnostic.

That would be fine if those shapes were unreachable. They are not: save_deploy_state (service.rs:326) documents itself as 'deliberately less durable' and writes via write_file_private with NO atomic rename. An interrupted write can therefore leave a truncated or zero-length file.

On the next apply, selfie reads it as an empty state, treats every dotfile as NotTracked, and re-prompts or re-deploys — indistinguishable from a first run on a fresh machine. The user is told nothing about why their tracked state vanished.

DISTINCT from selfie-y8ub (a corrupt state file being silently swallowed, since that one takes the parse-failure branch and now warns) and from selfie-flka (a parse failure quoting the file). This shape does not fail to parse at all — it parses to an empty document, which is a legitimate value that happens to be indistinguishable from data loss.

Related: selfie-aub already covers deploy state outliving a lost rename after a crash. This is the read-side counterpart — the same durability gap seen from the load path.

Options: distinguish 'file absent' from 'file present but empty' and warn on the latter; or make save_deploy_state atomic so the shape is unreachable; or both. Note the selfie-flka unit deliberately did not widen into this — its 15-row shape table covers exotic malformed inputs (alias-mediated duplicate keys, multi-document files) but not truncation, which is the one malformed shape selfie's own writer can produce.

title: sync_service hand-rolls ParseFailure's job for package files, worse
description:
Found by the selfie-flka unit author while implementing ParseFailure.

crates/selfie/src/sync_service/service.rs:671-687 does by hand, for package files, the two jobs ParseFailure now does properly for the deploy state:

1. Renders serde-saphyr's error with e.to_string(), forwarding its prose verbatim — duplicate-key messages included.
2. Chops the location suffix back off with rfind(" at line "), then re-formats 'line {} column {}' from e.location().

The result reaches a PackageValidationIssue and therefore the MCP JSON.

NOT filed as a leak. Package files are user-authored specs and quoting them back is defensible diagnostics, unlike the machine-written deploy-state file whose keys are dotfile source paths. The problem is that this is the same logic implemented a second time and less well: string-surgery on a rendered message to undo formatting the library just applied, where the typed accessor was available all along.

Two consequences:
- It is fragile in the way .claude/rules/verification.md names: rfind on ' at line ' is parsing selfie's own rendering, so any change to serde-saphyr's suffix format silently changes the output.
- It is a candidate consumer if ParseFailure (currently pub(super) in dotfile_service/state.rs) is ever moved somewhere shared.

Second of two package-file sites with their own saphyr handling; the other is crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:120, which calls bare serde_saphyr::from_str with no options at all — see the bead on unscrubbed package parse errors reaching MCP JSON. Deciding a single rule for package-file parse diagnostics would cover both.

title: A missing dotfiles directory silently disables the package name-collision check
description:
Found by the selfie-hat unit's plan reviewer; verified by the team lead. This is where selfie-hat and selfie-3kpg COMPOSE into a wrong write rather than a missing diagnostic.

THE CHAIN:
1. A stale or misspelled config key (e.g. the pre-rename configs_directory, which selfie-hat is about) is silently ignored, so dotfiles_directory falls back to its default — a sibling of package_directory (crates/selfie/src/config.rs:84-91) — which usually does not exist.
2. Two sites then silently drop the dotfiles repository when that directory is absent, and the thing they drop is the NAMESPACE UNIQUENESS CHECK:

crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:82-90
    // Validate namespace before creating
    let dotfiles_repo = if dotfiles_dir.is_dir() { Some(...) } else { None };
    if let Err(e) = namespace::validate_unique_name(name, &repo, dotfiles_repo.as_ref())

crates/cli/src/commands/spec/create.rs:138-151
    // Build an optional dotfiles repo for namespace validation
    let dotfiles_repo = if dotfiles_dir.is_dir() { Some(...) } else { None };
    match namespace::validate_unique_name(&current_name, repo, dotfiles_repo.as_ref())

3. validate_unique_name therefore checks only the package directory and passes, and selfie CREATES a package whose name collides with an existing standalone dotfile.

Every other site in the selfie-3kpg family loses a diagnostic. These two lose a GUARD, and the result is a write into the user's package directory that the guard existed to prevent.

A third site uses a different idiom for the same drop: crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:197, 'd.is_dir().then_some(d)' inside a repository list.

Full site inventory for this family (six is_dir sites plus the then_some):
- common.rs:80   — create_dotfile_service, silent (selfie-3kpg)
- common.rs:163  — handle_track_standalone, CORRECT: errors + suggestion + exit 1
- dotfiles/list.rs:100 — silent (selfie-3kpg)
- dotfiles/track.rs:32 — harmless, calls handle_track_standalone which refuses immediately after
- track.rs:83    — SILENTLY DISABLES the uniqueness check  <-- this bead
- track.rs:197   — then_some idiom, repository list
- spec/create.rs:140 — SILENTLY DISABLES the uniqueness check  <-- this bead

Neither selfie-hat nor selfie-3kpg predicts this outcome, because each describes a silence in isolation. It is only visible where the two meet.

ASSIGNED to the config-diagnostics unit of the specs-and-config batch, which already owns both halves.
notes:
HARM MODEL CORRECTED by the config-diagnostics unit author, verified by the team lead 2026-08-12. This bead as originally filed overstated the reachable damage.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH THE ORIGINAL FRAMING: it claimed two sites let a colliding package be written. Only ONE does.

crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:82 validates the namespace and then calls common::handle_track_standalone at :92, which refuses at common.rs:163 with 'Dotfiles directory does not exist' and exit 1 BEFORE writing anything. So the dotfiles half of the check is skipped and then nothing is written. Structurally identical to dotfiles/track.rs:31, which this bead already classified as harmless.

DEEPER CORRECTION: if the dotfiles directory genuinely does not exist, there are no standalone dotfiles, so validate_unique_name(name, repo, None) returns the CORRECT answer — the check is not skipped, its answer is trivially 'unique'. A real collision requires standalone dotfiles to EXIST AT A PATH SELFIE IS NOT READING, which is reachable only when dotfiles_directory is misconfigured — the stale-key case selfie-hat covers with a load-time warning printed before every command.

WHAT REMAINS: crates/cli/src/commands/spec/create.rs:139 is the one validation site where a write proceeds — spec create writes into the PACKAGE directory and has no dotfiles-directory refusal. crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:197 is a second, narrower one: find_existing_tracker drops the dotfiles repo, the file looks untracked, and choosing ExistingPackage writes to the package directory with no refusal.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: a targeted 'the namespace was only partly checked' notice at the validation sites would fire on the common correct case (a user with no standalone dotfiles at all) and add nothing in the harmful case that selfie-hat does not already announce. That is a noise generator.

The fix is instead the single rule covering all seven sites: warn when dotfiles_directory was EXPLICITLY configured and is missing; stay silent when the sibling default is simply absent. In the stale-key scenario the explicit key was dropped, so the value is implicit and this bead's sites stay quiet — selfie-hat is what speaks. Correct division of labor.

Priority lowered P2 -> P3 accordingly.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #111

title: dotfiles list swallows a package-load error behind a comment calling it non-fatal
config validate checks package_directory for absoluteness but not dotfiles_directory or state_directory
description:
Found by the selfie-0cb2 code reviewer.

crates/cli/src/commands/config.rs:26 validates the raw config, and the reported fields at :47-64 cover environment, package_directory, command_timeout and max_concurrency. Neither dotfiles_directory nor state_directory is validated for absoluteness or reported back.

Two consequences, and the second is the damaging one:

1. A user cannot see what selfie resolved those two directories to, so a wrong value is invisible until a command behaves oddly.
2. A relative or literal-~ value passes validation silently. Combined with selfie-hlsp (flag values bypass tilde expansion), a '~/state' value produces a directory literally named '~' relative to the process working directory, with exit 0 and a success message.

Paired with selfie-3kpg from the other side: a dotfiles_directory that does not exist is dropped with no message at all, so a typo produces an empty dotfiles listing indistinguishable from 'this package has no dotfiles'. config validate is the one command a user would run to catch that, and it does not look.

Fix: validate both fields the way package_directory is validated, and include them in the reported settings.

title: Promote the serde-saphyr reachability probe into the repo as a test fixture
description:
Two independent probe crates were built during the selfie-flka plan gate. Both are outside the repo and will be lost.

WHAT THEY ARE: crates linking serde-saphyr 0.0.29 against selfie's exact DeployState/DeployEntry shapes with options! { with_snippet: false }, feeding malformed inputs and recording which Error variant fires and what its Display renders. The plan REVIEWER built one (26 shapes); the plan AUTHOR then built a second, independent one (36 shapes) to check the reviewer's correction rather than accept it.

WHY THEY MATTER: reading the source got this WRONG twice over, in both directions.

1. The author read message_formatters.rs, found SerdeInvalidType { unexpected } interpolating a value, and concluded it was a second reachable leak the bead missed. It is NOT reachable — saphyr checks event shape in its own deserializer before serde's Unexpected machinery runs, so every container and scalar mismatch lands on Unexpected { expected: &'static str }, content-free by type. A test written on that premise passed against main before any fix: vacuous.

2. The reviewer's 26-shape sweep concluded the plain duplicate key was the whole class. The author's 36-shape probe found THREE MORE leaking shapes, all still DuplicateMappingKey but reached differently:
   - alias-wraps-dup-key:   anc: &a\n  K: 1\n  K: 2\ndeployed: *a
   - merge-wraps-dup-key:   same anchor, reached via a '<<:' merge key
   - dup-key-via-alias-key: anc: &a K, then '*a :' used twice as a mapping key

The third is the important one: the duplicated key NEVER APPEARS LITERALLY at the duplication site, and the error quotes it anyway. A hand-written fixture trying the obvious 'key:\nkey:' form misses all three.

Also established empirically rather than by reading: DuplicateMappingKey spans both a dotfile source path AND selfie's own field names (dup-inner-field renders 'source_checksum', dup-top-level renders 'deployed'), which is why the warning wording must be 'a key is listed twice' rather than 'an entry is listed twice'. And AliasError is reachable with a String-carrying msg field, though six attempts produced no content-bearing instance — recorded as 'no instance found', not as 'safe'.

WHY PERMANENT: selfie pins serde-saphyr at 0.0.29, a 0.0.x series. selfie-flka's fix is fail-closed — a new content-interpolating variant lands in a wildcard and renders content-free — but fail-closed means new variants are absorbed SILENTLY. Nothing would tell a maintainer a bump changed the reachable set.

SHAPE: selfie-flka's own test 2 (no_malformed_state_file_shape_quotes_its_contents) is the in-repo form and includes the alias/merge shapes. This bead is about promoting the WIDER probe coverage — the shapes that currently parse cleanly and the ones that error content-free — so a bump that moves a shape from one bucket to the other is visible. Assert 'no input marker survives into the message', never 'which variant fired', which would break on harmless upstream refactors.

Sources: scratchpad/saphyr-probe/ (reviewer, 26 shapes) and scratchpad/u7-probe/ (author, 36 shapes, includes src/bin/alias.rs).

title: available_packages and four other callers drop unreadable packages with no diagnostic
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr plan reviewer.

These call list_packages() and then read only valid_packages(), never invalid_packages(), so a package file that failed to read or parse vanishes with nothing said:

- crates/selfie/src/package/port.rs:74 (available_packages) — and therefore every consumer of the package-name list
- crates/cli/src/commands/dotfiles/list.rs:155
- crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:208
- crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:663 and :675

crates/selfie/src/package/service/audit.rs:95 has the same shape and is being fixed inside the selfie-h2kr unit, since audit --all is the command a user most expects to name what it skipped.

Already true today for ordinary parse errors, so this is not introduced by any one change. But it widens with every refusal class added: selfie-h2kr adds an irregular-file refusal, and on these paths the file will simply not appear rather than being reported.

Violates the maintainer's standing rule that selfie may proceed but must say what it ignored. Related: selfie-t5sw (spec search sets include_invalid: false).

The ListOutput type already carries invalid_packages() — the information is available at every one of these sites, it is just not read.

title: Three call sites report an unreadable package as 'not found'
Package parse errors reach MCP JSON with snippets and interpolated content unscrubbed
description:
Found by the selfie-flka plan author while sweeping serde-saphyr's message formatters; verified by the team lead.

crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:119 calls serde_saphyr::from_str(&content) with NO options — no with_snippet: false — and wraps the error in PackageParseError::YamlParse (crates/selfie/src/package/port.rs:370), which holds Arc<serde_saphyr::Error>. Rendering that error therefore emits both the source snippet and any content serde-saphyr interpolates into the message text.

That path reaches the MCP server's JSON via selfie_spec_validate and the selfie_package_* tools.

This is DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT from the deploy-state path that selfie-y8ub and selfie-flka fix, and the difference is defensible: package files are user-authored, so quoting the offending line is desirable diagnostics. Deploy-state files are machine-written and their keys are dotfile source paths, so quoting them is egress.

What is missing is that the asymmetry is undocumented and unenforced. Nothing records that one path deliberately quotes and the other deliberately must not, so the next person to touch either has no signal. And the exposure is real if a package file ever carries inline secret material — the same ~16 interpolating formatters apply.

Decide and record the rule: which deserialization sites may quote their input and which may not, and make it structural rather than a convention, per the selfie-3ij7 precedent.
notes:
RAISED STAKES, from the selfie-flka round-2 code reviewer.

The original filing reasoned that package files are user-authored spec, so quoting them back is defensible diagnostics — lesser stakes than the machine-written deploy state.

That understates it. Package files carry 'command:' and 'vars:' entries, i.e. secret-provider invocations such as:

    dotfiles:
      - command: op read op://vault/item/field
        target: ~/.npmrc

So a malformed package file can quote a credential-store path, a vault item reference, or an argument to a secret provider into an error that reaches the CLI and the MCP JSON. Those are not secrets themselves, but they are reconnaissance on the user's credential layout — the same class of exposure that .claude/rules/secrets.md treats as egress elsewhere.

Note the parse uses DEFAULT options (with_snippet: true, crop_radius: 64), so the rendered error carries a cropped WINDOW of the file, not just the failing field — neighbouring lines come with it. A parse error anywhere near a 'command:' line therefore quotes it.

The classifier built for selfie-flka (ParseFailure in dotfile_service/state.rs) is directly reusable here, which is the other half of the argument for doing this: the mechanism exists, it is scoped pub(super) to one module, and the two package-file sites (repository/yaml.rs:120 and sync_service/service.rs:671-687) are the consumers that would justify promoting it.

title: package list decides whether to show an invalid package by substring-searching the error text
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr plan author.

crates/cli/src/commands/package/list.rs:286 decides whether to display an invalid package row by searching the ERROR MESSAGE for the substring 'environments.'.

Stringly-typed control flow over human-readable text. Any rewording of a validation message silently changes which packages appear in the listing, with no test failure and no compile error to catch it — the exact class .claude/rules/verification.md warns about ('an invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces').

It is also a live hazard for anything adding a new PackageParseError variant: whether the new failure shows up in package list depends on whether its message happens to contain 'environments.'.

Fix by matching on the error variant rather than its rendering. Related: crates/cli/src/commands/package/list.rs:296 has clean_error_message, which strips a self-named path back out of error text — a second instance of parsing selfie's own messages.

title: spec search never mentions a spec file it could not read or parse
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr plan author.

crates/selfie/src/package/service/spec_search.rs:46 sets include_invalid: false, so spec search silently omits any package file that failed to read or parse. Every other enumerating command reports them: spec list prints an Invalid row, package list/status show an inline invalid row, spec validate --all counts them as unparsable and exits non-zero, apply warns 'Skipping unparsable package file', and the MCP server returns an invalid_packages array.

spec search is the one enumerating command that stays silent. A user searching for a package that exists but is corrupt is told it does not exist.

Pre-existing for ALL unparsable files, not specific to any one cause, and it widens as more refusal classes are added (an irregular file per selfie-h2kr becomes another way to vanish from search results).

Violates the maintainer's standing rule: if selfie can proceed it should, but it must say what it ignored.

title: irregular_target_refusal's trait contract says directories are refused; every impl deliberately excludes them
A ~ in a CLI path flag is used verbatim while the same value in the config file is expanded
description:
Found by the selfie-0cb2 code reviewer and REPRODUCED against the real binary, not inferred.

    selfie --package-directory=~/selfie/packages package list
    ✗ Package directory not found: ~/selfie/packages

while the same value in the config file works:

    package_directory: ~/selfie/packages

Neither bash nor zsh expands a ~ that follows '=', so the literal string reaches selfie. crates/selfie/src/config/yaml.rs:85-100 runs expand_path/expand_tilde_only on file-sourced values; build_cli_config (crates/cli/src/config.rs:137) assigns flag values verbatim. Flag values also bypass the absolute-path rule that config/validate.rs enforces on file-sourced values.

Same non-expansion applies to --dotfiles-directory and --state-directory, and the state variant fails worse than the loud error -p gives:

- -p: hard error, exit 1. Loud.
- --dotfiles-directory: create_dotfile_service drops the repository silently (see selfie-3kpg), so standalone dotfiles vanish with no diagnostic.
- --state-directory: state_file_path (crates/selfie/src/fs/target.rs:384-388) joins the literal ~, so deploy state lands in a directory literally named '~' in the current working directory.

NOT fixed in selfie-0cb2's unit deliberately: the fix means making expand_tilde_only public and threading a FileSystem into build_cli_config, which is a library API change well outside that diff and wants its own tests. The gap is documented in docs/configuration.md as an interim measure.

Decide whether flag values should go through the same expansion and absolute-path validation as file-sourced values. They probably should — the asymmetry is the bug, and a user has no way to know which surface expands.
notes:
DEMONSTRATED by the selfie-0cb2 code reviewer, not merely reasoned about:

    selfie --state-directory='~/state' apply -y
    Dotfiles applied: 1 deployed, 0 skipped, 0 conflict(s), 0 refused    # exit 0

created a directory literally named '~' in the process working directory, containing ~/state/deploy-state.yml. No error, no warning, success message, exit 0.

This is the more damaging half of the bead. The -p variant fails loudly ('Package directory not found: ~/packages', exit 1) and is therefore self-correcting; --state-directory and --dotfiles-directory fail silently and WRITE. Anyone running these flags from a repository checkout gets the stray '~' directory in their git working tree.

Confirmed that bash, zsh AND fish all leave --package-directory=~/packages unexpanded, so the shell is not going to save anyone here.

title: ValidationResult::config_file_path holds the package directory, not the config file path
description:
Found by the selfie-0cb2 plan reviewer.

crates/selfie/src/config/validate.rs:74 constructs the result with:

    config_file_path: Some(self.package_directory().clone())

The field is named for the config file but is handed the package directory. ValidationResult::config_file_path() is pub, so this is wrong on the public API, not just internally — any consumer that renders it (CLI table, MCP JSON) reports the wrong path to the user and has no way to notice.

Decide whether the field should carry the actual loaded config file path (the loader knows it) or be removed as unused; do not paper over it by renaming the getter to match the wrong value.

title: config validate exits 0 on warnings and prints no configuration at all
description:
Found by the selfie-0cb2 plan reviewer, confirmed by running the binary.

crates/cli/src/commands/config.rs has three branches. The error branch prints the issue table and returns 1. The success branch prints 'Configuration is valid.' followed by the settings dump (environment, package_directory, command_timeout, max_concurrency) at :47-52. The WARNING branch (:38-44) prints only the issue table and returns 0 — no 'valid', no 'invalid', and no settings dump.

Two consequences:

1. A user running config validate on a config with warnings gets a verdict-free output: it neither says the config is valid nor that it is not, and shows none of the effective settings they ran the command to see.
2. Anything using the settings dump as an oracle silently gets nothing to match. A nonexistent package_directory produces a warning, so the environment: and package_directory: lines are absent entirely — which is how a test asserting on them can pass vacuously.

Related but distinct from selfie-hat, which is about the loader dropping unknown keys before validation ever sees them.

title: apply_all and apply are ~45 lines of near-identical code
description:
The two DotfileService methods differ only in the operation's package name and 'None' vs 'Some(&name)' passed to handle_apply. Everything else -- the collect, the clones, the sender setup, the sudo refusal arm, the warning loop, the ApplyContext -- is duplicated verbatim.

Pre-existing; selfie-tcu2 widened it by adding the refusal arm to both rather than sharing it.

The hazard is the one that already bit once: apply.rs used to duplicate create_dotfile_service line for line, which is how apply ended up running provider commands under a different shell than install and check. A change to the gate or the context has to be made twice here and can be made inconsistently.

Also worth folding in while touching it: both methods call collect_all_packages before the refusal arm discards the result, so a refused run still reads and deserializes every spec file in both repositories.

title: DotfileDriftDetected flattens the DriftType enum to a String at the event boundary
description:
Raised while answering the user's point that finite states and labels should be enums, not strings (2026-08-01).

DriftType IS already an enum -- crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/state.rs:32 -- with five variants: None, RepoChanged, TargetChanged, BothChanged, NotTracked. It has a Display impl.

But PackageEvent::DotfileDriftDetected carries a String field named drift_type (crates/selfie/src/package/event.rs:2111), and the constructor stringifies at the boundary via to_string() (event.rs:579). So a perfectly good enum is flattened to free text on the way out, and every consumer receives a label it cannot match on:

  - the CLI prints it
  - crates/mcp-server/src/event_collector.rs serializes it into JSON that an AI assistant reads AS a typed label

THE FLATTENING IS ALREADY CAUSING FRICTION. PR #93's code reviewer rejected appending a reason clause to that field precisely because it "is no longer a type" once prose is in it -- an AI consumer reads it as an enum. The fix there was to add a separate optional reason field, which is correct, but it works around the stringly-typed label rather than removing it.

Carrying DriftType itself would let the MCP server serialize a stable machine-readable variant name independently of whatever the CLI chooses to print. That is the adapter boundary the architecture already asks for: the library says what happened, each adapter decides how to say it.

CHECK THE SIBLINGS BEFORE DESIGNING. event.rs also has String fields named reason at :925, :1944 and :2090. Some are genuinely free text -- a human-readable explanation -- and should stay String. A skip reason may be a finite set and may not. Decide per field rather than converting all four: the principle is "finite states and labels", not "no strings on events".

Same class as selfie-01pl (SyncError::GitError carrying free text into MCP JSON) and selfie-6k5i (load_deploy_state returning an untyped Option<String>).
acceptance_criteria: DotfileDriftDetected carries DriftType rather than a stringified copy, and the MCP server serializes a stable variant name; or each String-typed event label is confirmed genuinely open-ended and documented as such.

title: load_deploy_state returns an untyped (DeployState, Option<String>) instead of a typed outcome
description:
Raised by the user reviewing PR #91 (2026-08-01): the return type smells.

CURRENT: fn load_deploy_state(...) -> (DeployState, Option<String>)

Result<DeployState, String> is NOT the fix and should not be attempted. The function always yields a usable DeployState -- the warning is orthogonal, not an alternative. On a corrupt file the caller gets an empty state AND a message, and both matter; the doc comment states the invariant outright ('Every caller proceeds afterwards'). Encoding it as Result forces every caller to unwrap_or_else(|_| DeployState::empty()), which is literally the silent swallow selfie-y8ub was filed to remove, relocated from the callee to four call sites.

WHAT ACTUALLY SMELLS, and it is two things:

1. Option<String> is an untyped free-text carrier. The three conditions -- locate, read, parse -- are distinguished ONLY by string content. That is why mutation M6 could be written at all: swap the read message for the parse message and see which test fails. A typed enum makes the distinction structural and the mutation unwritable. Same 'a compile error beats a test' move Unit 4 makes by deleting FileSystem::write_file.

2. The tuple is nameless and silently ignorable.  compiles. Mutations M4a-M4d exist precisely because deleting any one of the four send_warning forwards is invisible.

PROPOSED:

    enum StateLoadFailure {
        Locate(FileSystemError),                              // no path -- that is what failed
        Read  { path: PathBuf, source: FileSystemError },
        Parse { path: PathBuf, source: ... },
    }

returned in a named struct rather than a bare tuple.

THREE PAYOFFS:
- the read/parse distinction stops being a string-equality property
- selfie-jlj2 is fixed for free: it reports that the locate branch names no path, and the Locate variant simply has no path field, which is honest rather than a gap
- each adapter renders the variant its own way instead of receiving a pre-formatted sentence, which is the boundary rule the architecture already asks for

SAME CLASS: selfie-01pl (SyncError::GitError(String) reaching MCP JSON as free text) and the drift_type bead filed alongside this one. The general principle the user stated: finite states and labels should almost always be enums, not strings.

DEFERRED FROM #91 DELIBERATELY -- that PR is green, independently reviewed, and has two more stacked on it; this is a refactor of correct behavior, not a fix. Doing it means touching four call sites, the mock tests and the message-distinguishing test.
acceptance_criteria: load_deploy_state's failure outcome is a typed enum carrying the path where one exists, not a pre-formatted String -- and each adapter renders it.

title: A fifo at the deploy-state path hangs every dotfile command
description:
Found by the Unit 4 plan reviewer. VERIFIED at 9fc9f05.

load_deploy_state checks path_exists and then read_file on the deploy-state path with no irregular-file guard. path_exists is path.exists(), which FOLLOWS, and read_file is fs::read_to_string, which blocks on a fifo. So a fifo at the configured state path hangs 'apply', 'dotfiles drift', 'dotfiles track' and anything else that loads state -- every dotfile command, before it does any work.

THIS IS THE FOURTH UNGUARDED FOLLOWING READ, and the count is the point:
  1. the dotfile TARGET      -- guarded by selfie-qwj3 / PR #93
  2. the repository SOURCE   -- selfie-lwv5, being guarded in Unit 4
  3. the TEMPLATE source     -- resolve_content's ContentSource::Template arm, also Unit 4
  4. the DEPLOY-STATE file   -- this bead, unguarded

Deliberately outside selfie-lwv5's scope, which is the dotfiles repository. Filed because Unit 4 ships prose saying selfie refuses irregular files it would read, and that claim is not complete while this one stands. selfie-yw7i's bead names exactly this hazard: 'shipping a partial invariant is the kind that gets mistaken for a complete one.'

LOW SEVERITY, and say so rather than inflating it: the state directory is selfie's own, under the user's control, and nothing but the user puts a fifo there. There is no attacker in this story. What makes it worth closing is completeness of the claim, not exposure.

Fix: Unit 4 lands the primitive -- irregular_target_refusal, and a pub(crate) repository_path(&Path) constructor to call it with. Reuse both; do not write a third classifier. The guard goes between the path_exists check and the read, matching the ahead-of-the-first-read rule Unit 3 established.

Note the wording will need a third variant: this is neither a deploy target nor a repository file, it is selfie's own state. 'Cannot read the deploy state: {path} is a {kind}' rather than either existing frame.
acceptance_criteria: A fifo, socket or device node at the deploy-state path is refused with a diagnostic rather than hanging every dotfile command.
notes:
CONFIRMED as the least reachable of this family by the PR #94 code reviewer, which reproduced the other two and deliberately did not reproduce this one: it needs a hand-planted fifo at a path selfie composes from config, where the package-directory and dotfiles-repository cases only need a file in a directory the user already manages. Priority stays P3 for that reason.

The family, for whoever picks one up:
  selfie-lwv5  dotfiles repository source  -- fixed in PR #94
  <the spec-enumeration bead>              -- P2, reproduced, spec list/info/package list wedge
  selfie-8szl  deploy-state file           -- this one, P3, not reproduced
  and the template read behind read_referenced_file, folded into #94 during review

title: dotfiles drift is silent for a package whose dotfiles a shadowing key dropped
description:
Found by the PR #92 code reviewer.

selfie-g199 makes 'selfie apply' refuse a package whose YAML carries a top-level key shadowing a real field -- '_dotfiles:' being the case that started it, where every dotfile in the package silently vanished. Package::shadowing_top_level_keys is consulted in handle_apply and nowhere else.

handle_check_drift has no equivalent gate. So 'selfie dotfiles drift' reports NOTHING for exactly the file whose dotfiles disappeared: apply now says 'refused, this key hides a real field', and drift says nothing at all, because from its point of view the package has no dotfile entries to check.

That is within selfie-g199's acceptance criteria as filed, which scope it to apply -- the unit did not overreach. It is the same silence one command over.

RELATED PATTERN, worth reading before designing: this batch closed selfie-m5dv, selfie-c28 and filed selfie-l9y4 on the identical shape -- one path drew a distinction and its sibling path did not, and the asymmetry was invisible from either side because each was read alone. PR #93's fix for selfie-ktha is the counter-example to copy: it put the shared condition in ONE function (unmanaged_symlink_reason) called from both handle_apply and handle_check_drift, so the parity is structural rather than two copies that can diverge.

Fix direction: consult shadowing_top_level_keys in handle_check_drift too, and decide what drift SAYS -- a drift line for a package that cannot be checked is a different thing from a per-entry drift line, and there are no entries to attach it to. Consider whether the answer is a package-level warning rather than a drift line at all. Check selfie-utzh at the same time; it is the same question for secret-bearing entries on the drift path.
acceptance_criteria: 'selfie dotfiles drift' reports something for a package whose dotfiles were dropped by a shadowing top-level key, rather than staying silent -- and apply and drift agree.

title: secrets.md's refusal convention does not mention irregular targets
description:
Found by the Unit 3 (PR #93) code reviewer.

.claude/rules/secrets.md's last bullet reads: 'A symlinked dotfile target is refused, and every command says so the same way' -- apply refuses the write, drift reports the refusal wherever apply would refuse, track refuses the entry outright. It goes on to say the parity is structural rather than asserted, because drift gates on deploy_decision, the same function apply calls.

After PR #93 that bullet has an exact sibling the rules file does not mention: an IRREGULAR target (fifo, socket, character or block device) is refused by apply, drift and both track handlers alike, worded through the same refusal_warning. Same convention, same wording discipline, same parity -- and a reader extending refusals will read the rules file rather than docs/.

TWO THINGS BELONG IN THE COMPANION SENTENCE, and the second is the one that matters:

1. The convention itself: an irregular target is refused everywhere a symlinked one is, through the same formatter.

2. THE TRAP. The two checks use DIFFERENT stats, deliberately, and getting it backwards reintroduces a hang:
   - symlink_refusal uses fs::symlink_metadata -- does NOT follow -- because 'is the final component a link' is a question about the name.
   - irregular_kind uses fs::metadata -- DOES follow -- because the hazard is what open() will land on, and read_file/path_exists both follow.
   PR #93's review found exactly this hole in the first draft: with symlink_metadata, a symlink pointing at a fifo passed the guard and then blocked on the read, with the symlink refusal sitting ~57 lines downstream. Mutation M12 (fs::metadata -> fs::symlink_metadata) reproduces it.

Also worth stating: layer 2 (write_file_no_follow's O_NONBLOCK plus post-open descriptor check) protects only the WRITE. The reads in apply, drift and track have no layer 2, so for reads the layer-1 guard IS the enforcement -- which is why it must not be described as merely advisory.

Note selfie-ley3 (secrets.md is 213 lines and needs condensing) -- do not simply append. If ley3 is done first, this content belongs wherever the paths-and-permissions material lands.
acceptance_criteria: secrets.md states the irregular-target refusal convention alongside the symlink one, including which stat each check uses and why they differ.

title: validate_unknown_fields swallows a re-parse failure and reports nothing
description:
Found by the Unit 3 plan reviewer. VERIFIED at crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:239-243: validate_unknown_fields re-parses the package's raw_yaml to enumerate its top-level keys, and on a parse failure does 'return vec![]'.

So a package whose raw YAML fails to re-parse gets NO top-level unknown-field diagnostics AND no signal that the check was skipped. 'selfie spec validate' reports whatever the other checks found and says nothing about the one that did not run.

Same silent-fallback shape as selfie-y8ub (load_deploy_state swallowing a corrupt state file), which Unit 2 fixed by warning on three of four paths while staying silent only on the genuinely-normal case. The principle the user stated there applies here: if it can proceed, it should, but it must say what it ignored.

DISTINCT from selfie-t8t2, which is the EMPTY raw_yaml case (a programmatically built Package, where the check correctly has nothing to look at). This is the NON-EMPTY but unparsable case, where there is something to look at and selfie could not.

Note the condition is odd on its face: the package was already deserialized successfully, so its YAML parsed once. A re-parse into HashMap<String, Value> can still fail on input the typed deserialize tolerated. Worth establishing whether the branch is reachable at all before designing a fix — if it is not, the honest change may be to say so rather than to add a warning nobody will see.

Relevant to selfie-g199's work: Unit 3 adds shadowing-key detection that runs through the same re-parse, so this branch now suppresses two checks rather than one.
acceptance_criteria: An unparsable raw_yaml either produces a diagnostic naming the package, or the branch is shown unreachable and documented as such.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #121

title: A conflict diff against an unreadable target renders the whole file as an addition
description:
Found by the Unit 3 plan reviewer. VERIFIED at crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1394-1395:

    let target_content =
