        filesystem.read_file(target_path.path()).unwrap_or_default();

This is the SECOND read of the target on the apply path -- the first is at :1276 for the checksum -- and it is the one that builds the diff shown to the user during conflict resolution.

If the target became unreadable between the two reads (permissions changed, the file was replaced, an IO error), unwrap_or_default() yields an empty string and unified_diff then renders the ENTIRE repository file as an addition. The user is shown a diff asserting the target is empty, and asked to accept or reject on that basis. If they accept, the write proceeds -- which is the correct outcome by luck rather than by decision.

The severity is in the prompt, not the write: a conflict prompt exists precisely so a human can judge, and it is showing them a diff that is not true. Same class as selfie-7baj ('Revealing a conflict shows an unreadable target as empty') -- CHECK WHETHER THIS IS A DUPLICATE OF selfie-7baj BEFORE WORKING IT; that bead may already cover this exact site, in which case close this against it and carry the line reference across.

Fix direction: distinguish 'read failed' from 'read empty'. A failed read at this point should abandon the conflict rather than diff against nothing -- the entry is already refused-or-conflicted, and 'selfie could not read the target to show you the difference' is an honest outcome where a fabricated diff is not.
acceptance_criteria: A conflict whose target cannot be read reports that, rather than presenting a diff against empty content -- or this is closed as a duplicate of selfie-7baj.
notes:
NOT A DUPLICATE of selfie-7baj — checked. They are siblings on the two content paths, and both should be fixed together or the asymmetry persists:

  selfie-7baj  SECRET path      — secret_conflict_summary / ConflictDetail::Secret / the reveal flow, service.rs:876, where current.unwrap_or_default().to_vec() turns Unreadable into b""
  selfie-l9y4  REPOSITORY-FILE  — the ordinary conflict diff, service.rs:1394-1395, where read_file(...).unwrap_or_default() feeds unified_diff

7baj is the more developed writeup and records the principle: secret_conflict_summary's own comment says reporting '0 lines' 'would read as an empty file and understate what an overwrite destroys'. That principle applies verbatim here — the repository-file path never got the distinction the secret path deliberately drew.

Same shape as selfie-m5dv and selfie-c28: the secret path drew a distinction, the repository-file path did not, and the gap went unnoticed because each path was read on its own. Whoever fixes one should fix both.

title: A fifo or device node committed into the dotfiles repository hangs apply
description:
Found by the Unit 3 plan reviewer. VERIFIED: handle_apply reads the SOURCE at crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1257 with no irregular-file guard.

selfie-qwj3 and Unit 3 are scoped to dotfile TARGETS -- the path selfie writes to. This is the identical defect on the other side of the copy: a fifo, socket or device node committed into the dotfiles repository is read as a source, and reading a fifo blocks exactly as reading one as a target does. apply hangs with no timeout, since command_timeout governs provider commands rather than filesystem reads.

Reachable in practice: the dotfiles directory is a git repository the user syncs between machines. Git cannot store a fifo or a device node, so this is not reachable through a normal clone -- but it IS reachable through a local mkfifo in the dotfiles directory, a restored backup, or a filesystem-level copy. Lower severity than the target-side case for that reason, which is why Unit 3 correctly declined to widen.

Unit 3 lands the primitive this needs: a free irregular_refusal(&Path) in fs/real.rs using a FOLLOWING stat (fs::metadata), plus FileSystemError::IrregularTarget. Reuse it -- do not write a second classifier. Note the source path wants different wording than the target path: refusing to READ a repository file is a different user-facing message than refusing to WRITE a target, in the same way selfie-yw7i notes track's refusal reads differently from apply's.

Check whether the containment guard (crate::paths::is_within) runs before the read; if so the guard belongs immediately after it, following the ahead-of-the-first-read rule Unit 3 established.

Also check the secret path: SecretApply resolves content by running a command rather than reading a repository file, so it may not be affected -- confirm rather than assume.
acceptance_criteria: A fifo, socket or device node in the dotfiles repository is refused with a diagnostic rather than hanging apply.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #94 (squash-merged as 2398495). Guards sit ahead of every repository read, reusing the primitive from selfie-qwj3 rather than a second classifier.

FOUR reads, not the one this bead names. apply, drift, resolve_content's Template arm -- the source:+vars: credential path, which this bead guessed was unaffected and is not -- and read_referenced_file behind selfie spec validate. That fourth was found in review after the docs already claimed it was covered, and reproduced as a hang.

Still open in this family: selfie-h2kr (P2, a fifo in the PACKAGE directory wedges spec list, spec info, package list/status and validate --all) and selfie-8szl (the deploy-state path).

title: spec edit silently deletes a top-level _dotfiles block on rewrite
description:
Found by the Unit 3 plan author while scoping selfie-g199.

YamlPackageRepository::save_package (crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:243-261) guards against laundering ENTRY-level unknown keys back out to disk, but not TOP-LEVEL ones. So a package file containing '_dotfiles:' -- the selfie-g199 bug -- survives a read but is silently dropped when 'selfie spec edit' rewrites the file, because the deserialized Package has no field holding it.

Net effect: the user's dotfile block disappears from their spec with no diagnostic, as a side effect of editing something unrelated.

Same hazard class as selfie-g199 (an underscore-prefixed top-level key that shadows a real field), but a different mechanism and a different command. g199 makes apply REFUSE such a package; this is about what happens when a package like that is written back.

NOT folded into selfie-g199's unit deliberately: the fix needs either a new PackageRepoError variant or a rename of the existing UnknownDotfileFields, and an error-variant change does not belong smuggled into a unit scoped to apply-time refusal. Filed so the two can be sequenced properly.

Check selfie-g199's implementation first -- if it lands 'shadowing_top_level_keys' on Package (the approach under review), save_package can consult that directly rather than re-deriving the check from raw_yaml.
acceptance_criteria: A package whose YAML carries a top-level key that shadows a real field is not silently rewritten without it -- save_package refuses or preserves it.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #127

title: apply and drift are both silent about an untracked in-sync symlinked target selfie will never manage
description:
Handed over from Unit 2 (selfie-phnh / selfie-y8ub, PR #91) by its author, who correctly declined to widen that unit to cover it.

After PR #91, an untracked dotfile whose target is a symlink and whose contents already match the repository file produces a PERMANENT 'not tracked' drift line and a non-zero 'selfie sync status' count -- with NO reason attached. The user is told something is wrong and never told what.

The reason is gated on apply's decision. deploy_decision answers Skip for an in-sync target, and both refusal checks exclude Skip by design -- apply's (service.rs:1333 at cc8e1f8) and drift's (service.rs:1638), the latter carrying a comment stating outright that gating on drift type instead would warn exactly where apply is silent. So neither command mentions the symlink.

IMPORTANT FRAMING, from the Unit 2 author: after #91 this is NOT merely inherited silence, it is slightly LOUDER. Before #91 the Skip record settled the entry and drift went quiet after the first apply; now the drift line persists forever. So the problem is 'a visible symptom with no stated cause' rather than 'an invisible problem' -- easier and more urgent than it sounds, because the user is already looking at it.

WHY UNIT 2 CORRECTLY REFUSED TO FIX IT THERE (do not re-derive):
1. It breaks an_in_sync_symlinked_target_is_left_alone_and_not_reported, a control whose entire value is the silence.
2. It forces a parallel change on the drift side to preserve the parity .claude/rules/secrets.md pins as STRUCTURAL -- 'drift reports the refusal wherever apply would refuse, gated on deploy_decision, the same function apply calls'. Breaking that symmetry from inside a unit about the state file is the wrong place to make a two-command visibility decision.
3. It requires rewriting docs/package-files.md's symlink and drift passages, both of which #91 already edited.

Fix direction: this is a decision about what apply and drift each say for an entry selfie will never manage, and it has to be made for BOTH commands together or the parity breaks. Consider whether the drift LINE alone (without a warning) is the right place for the reason, since that is where the user already is.

Distinct from selfie-v7py (a TRACKED entry whose target later becomes a symlink -- that one is fully invisible, no drift line at all) and from selfie-utzh (drift never applies the target rule to secret-bearing entries). Three different symlink-visibility gaps; read all three before designing.
acceptance_criteria: A user who sees a permanent 'not tracked' drift line for a symlinked in-sync target can find out from selfie why it never clears -- and apply and drift still agree with each other.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #93 (merge 0c5c36c). An untracked, in-sync, symlinked target now says why it will never settle -- on apply's skip line and on the drift line, in the channel each command already uses, with no new warning.

One shared predicate read by both commands, so they cannot diverge. DotfileDriftDetected gained a reason field rather than having prose appended to drift_type, which MCP serializes as a typed label.

Both silence controls pass unmodified, which was the design's central claim.

Scoped to NotTracked on purpose. A TRACKED entry whose target later became a symlink is selfie-v7py -- a different bug with no drift line at all. Mutation M11 survived until a test was added for that boundary, so the scoping is now enforced rather than asserted; see the note on selfie-v7py before changing it.

title: Suppressing serde-saphyr snippets does not stop a parse error quoting state-file content
description:
VERIFIED at source by the Unit 2 code reviewer and independently by team-lead.

Unit 2 (selfie-y8ub) deserializes the deploy state with serde_saphyr::options! { with_snippet: false } so that a parse failure cannot render the file's contents into a warning that reaches PackageEvent and the MCP server's JSON. That works for SNIPPET rendering. It does not achieve the broader intent, because serde-saphyr interpolates content into some error MESSAGES directly, independent of any snippet setting:

  serde-saphyr-0.0.29/src/de/message_formatters.rs:217
    "duplicate mapping key: {k}, set DuplicateKeyPolicy in Options if acceptable"
  and :499
    "duplicate mapping key: {k} not allowed here"

DuplicateKeyPolicy defaults to erroring. In a deploy-state file THE KEYS ARE DOTFILE SOURCE PATHS, so a duplicated key quotes a repository-file dotfile path verbatim into the warning:

  Cannot parse deploy state '/state/deploy-state.yml': duplicate mapping key: zzz-recon-marker/id_rsa.conf, set DuplicateKeyPolicy in Options if acceptable at line 3, column 3; continuing as though nothing had been deployed

Not a credential exposure -- secret-bearing entries record nothing (ADR-0003) -- but it is exactly the reconnaissance content save_deploy_state writes owner-only to protect: the set of dotfiles managed on this machine.

WHY THE UNIT'S TEST COULD NOT SEE IT: a_parse_failure_does_not_quote_the_state_file uses a SCANNER error ('key: [unclosed'). Scanner and typecheck errors carry only line/column plus the struct's own field names -- they are the one error class that structurally cannot quote a key. The fixture did not vary along the axis under test, which is .claude/rules/testing.md's documented failure mode occurring inside the test written to prevent it. Unit 2 adds a duplicate-key case; this bead is the REMAINING structural gap.

The narrow fix is in Unit 2. This bead is the general question: if the invariant is 'no state-file content reaches an event', relying on a third-party library's message shape cannot enforce it. A future serde-saphyr version can add a new message that interpolates a key, and nothing would fail.

Fix directions:
- Scrub the rendered error before it reaches the message -- e.g. render location only (line/column) and discard the library's prose entirely. Cheapest and structural; costs diagnostic quality.
- Set DuplicateKeyPolicy explicitly so the duplicate-key path is not an error at all. Check what that does to state files that legitimately contain a duplicate -- last-wins may be the honest behavior for a mirror file.
- Allowlist the error kinds known not to interpolate. Fails open for every kind added later; noted only to be rejected.

Related: selfie-8qyv (the unusable state file is also overwritten), and .claude/rules/secrets.md's rule that a bound belongs at every forwarding site.
acceptance_criteria: Either no serde-saphyr error message can carry state-file content into an event, or the residual is documented with the specific error classes that can and why that is accepted.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #109

title: secrets.md has grown to 213 lines and needs condensing
description:
Raised by the user while reviewing PR #90 (2026-08-01): secrets.md is over 200 lines, which reads as accreted AI-written prose rather than a rule someone would keep in their head.

Measured at a6c5baa:

  .claude/rules/secrets.md      213
  .claude/rules/architecture.md 113
  .claude/rules/testing.md       82
  .claude/rules/verification.md  65
  .claude/rules/domain.md        57
  CLAUDE.md                     156

secrets.md is nearly double the next largest and larger than CLAUDE.md itself. PR #90 added 21 lines to it (the three-functions/two-constructors passage) and PR for Unit 2 touches the adjacent filesystem doc, so it is still growing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: .claude/rules/*.md load into agent context by path glob, and a rule nobody finishes reading is a rule that does not bind. This project has already been bitten four times by agents quoting STALE rule text (see the bd memory 'agent-context-goes-stale-when-the-repo-moves'); length compounds that, because the longer the file the likelier a reader skims to the heading they expected rather than the sentence that changed.

DO NOT SIMPLY CUT. Much of the length is load-bearing and was written because the short version was misread — several passages explicitly say 'do not read this backwards', 'it has been stated backwards before', or record a specific wrong fix someone attempted. Deleting those re-opens the failure they document. The task is CONDENSING, not trimming:

- Look for passages that restate the same rule at three levels of detail (the TargetPath section now does this: the newtype bullet, the three-constructors bullet, and the never-canonicalize bullet overlap).
- Look for narrative that could become a table or a list of call sites.
- Look for content that belongs in a doc comment at the site it governs rather than in the rules file — Unit 1 and Unit 2 both moved justifications INTO the code for exactly this reason, and the rules file was not shortened correspondingly.
- Consider whether the leak-scanning material and the paths/permissions material are one rule or two files. selfie-4pa3 is relevant: it reports secrets.md does not load for the files that implement its leak-scanning rule, which is a scoping problem a split might also fix.

Check selfie-4pa3 before starting; the two may want to be done together, since one is about which files trigger the rule and this is about what the rule says.
acceptance_criteria: secrets.md is materially shorter with no load-bearing constraint lost -- every 'do not read this backwards' style warning still present or relocated to the code it governs -- and the split-vs-condense decision is recorded.

title: A tracked entry whose target later becomes a symlink goes silent while the state keeps claiming a deployment
description:
VERIFIED by the Unit 2 plan reviewer against 14daa1a.

Sequence: selfie deploys a dotfile normally and records it. The user (or stow, or another dotfile manager) later replaces that target with a SYMLINK whose content still matches the repository file.

From then on: detect_drift returns None (checksums still match), so deploy_decision yields Skip, and BOTH apply's refusal check (service.rs:1236) and drift's (service.rs:1517) exclude Skip by design. Nothing warns. The deploy state continues to assert a deployment selfie can no longer perform -- the next repository edit will route to the refusal and the entry will never advance again.

SAME FAMILY as selfie-phnh but NOT fixed by it. phnh guards the record on the NotTracked path -- an entry that was never legitimately deployed. This is an entry that WAS legitimately deployed and whose target changed underneath it. The record was honest when written and became a lie afterwards.

ALSO DISTINCT from the residual silence handed to Unit 3, which is about the UNTRACKED in-sync symlinked case. Three different symlink-and-state situations; do not merge them without re-reading all three.

The state entry is what makes this invisible: with a recorded checksum the drift type is None, so there is no drift line either. Compare selfie-phnh's case, where removing the record at least produces a permanent 'not tracked' line the user can see.

Fix directions: the Skip exclusion at :1236 is deliberate and documented (an in-sync target is not written to, so nothing is refused) -- do not simply delete it, that breaks an_in_sync_symlinked_target_is_left_alone_and_not_reported. Consider instead checking symlink-ness when an entry HAS a recorded deployment, which is the case where selfie has made a promise it can no longer keep. That asymmetry is the fix's shape.

Found by the Unit 2 plan reviewer while checking whether the phnh fix covered every route to a lying state entry. It does not, and the bead's scope never claimed to.
acceptance_criteria: A tracked entry whose target has become a symlink is either reported, or the silence is documented as deliberate with the reason.
notes:
A TEST NOW ASSERTS THE CURRENT (BUGGY) BEHAVIOR AS FACT — read this before you start, or a deliberate design decision will look like a regression you caused.

PR #93 (selfie-ktha) added crates/selfie/tests/dotfile_service_tests.rs :: a_tracked_symlinked_target_is_outside_this_reason. It deploys to a plain file, moves it aside, links to it, and asserts that NEITHER apply NOR drift says anything — which is exactly the invisibility this bead is about.

It exists because mutation M11 SURVIVED: widening unmanaged_symlink_reason's predicate from DriftType::NotTracked to also answer for None failed no test at all, because every other fixture varied the symlink axis and none varied the drift type. So the NotTracked scoping — argued for in that function's own doc comment — was enforced by nothing until this test.

Consequence for you: fixing v7py MUST change that test, on purpose. Its own docstring says so. Do not read the failure as a regression and do not weaken the assertion to make it pass — the correct move is to rewrite it to assert whatever the fixed behavior is, and to confirm the mutation still bites afterward (widening the predicate should still fail something).

Also relevant: PR #93's shared predicate unmanaged_symlink_reason is called from both handle_apply and handle_check_drift, so whatever you decide has to hold for both commands or the parity secrets.md pins breaks. Do not fix one side.

title: An unusable deploy-state file is overwritten, destroying whatever was recoverable
description:
Deferred deliberately from selfie-y8ub's unit (Unit 2 of the target-semantics batch), with the reasoning recorded here rather than lost.

selfie-y8ub makes load_deploy_state REPORT an unusable state file instead of swallowing it silently. It does not stop selfie from then DESTROYING that file. The sequence is unchanged: load returns an empty state, apply or track records into it, and save_deploy_state writes a fresh file over the old one. Every entry that was in the unreadable-or-corrupt file is gone, including any a human could have salvaged by hand.

That is the second half of y8ub's own description -- 'answering those prompts then overwrites the state with a fresh empty-derived one, destroying whatever was recoverable' -- and it is NOT covered by that bead's acceptance criterion, which asks only for a warning naming the file.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED rather than folded in:

1. Preserving the file needs a rename or copy that the FileSystem port does not currently expose. Adding a port method is an adapter change, which is a different unit's territory.
2. The READ-failure case cannot be preserved by copying at all -- if selfie could not read the bytes, it cannot write them somewhere else either. So 'move it aside' and 'copy it aside' are different fixes for the two conditions, and only one of them works for both.
3. The user's stated principle (selfie-hat) is 'if it can proceed, it should, but it must say what it ignored'. The warning satisfies that. Refusing to save would satisfy a stronger principle the user has not asked for, and would make a corrupt state file block all future applies until hand-repaired.

Fix directions, roughly in order of cost:
- Refuse to save when the load reported a failure, so the old file survives until the user deals with it. Cheapest, but converts a degraded run into a blocked one -- needs a decision about whether that is wanted.
- Rename the unusable file aside (deploy-state.yml.corrupt or similar) before the first save, so the fresh file is created beside it rather than over it. Needs a rename on the FileSystem port. Works for the parse-failure case; for the read-failure case a rename may still succeed where a read did not, which is the argument for preferring rename over copy.
- Both, keyed on which of the three failure conditions occurred (see selfie-y8ub's unit for the three-way split: resolve, read, parse).

Documented as a known limitation in docs/configuration.md under state_directory by the y8ub unit, so the behavior is at least stated rather than surprising.

Filed at plan time by the Unit 2 author, who identified it and correctly declined to widen the unit.
acceptance_criteria: An unusable deploy-state file is not destroyed by the next apply or track -- it is preserved, or the save is refused -- or the overwrite is confirmed as the deliberate choice with the reason recorded.

title: dotfiles drift never applies the target rule to secret-bearing entries
description:
VERIFIED by the Unit 1 code reviewer against c67a986 (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1421-1430).

A spec entry with a 'command:' source and 'target: ~alice/x' produces:

  selfie apply           -> "Skipping '~alice/x': target uses the '~user' form; selfie does not resolve another user's home directory"
  selfie dotfiles drift  -> "provider-sourced (not verifiable without resolving)"

Drift's secret-bearing arm returns that message before any target rule is consulted, so it never tells the user the entry can NEVER deploy -- only that drift cannot verify it. Those are different facts and the second one hides the first. A user checking drift to find out whether their config is healthy is told the entry is merely unverifiable.

NOT a defect introduced by the Unit 1 target-rule reconciliation (selfie-jlum/q9t3/hkhb/m5dv, commit c67a986), and nothing in that commit claims otherwise -- its new drift guard sits in the REPOSITORY-FILE branch, and .claude/rules/secrets.md's drift-parity sentence is scoped to symlink refusals. So this is a gap in the reconciliation's coverage, not a false claim in it.

DISTINCT from selfie-tl1w, which is about the ORDER of the containment and target-rule checks on the repository-file path. This is about the target rule not being reached at all on the secret-bearing path.

The parity that secrets.md asserts -- 'drift reports the refusal wherever apply would refuse' -- is structural for symlinks because both go through deploy_decision. The target rule has no equivalent shared gate on the secret-bearing branch.

Fix direction: apply TargetRejection::of (crates/selfie/src/fs/target.rs) to the entry's target in drift's secret-bearing arm before the not-verifiable message, and report the refusal in apply's words -- the same wording deploy_target's callers already share. Cheap: the rule is textual and needs no home directory, so it costs no filesystem access on a path that deliberately avoids resolving anything.

Likely Unit 3 territory ('A refusal must be visible').
acceptance_criteria: 'dotfiles drift' names the target-rule refusal for a secret-bearing entry whose target the rule rejects, rather than reporting only that it is provider-sourced.

title: apply and drift order the containment and target-rule refusals differently
description:
Reported by the Unit 1 author during selfie-jlum/q9t3/hkhb/m5dv implementation (commit c67a986). Author's own confidence ~55-60%; VERIFY BEFORE ACTING.

handle_apply checks source containment (crate::paths is_within) BEFORE the target rule; handle_check_drift checks the target rule FIRST. Both orderings are pre-existing -- the Unit 1 work preserved each site's original order rather than unifying them, deliberately, to keep that diff scoped.

Consequence: for an entry that fails BOTH checks -- a source escaping the package directory AND a target that is relative or uses the ~user form -- 'selfie apply' names the containment problem and 'selfie dotfiles drift' names the target problem. Same entry, same defect set, two different first diagnoses.

The disposition is IDENTICAL either way (both refuse the entry), so this is a diagnostic-consistency bug, not a safety one. It matters because target_refusal exists precisely to make apply and drift say the same thing about the same entry -- .claude/rules/secrets.md documents that parity as structural ('drift reports the refusal wherever apply would refuse -- gated on deploy_decision, the same function apply calls'). An entry with two defects escapes that parity through the ordering rather than through the message.

Fix directions: unify the order at both sites (pick one and document why), or emit both diagnoses rather than the first. Check whether deploy_decision can carry the full set instead of the first failure.

Do not fold this into a larger refactor without measuring first: confirm the divergence with a two-defect fixture through both commands before changing anything, since the author flagged its own confidence as moderate.
acceptance_criteria: apply and drift report the same first diagnosis for an entry that fails both the containment check and the target rule -- or the divergence is confirmed absent and this bead is closed as not-reproducible.
close_reason:
Duplicate of selfie-tl1w, which predates it and describes the identical divergence: handle_apply checks is_within before the target rule, handle_check_drift checks them in the opposite order, so an entry failing BOTH gets a different first diagnosis depending on which command was run.

selfie-tl1w is the one to work. Nothing to carry across -- it is the fuller writeup and already records that both commands suppress the entry either way, so no guard is weaker than it looks.

My fault for filing without searching first; the Unit 1 code reviewer caught the duplication. Independently rediscovered by the Unit 1 author during c67a986, which is corroboration that the divergence is real and still present after the target-rule reconciliation.

title: normalize_path silently drops a leading '..' and its doc does not say so
acceptance_criteria: normalize_path's behavior on a leading '..' is either documented where it lives, or changed to preserve the component -- and any caller relying on the drop says so.

title: selfie track reports 'Already tracking' and exits 0 for an entry whose target can never deploy
description:
VERIFIED at 4ef9c05. crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:51 -- handle_track calls find_existing_tracker(file, config) and, on a match, prints "Already tracking '<target>' in spec '<pkg>'" and returns 0. That happens BEFORE the library is called at all.

find_existing_tracker (same file, :183-210) expands the caller's path and each entry's target with expand_target_path and compares them. It has NO notion of whether the recorded target is one selfie could ever deploy to. So a spec entry carrying a relative or '~user/...' target that string-matches the argument produces a success exit code and a message asserting the file is tracked -- when a later apply is guaranteed to refuse it.

This is the CLI's own pre-check, independent of the library guards. Unit 1 (selfie-jlum/q9t3/hkhb/m5dv) adds a target-rule guard to BOTH library track handlers (dotfile_service/service.rs handle_track_standalone and handle_track_for_package), which covers 'selfie dotfiles track', 'selfie package track-dotfile' and the MCP tool -- but NOT the interactive 'selfie track <file>' path when the short-circuit fires. Unit 1's user-facing claim is therefore scoped to those three entry points, deliberately, and this bead carries the remainder.

Note the gap is narrow but lands on the most likely command: it fires only when the spec ALREADY contains a bad entry matching the argument. A brand-new file falls through to the library and is guarded correctly.

Same shape as selfie-ywvs and selfie-q9t3 -- a track path reporting success for an entry apply will refuse -- but one layer up, in the adapter rather than the service.

Fix directions: have find_existing_tracker consult the same rule Unit 1 centralizes (selfie::fs::TargetRejection::of, once it exists), and report the entry as tracked-but-invalid rather than as tracked; or move the already-tracked check into the library so there is one answer. Prefer the former if the CLI pre-check is there to avoid loading the service.

Found by the Unit 1 plan reviewer while checking whether the plan's track-refusal claim held for every entry point. It does not.
acceptance_criteria: 'selfie track <file>' does not report a plain success for a spec entry whose recorded target violates the deploy target rule.

title: Evaluate cap-std to make the no-symlink-write invariant structural
description:
selfie's rule is 'never write through a symlink', and today it is enforced per call site: write_file_no_follow passes libc::O_NOFOLLOW via custom_flags (fs/real.rs:137), and every OTHER write site has to remember to use it. selfie-yw7i is the direct evidence that this does not hold -- three sites (service.rs:1481, service.rs:1607, package/repository/yaml.rs:249) still call plain FileSystem::write_file, each guarded only by a path_exists check that FOLLOWS symlinks.

ADR-0003 already had this exact problem called out once: selfie-lkco found it claiming the no-leak rule was structurally enforced when it was call-site discipline. This is the same shape, in the filesystem layer.

cap-std offers capability-based filesystem access -- operations go through an opened Dir handle and resolve relative paths without escaping it, which would make 'this write cannot follow a symlink out of the tree' a property of the API rather than of the author remembering a flag. That is the kind of enforcement .claude/rules/verification.md asks for: 'if it matters, make it a type, a guard in a shared module, or a compile error.'

NOT YET VERIFIED. cap-std is not in the local cargo registry and its API has not been checked against source. Before adopting, confirm against ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/cap-std-*/ (per the verification rule -- do not go on the README):

1. Does its Dir API actually cover selfie's write shapes -- atomic replace via tempfile + persist, explicit mode setting (needed by selfie-5nk), and O_NOFOLLOW on the FINAL component specifically? selfie's targets are absolute user-chosen paths, not paths inside one sandbox root, which is cap-std's primary design case. That mismatch is the main risk and should be settled first.
2. What is the non-unix story? selfie-9gic already notes the non-unix arms of write_file_no_follow and write_file_private are built by no CI job.
3. Dependency weight against the CLAUDE.md guidance to keep the codebase small -- traded against a full rewrite of the fs adapter.

If the answer is no, the fallback is cheaper and should be recorded here: keep the hand-rolled writers but delete FileSystem::write_file from the trait so there is no non-refusing write to reach for, forcing every site through a no-follow constructor. That gets the compile error without the dependency.

Filed at the user's request during the 2026-07-31 target-semantics batch triage, which deliberately scoped selfie-yw7i to reusing the existing O_NOFOLLOW primitive rather than changing the adapter.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded either way, with cap-std's API checked against its source rather than its README: adopt it, or record the delete-write_file alternative as the chosen enforcement mechanism.

title: track has no absoluteness guard, so a relative target resolves against CWD
description:
apply, drift and the secret-bearing path each guard that a dotfile target is absolute after expansion (dotfile_service/service.rs:690, :1234, :1530). TRACK DOES NOT. Both track handlers call only symlink_refusal and path_exists on the expanded target.

Consequence: 'selfie dotfiles track config.toml ./somewhere/x' resolves './somewhere/x' against the PROCESS WORKING DIRECTORY when path_exists stats it, records that relative string in the spec, and succeeds. The entry is then refused by every later apply, since apply does guard absoluteness -- so track once again records something that can never deploy.

Same shape as selfie-ywvs (P1, since fixed): track accepting an entry apply is guaranteed to refuse. That one was about symlinks; this is about relativity. The lesson from ywvs applies -- the cheap moment to tell the user is at track time, when they are standing at the path they named.

Also relevant to selfie-jlum: that bead is about '~user/' passing the TEXTUAL validator and failing the POST-EXPANSION guard. This is the third variant -- a form that passes track's (absent) guard and fails apply's. Three rules about what a target may be, enforced in three places, disagreeing in three different ways.

Found by the selfie-h15 plan author while prototyping collapse_home: a relative target passes through the collapse unchanged, because Path::strip_prefix simply fails, which is correct -- but it surfaced that nothing upstream rejected it.

NOT fixed by selfie-h15, deliberately. Consider doing it after selfie-zv4b lands, which gives selfie one constructor for target paths where a reconciled rule could live.
close_reason: Closed by PR #90 (merge a6c5baa, commit 14daa1a). One target rule, expressed once in crates/selfie/src/fs/target.rs as TargetRejection + deploy_target, enforced at five call sites plus the validator.

title: state_file_path launders the configured state directory unexamined
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:210-212: the configured branch of deploy_state_path returns config.state_directory().join(FILENAME) with NO expansion and no examination of what the configured value is.

Safe today: config/yaml.rs:100-103 runs the configured directory through expand_tilde_only, which does not canonicalize. But nothing enforces that. SelfieConfigBuilder::state_directory and state_directory_mut (crates/cli/src/config.rs:127-128) accept an arbitrary PathBuf, so a caller-supplied value reaches the state path untouched.

This matters more after selfie-zv4b: that unit makes deploy_state_path a CONSTRUCTOR for the TargetPath newtype, whose whole guarantee is that the paths inside were never canonicalized. Whatever is in config becomes a TargetPath unexamined, so the config loader's expand_tilde_only is load-bearing for a guarantee stated somewhere else entirely.

Note also that service.rs:216-219 documents the reason for avoiding expand_path as AVAILABILITY -- 'expand_path canonicalizes, which fails if the directory does not exist yet' -- not as avoiding canonicalization. A maintainer reading only that rationale could reasonably mkdir-then-canonicalize and punch through the guarantee. selfie-zv4b adds a note pinning the security reason; this bead is the structural version.

Fix direction: a validated StateDir type, or a guard in the constructor. Found by the selfie-zv4b plan reviewer.

title: Orphan detection: a changed target abandons the old file with no event
description:
The user-visible half of selfie-13bq that deleting DeployEntry::target leaves undone.

If a package's 'target:' is edited, the old target file stays on disk, no longer managed by selfie and never mentioned again. Drift is computed against the NEW target; the OLD file is silently orphaned.

selfie-13bq resolves by DELETING the unused field rather than building detection on it, because detection cannot be built on today's value -- see selfie-x1 (apply and track record different formats). That closes the bead's either/or criteria honestly but leaves this behavior unchanged.

BLOCKED ON selfie-1xg9. Whoever takes this re-adds a recorded target WITH DECIDED SEMANTICS -- what a recorded target means, in which format, normalized or verbatim -- rather than inheriting the apply-vs-track inconsistency that exists today. That is 1xg9's question and it must be answered first or the detection will be wrong in the same way.

Design questions when it is taken: does selfie report the orphan, remove it, or offer to? An orphan is a file the user may still want. Reporting is the conservative default and needs a PackageEvent.
notes:
TRAP INHERITED FROM selfie-u36f (closed 2026-07-31 as resolved-by-deletion). This bead is the one that would re-add a recorded target to DeployEntry. Before writing that field, decide what the recorded target MEANS -- the raw as-configured string, or the expanded path.

History: the field used to exist and was written in BOTH formats. apply recorded the expanded path; track recorded the raw as-configured string. Nothing read it, so the divergence was invisible, and selfie-13bq's resolution was to delete the field rather than build detection on it (PR #88). If orphan detection re-adds it without settling the question first, a track-then-apply cycle records '~/.config/x' and then compares it against '/home/u/.config/x', and orphan detection reports a spurious 'target moved' on the FIRST APPLY OF EVERY TRACKED FILE.

Note selfie-h15 (PR #89) has since made track record a target relative to home, which is a decision about the same question in the spec -- align with it rather than re-deriving.

title: apply and track record different target strings in the deploy state
description:
DeployEntry::target is written from two paths with two different formats:

  apply  -> the EXPANDED path. service.rs:1053-1057 (&unit.target_path.to_string_lossy()) and 1345-1349 (&target_path.to_string_lossy(), from the expand_target_path at 1229).
  track  -> the RAW as-configured string. service.rs:1723 and 1851, where target_path is the untouched &str function parameter.

So a track-then-apply cycle records '~/.config/x' and then compares it against '/home/u/.config/x'. Any future orphan detection built on this field would report a spurious 'target moved' on the FIRST APPLY OF EVERY TRACKED FILE.

Invisible today because nothing reads the field -- which is selfie-13bq, and is why that bead's resolution is to delete it rather than build detection on it. Verified independently by the selfie-zv4b plan author and its reviewer.

This is the trap under any future orphan-detection work: whoever re-adds a recorded target must decide what it MEANS first, which is selfie-1xg9's question. Filing so the inconsistency is recorded rather than rediscovered when the field comes back.
close_reason:
Resolved by deletion in PR #88 (selfie-13bq). Verified against the tree at 560a4d4: DeployEntry (dotfile_service/state.rs:25-29) now has exactly three fields -- source_checksum, deployed_checksum, deployed_at -- and no target. record_deployment's signature is (source: &str, checksum: &str) (state.rs:65); all four call sites (service.rs:949, 1237, 1614, 1749) pass only those two. There is no recorded target string, in either format, so the divergence this bead describes cannot occur.

The WARNING it carries is still live and has been folded into selfie-pfwk, which is the bead that would re-add the field: whoever re-adds a recorded target must decide what it MEANS before writing it, or apply-records-expanded vs track-records-raw comes straight back and orphan detection reports a spurious 'target moved' on the first apply of every tracked file.

title: Eliminate the capture-descriptor collision class rather than narrowing it
description:
selfie-evf9's fix captures a provider command's stdout on a fixed file descriptor (8) so a login profile's own output cannot be spliced into a deployed credential. A profile that takes descriptor 8 -- 'exec 8>somewhere' -- receives the content instead, and selfie then fails closed with nothing deployed.

That residual is DOCUMENTED, not defended, and deliberately so: the threat model is ACCIDENTAL collision, not an adversarial startup file. A hostile profile already owns the session -- it can read the deployed credential directly or wrap 'op' -- so the capture descriptor is not a security boundary. Filing the elimination option so 'we chose to narrow it' is a recorded decision with a named alternative.

WHY A FIXED DESCRIPTOR RATHER THAN A RANDOM ONE, since that reasoning should survive:
- A fixed number can be NAMED in the documentation and acted on ('selfie captures on descriptor 8; if your profile has taken it, take it back'). 'A descriptor chosen afresh each run' tells the user nothing.
- A collision on a fixed descriptor fails EVERY apply, so the user investigates and the leak stops. A collision on a random one over five values gives four successes in five, so the user retries the odd failure and keeps leaking one credential copy in five, indefinitely.
- 8 specifically: 3 and 4 are the conventional first-free descriptors; flock's convention is 'exec 9>lockfile'. That leaves 5-8, and 8 is furthest from the claimed ones.
- The range is 5-9 and not higher because dash, zsh and ksh all REJECT a redirect to descriptor 10 or above. Measured at 3, 9, 19, 47, 63, 90; only bash and fish accept the high ones, and the outer wrapper is /bin/sh, which is dash on Linux CI.

THE ELIMINATION OPTION, evaluated and deferred: path-based capture through a FIFO in a private 0700 directory. It removes the numbered-descriptor class entirely. Costs measured before deferring:
- reintroduces unsafe (the current design has none) for libc::mkfifo -- though note libc is ALREADY a cfg(unix) dependency of selfie, so no new crate;
- tokio's 'net' feature is not enabled, so a non-blocking FIFO reader needs that feature or a hand-rolled O_NONBLOCK + AsyncFd;
- THE DECIDING COST: the failure mode changes shape. Today a profile that exits before the recipe runs fails in milliseconds. With a read-only FIFO and no writer, the read stalls to command_timeout -- sixty seconds by default, on the credential path, for EVERY user rather than the few with a collision. Trading a rare deterministic failure for a common slow one is the wrong direction for a P1.

ALSO RECORDED, so nobody re-derives it: the cheap hardening -- have the recipe check '[ -p /dev/fd/8 ]' and refuse before writing, so a collision leaks nothing -- DOES NOT WORK. On macOS that test is false even for a genuine pipe, in all five POSIX shells, because /dev/fd entries stat as character devices there. The guard would refuse every run on macOS.

If this is taken up, do it on its own rather than gating the P1 on new failure modes.
notes:
REFRAMING, verified independently on main (2026-07-31). Earlier discussion of this work described the capture descriptor as a NEW credential egress created by the fix. That was wrong, and the reviewer withdrew it after measuring main directly.

A login profile containing 'exec >$HOME/stolen.log' -- redirecting the shell's STDOUT -- already receives the credential verbatim on today's main, with selfie's capture left empty. Measured on all five POSIX shells:

  sh, dash, bash, zsh, ksh:  capture=[]  stolen.log=SECRET1234

And 'exec >somewhere' is a considerably more common idiom than 'exec 8>somewhere'.

So selfie-evf9's wrapper NARROWS a pre-existing class rather than creating one: it moves the content off the shell's stdout -- the descriptor profiles actually redirect -- onto an uncommon numbered one. Measured against the same profile, the wrapped run captures the content intact and stolen.log stays empty.

This bead is therefore about ELIMINATING a residual that predates the fix and was reduced by it, not about closing a hole the fix opened. The distinction matters for prioritisation: nothing regressed.

title: Async profile output survives the stdout fence
description:
Filed as the known residual of selfie-evf9's fix, so the gap is recorded rather than implied.

The stdout fence being built for selfie-evf9 is TIME-ORDERED, not source-separated: it discards bytes written before the command's first byte. A login profile that BACKGROUNDS a writer holding fd 1 therefore splices inside the fence.

Measured with a profile doing '{ sleep 0.2; printf ASYNCCHATTER; } &' -- the shape of async update-checkers and version-manager notices -- in all five POSIX shells tested:

  sh dash bash zsh ksh  ->  EXTRACT[[ASYNCCHATTERs3cr3t-Value-9x7]]

AND IT IS A RACE, not a constant. With the command sleeping 0 / 0.1 / 0.4s the results were clean, clean, spliced. A real 'op read' takes several hundred ms, so the window is wide. That also means it will reproduce intermittently and look like flakiness rather than a bug.

THE FIX IS KNOWN AND WAS MEASURED IMMUNE: file-descriptor separation at spawn time -- child gets fd1 = /dev/null and fd3 = the capture pipe, command output redirected to fd3. A backgrounded child inherits fd1 = /dev/null and never touches the capture fd. Verified immune in all five shells.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN selfie-evf9: it requires one unsafe { pre_exec } dup2 (tokio's Command reaches pre_exec only via as_std_mut), and it loses the discarded-byte count that drives that unit's warning unless fd1 becomes a second counting pipe. No no-unsafe variant was found: doing 'exec 3>&1 1>/dev/null' inside the -c string is too late, because the profile's background children already hold the real pipe.

Note the two mechanisms are COMPLEMENTARY, not alternatives: the fence covers zsh/ksh trailing exit-trap output that fd separation leaks into the capture fd, and fd separation covers the async case the fence cannot see. A complete fix is both.

Found by the selfie-evf9 plan reviewer.
close_reason: Closed

title: sync status drops Warning events, so it cannot relay a drift reason
description:
crates/selfie/src/sync_service/service.rs:910-943, collect_drift_summary matches only DotfileDriftDetected and Completed; every other event hits '_ => {}'. Warning events are discarded.

Consequence after unit A of the target-semantics batch lands: 'selfie dotfiles drift' will name a symlinked target as the reason an entry is stuck, but 'selfie sync status' -- which reads the same stream -- will still say '1 drifted' with no mention of why. And docs/sync.md points the user at drift for the details, so the two commands disagree about how much they know.

That is acceptable as a division of labor (the summary points at the detailed command, and the detailed command answers), which is why unit A scoped it out rather than widening the SyncStatus event shape mid-unit. Filing so the gap is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.

Fix direction: decide whether the drift summary should carry a reason at all. If yes, it needs a field on the summary rather than free text, since the MCP server serializes it -- and adding a Warning passthrough would put arbitrary library text into a structured surface, which .claude/rules/architecture.md argues against. Consider instead a typed 'blocked' count alongside 'drifted'.

Found by the unit-A plan author and confirmed by its reviewer.

title: Record the non-racy option for the lexical containment guard
description:
selfie-86o was resolved by DOCUMENTING that is_within is lexical rather than by fixing it, which is the branch that bead's own either/or criteria permits and that .claude/rules/secrets.md:158 instructs. Filing the alternative so 'we chose to document' is a recorded decision with a named option rather than an absence.

THE OPTION: a FileSystem::read_within(base, relative) port method backed by cap-std or openat2's RESOLVE_BENEATH. Kernel-enforced containment, so it is NOT the check-then-read TOCTOU race that a userspace symlink walk would be -- which matters, because selfie-4m9 spent a P1 closing exactly that class using O_NOFOLLOW, and adding a racy check that ADVERTISES symlink protection would replace an honestly-lexical guard with a dishonestly-strong one.

It is also the correct hexagonal shape: paths.rs imports only std::path and has no FileSystem, which is the whole reason it cannot do this today. A port method threaded through the four is_within call sites (service.rs:1212, service.rs:1535, resolve.rs:100, yaml.rs:142) keeps the boundary intact, and CLAUDE.md's 'lean towards third-party libraries for substantial features' argues for the crate rather than a hand-rolled walk.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED, not rejected: selfie-86o is a P3 whose threat model requires a hostile package repository, and resolve.rs already observes that such a repository can simply run an arbitrary command: -- so this guard is not the security boundary in that scenario. The cost (a new port method, four call sites, a new dependency) is disproportionate to that.

WHEN IT WOULD BECOME WORTH DOING: if selfie ever gains a path where a package repository is not fully trusted -- shared/team package directories, a package registry, or anything fetched rather than authored locally. At that point the lexical guard's documented limit stops being acceptable and this is the fix to reach for.

Verify cap-std / openat2 guarantees against their source and check macOS support before adopting -- .claude/rules/verification.md records three claims about a crate's behavior that were wrong in this repo, one in the unsafe direction. RESOLVE_BENEATH is Linux-specific; cap-std's macOS story needs checking.

Raised by the unit-A plan reviewer.
notes: CORRECTION (2026-07-31): the note above says cap-std and openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH are both 'kernel-enforced'. That is only true of openat2, which is Linux-only. cap-std is kernel-enforced WHERE openat2 is available; elsewhere -- macOS included -- it emulates resolution in userspace, so the race-freedom property does not carry over. Since this project's developer is on macOS and CI is Ubuntu, a cap-std-based fix would be TOCTOU-free in CI and racy locally, which is the worst configuration for noticing. Verify against cap-std's source before adopting, and if the guarantee matters, say 'kernel-enforced on Linux' rather than 'kernel-enforced'.

title: Reconsider try_send vs send().await for streamed chunks once the pump is async
description:
Filed as input to selfie-qd3r / selfie-z6cr, not as a duplicate of them.

The reason execute_streaming uses a non-blocking try_send (and therefore drops chunks) is structural: handle_chunked_read_result_streaming is a SYNC fn and cannot .await a send. Commit 9891f05 replaced an earlier blocking send().await for that reason, and CommandError::Callback -- the variant that used to report the drop -- was orphaned and later deleted in PR #79.

selfie-6bav's rewrite makes the pump an async block under an outer deadline, which removes that structural constraint. The 6bav plan reviewer measured send().await in the new shape:

  RV-1a send().await: total=8 received=4 completed=true in 11.2ms

No hang, every chunk delivered, bounded by the outer timeout. So the objection that killed the blocking send in 9891f05 -- that it can stall the output pump forever on a slow consumer -- no longer applies once the pump itself is bounded.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED: the reviewer did not test it under the 8000-chunk fixture with a 50ms-per-item consumer, which by construction would take ~400s. So the open question is the resulting SLOWDOWN, not the safety. A command producing a lot of output with a slow event sink would now be throttled by the sink rather than dropping output -- which is arguably correct, and arguably a regression in perceived responsiveness.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR qd3r: that bead's 'cheapest first' option is a drop counter plus an end-of-stream event. That was the right call while send().await could hang. It may no longer be cheapest once 6bav lands -- 'stop dropping' may be simpler than 'count the drops and report them', and it needs no new PackageEvent variant. Decide between them with the measurement, after 6bav.

title: A timed-out command leaks grandchildren that inherited its pipes
description:
When a command times out or is cancelled, ShellCommandRunner calls child.kill(). That kills only the DIRECT child. A grandchild the child spawned -- 'sh -c "daemon &"' is the ordinary shape -- survives.

MEASURED (U2's prototype, experiment E3b): after the timeout fired,
  direct child = <gone>
  grandchild sleep still running? true

So selfie can leave orphaned processes behind on every timed-out or cancelled command. They keep whatever file descriptors they inherited, including the pipes selfie was reading.

DISTINCT FROM selfie-b7mv, which is about selfie itself HANGING because a grandchild holds the pipe open past the deadline. That one closes for free under selfie-6bav's rewrite (reads and wait become one future under one deadline; measured Err(Timeout) at 2.0029s versus an 8.0089s unbounded hang today). THIS bead is the other half: even once selfie stops waiting, the grandchild is still running.

FIX DIRECTION: process-group management, so a kill reaches the whole tree. The candidate is process-wrap (watchexec org) -- U2's author checked its health rather than its reputation: version 9.1.0, published 2026-03-08, ~4.19M recent downloads. command-group is superseded (last release 2023-11-18).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE IN selfie-6bav. Adopting a new dependency to fix an unfiled issue, inside a unit whose stated job is REMOVING hand-rolled code, would be exactly the silent scope absorption that unit was told to avoid. Filed so the decision is made on its own merits.

Verify process-wrap's actual guarantees on macOS AND Linux against its source before adopting -- .claude/rules/verification.md records three claims about a crate's behavior that were wrong here, one in the unsafe direction.

title: run_git's success path returns git stdout raw while its failure path is now type-enforced
description:
After selfie-cvpm, crates/selfie/src/git/adapter.rs's FAILURE path is compiler-enforced: GitSyncError::OperationFailed's fields are a GitMessage newtype whose only constructors redact-then-bound, so no struct-variant literal anywhere can put raw text in.

The SUCCESS path at adapter.rs:89 is not:

  Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())

Raw, unbounded, unredacted.

NOT A LEAK TODAY, verified: no current call site can echo a URL. 'remote' lists names only; rev-parse, ls-files --deleted, diff --name-status and rev-list --count cannot carry one.

The problem is the asymmetry. One half of the same function is enforced by the type system and the other half is convention, which makes the guarantee look more general than it is. A future run_git(root, &['config', '--get', 'remote.origin.url']) or ['remote', '-v'] -- both ordinary things to add -- puts a credential straight into a String return value with nothing stopping it, and the next reader has every reason to assume run_git is safe because its error path visibly is.

This is the same argument selfie-cvpm's author used to justify typing the 'operation' field even though it was not an exposure at the time: the cost is small, and the alternative is a puzzle every future reader has to re-solve.

Fix direction: return GitMessage (or a sibling type) from run_git's success path too, or document at the function why the two halves differ. Prefer the type.

Found by the selfie-cvpm final code reviewer (U4 of the command-execution batch).

title: stop_on_error governs only secret-resolution failures, which is undocumented
description:
In dotfile_service/service.rs's handle_apply, a repository-file failure always continues to the next entry, while a secret-resolution failure honors stop_on_error. The code comments this explicitly around service.rs:1046 -- so it is deliberate, not an oversight.

But stop_on_error is a user-facing config key documented as an execution setting (see .claude/rules/domain.md, docs/configuration.md), and nothing tells the user it applies to only one class of dotfile failure. Someone who sets stop_on_error: true expecting apply to halt on the first problem gets that behavior for provider/vars entries and silently does not for plain source-file entries.

Either behavior is defensible. The gap is that the config key claims more than it does, which is the same shape as the invariant-you-state-versus-invariant-you-enforce rule in .claude/rules/verification.md.

Fix direction: decide whether the asymmetry is intended. If yes, document it in docs/configuration.md and docs/package-files.md and name the reasoning. If no, make repo-file failures honor the flag too. Do not resolve it by making the doc vaguer.

Found by the selfie-w8gd/selfie-fbwo plan reviewer (U3 of the command-execution batch).

title: login_shell assumes $SHELL accepts -l -c
description:
ShellCommandRunner::login_shell (commands/shell.rs:77-92) reads $SHELL and build_command (:98-102) invokes it as '<shell> -l -c <command>'.

That contract is not universal. fish honors both -l and -c. nushell wants --login rather than -l. Other shells a user may legitimately set as $SHELL (elvish, xonsh, oil) vary. When the flags are not understood the failure is opaque -- the shell errors on its own argument parsing, so the diagnostic is about a flag the user never wrote, for a command they did write.

Pre-existing for install/check/audit and for the MCP server. selfie-w8gd extends it to CLI apply, so a user with an exotic $SHELL who could previously run 'selfie apply' under /bin/sh may find it stops working -- the fix for one bug surfacing this one.

There is a fallback but it does not cover this: login_shell falls back to default_shell() only when $SHELL is UNSET, not when it is set to something that rejects -l -c.

Fix direction: a small known-shell table mapping the login flag per shell basename (fish/bash/zsh/sh -> -l, nu -> --login), falling back to no login flag rather than to an unsupported one, so an unknown shell degrades to a working non-login invocation instead of failing. Alternatively detect the failure and re-run without -l once, though that doubles the command on the credential path and is worse.

Found by the selfie-w8gd/selfie-fbwo plan reviewer (U3 of the command-execution batch).

title: Nothing observes the reader-task abort on run_buffered's early-return arms
description:
run_buffered's timeout, cancellation and wait-failure arms call stdout_handle.abort() / stderr_handle.abort() before returning. Removing BOTH calls fails no test in the workspace -- confirmed by mutation M8 during selfie-ql8m (PR for U1 of the command-execution batch), run one-per-invocation in an isolated git archive copy.

The behavior is correct and should stay: dropping a JoinHandle merely detaches the task, so without the abort a detached reader keeps buffering a killed command's output after the caller has given up -- and on the credential path that means it keeps buffering credential bytes nobody will ever read. child.kill() only kills the direct child, so where a grandchild holds the pipe (see selfie-b7mv) the detached reader can live indefinitely.

But it is currently unenforced. A future edit can delete both aborts and every gate stays green.

Reported rather than papered over: per .claude/rules/testing.md, 'mutations that pass are informative' and the author declined to invent an observation just to make the mutation bite. Filing so the gap is tracked rather than lost.

Fix direction: find an observation that is honest rather than contrived -- e.g. assert the reader task is finished (JoinHandle::is_finished) shortly after a timeout return, or restructure so the abort is not separable from the return. If no honest observation exists, closing this as won't-fix with that reasoning recorded is a legitimate outcome.

Note the interaction with selfie-b7mv: whoever bounds the post-wait join may make this observable as a side effect.

title: push's rejection remap discards the original error wholesale
description:
crates/selfie/src/git/adapter.rs:458-466. On a failed push, the code string-matches the message for 'rejected' and substitutes a fixed diagnosis:

  'Remote has new commits. Run selfie sync pull first.'

The original error is discarded, not wrapped. A push can be rejected for reasons that are not a non-fast-forward -- a pre-receive hook rejecting the push, a protected-branch policy, a quota or file-size limit, a permission failure that git words as a rejection. All of them get told to run 'selfie sync pull', which will not help and sends the user down the wrong path with the actual reason gone.

Fix direction: keep the specific guidance for the non-fast-forward case but narrow the match, and preserve the original message either way rather than replacing it. Note the interaction with selfie-cvpm: after that lands the message is redacted and bounded, so preserving it is safe to surface -- but bounding could in principle elide the marker this match depends on when stderr is large, which is a second reason not to hinge the whole diagnosis on a substring.

Found by the selfie-cvpm plan reviewer (U4 of the command-execution batch).

title: SyncError::GitError is an untyped free-text carrier reaching MCP JSON
description:
crates/selfie/src/sync_service/port.rs:27 defines SyncError::GitError(String) -- an untyped free-text field that reaches an AI assistant's transcript directly via crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:757-765, which builds json!({"status":"error","message": e.to_string()}) without going through the event stream.

It is safe today only because its sole source is a GitSyncError's Display. Once selfie-cvpm lands and GitSyncError's fields are a redacting type, that safety becomes a CONVENTION rather than a type: SyncError::GitError still accepts any String, so a future arm that formats something else into it reintroduces the exposure with nothing to stop it.

This is the shape .claude/rules/verification.md names: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces.' selfie-cvpm fixes the git side by construction; this is the adjacent hop that stays convention-only.

Fix direction: give SyncError::GitError the same redacting/bounded type selfie-cvpm introduces, so the guarantee survives the hop. Cheap once that type exists -- file now so it is not lost when cvpm closes.

Depends on selfie-cvpm landing first. Found by the selfie-cvpm plan reviewer.

title: MCP sync tools cannot be tested end to end because the service type is fixed
description:
crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:39 fixes the concrete type:

  type ConcreteSyncService = SyncServiceImpl<GixGitAdapter, ConcreteDotfileService>;

So no test can inject a mock GitSyncProvider and assert on the actual JSON that selfie_sync_push / selfie_sync_pull / selfie_sync_status return. Tests can only reach one layer short of the real boundary -- they assert on the string event_collector.rs:34 serializes, not on the tool result an AI assistant actually receives.

This matters for the sync path specifically because that path has TWO distinct AI-facing exits with different shapes:
  1. the event stream -> event_collector.rs:33-35 -> {"status":"failure","error":...}
  2. server.rs:757-765 -> {"status":"error","message":...}  (bypasses the event stream entirely)
A test that covers only the first proves nothing about the second, and nothing today covers either at the tool boundary.

Fix direction: make the sync tool handlers generic over the service trait the way the package tools are, so a mock can be injected -- or add a seam that lets a test drive the tool handler with a substituted service. Compare how the package tools are structured; the boundary rule in .claude/rules/architecture.md says both adapters should consume the same trait.

Found by the selfie-cvpm plan author (U4 of the command-execution batch) while mapping every egress from git output to an AI transcript.

title: A streaming read failure names neither the command nor the directory
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:485-490. handle_chunked_read_result_streaming builds its failure as:

  CommandError::IoError {
      command: "streaming command".to_string(),
      working_directory: std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(...),
      ...
  }

Two defects in one constructor. The command field is a hardcoded literal rather than the command that actually failed. And working_directory re-reads the process's current directory instead of the recorded working_directory -- which is precisely the substitution execute_in_dir exists to avoid, since run_buffered:127-132 deliberately reports 'the directory the command actually ran in, not selfie's own, so a failure names the place the user configured.'

Consequence: a read failure during 'selfie package install' produces a diagnostic that identifies neither what ran nor where. Diagnostics only -- no incorrect behavior and no egress -- but it defeats the context the surrounding code goes out of its way to preserve.

Found by the selfie-ql8m plan author and confirmed by its reviewer (U1 of the command-execution batch); verified by the lead.

title: execute_streaming's exit_status.unwrap() is guarded only by a comment
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:437: status: exit_status.unwrap(), guarded by a // SAFETY: comment asserting that the loop only exits when process_done is true, which is only set after exit_status is assigned Some(status).

The invariant is real today. Nothing enforces it. This is the exact shape .claude/rules/verification.md names: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces... If it matters, make it a type, a guard in a shared module, or a compile error.' A future break added to that loop for any reason turns this into a panic in the library -- and the selfie library panicking takes down whichever adapter is hosting it, CLI or MCP server.

Fix direction: restructure so the status cannot be absent by construction -- e.g. have the loop return the status rather than assign into an Option the code later unwraps, so the type carries the invariant instead of the comment.

Found by the selfie-ql8m plan reviewer (U1 of the command-execution batch); verified by the lead.
notes: LIKELY SUBSUMED by selfie-6bav (2026-07-30). This unwrap exists only because execute_streaming's hand-rolled loop needs a process_done/exit_status state machine. A FramedRead/Stream rewrite has no such Option to unwrap, so the invariant disappears rather than being enforced. Verify it is actually gone before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: BoundedText's lossy decode defeats the byte-rendering leak scan
description:
Blocked on PR #78 (selfie-iuhz) landing; not a change to that PR.

selfie-gwhw taught the leak scan to look for a credential in BOTH renderings: as text, and as a Debug of Vec<u8> ([115, 51, 99, ...]). That closed the blind spot where std::process::Output's Debug switches to a byte array for non-UTF-8 content.

BoundedText::bound() decodes with String::from_utf8_lossy. Every invalid byte becomes U+FFFD. So on the stderr path, binary content reaching an event renders as replacement characters that match NEITHER needle:
  - the byte needle never matches, because the value is no longer bytes
  - the text needle matches only if the secret's readable prefix survives normalization at 12 characters

The two changes are individually correct and jointly reopen a narrow hole on one path. gwhw's scan assumes binary content stays binary; BoundedText makes it lossy text first.

Scope is narrow — it needs a secret that is BOTH non-UTF-8 AND has a short readable prefix, on the stderr path specifically. Overlaps selfie-i8qh (the same lossy blind spot, described generally); this bead is the concrete instance created by BoundedText. Consider closing them together.

Possible fix: a third needle derived from the lossy decoding of the secret, so whatever from_utf8_lossy would produce is also scanned for.

Found by selfie-gwhw's independent final reviewer, looking forward at #78 rather than at the code in front of it.
acceptance_criteria: A non-UTF-8 credential reaching stderr is caught by the leak scan in its lossily-decoded form.

title: resolve.rs copies the whole provider output a second time
description:
resolve.rs:268 calls output.stdout().to_vec() while 'output' is still live, so the provider's entire stdout exists twice at peak — roughly 2x for a dotfile whose content comes from a command.

The size cap is 8 MiB, so worst case is ~16 MiB transient rather than anything unbounded. Not urgent. But this is the credential-bearing path (command-sourced dotfile content), and a second copy is a second buffer that has to be reasoned about for zeroization if this project ever goes there.

Fix is likely to consume 'output' rather than borrow-then-copy. Check whether CommandOutput exposes an owning accessor; if not, adding one is the change.

Found by selfie-3hap's author while reading the surrounding code. Note selfie-ql8m also concerns resolve.rs:268 — that one is about TRUNCATED output being written past the cap, which is the more serious defect at the same line. Fix ql8m first; this may fall out of it.
acceptance_criteria: Provider output is not duplicated at peak.
close_reason: Closed

title: secrets.md does not load for the files that implement its leak-scanning rule
description:
.claude/rules/secrets.md's paths: frontmatter matches none of the files that implement the leak-scanning rule the file prescribes.

Not matched:
  crates/test-common/src/secrets.rs   the scanner itself (assert_secret_free)
  crates/selfie/tests/**              every leak-regression test that calls it

Matched today: crates/selfie/src/** (parts), three CLI files, crates/mcp-server/src/**.

So a session editing the scanner — or writing a new leak test — does not get the rule that governs it auto-loaded. That is the population most likely to weaken the scan by accident, and the least likely to have the rule in context.

This is not hypothetical for this file specifically: selfie-gwhw exists because the rule said 'scan for the secret literal', an instruction that was wrong once Vec<u8> Debug entered the picture, and nobody editing the tests had the rule in front of them to notice.

Scored 75 by selfie-gwhw's own code review — below its 80 fix-threshold, so deliberately left. Cheap to fix: add the two paths. Worth a moment's thought about whether crates/selfie/tests/** is too broad, since it would load the secrets rule for every integration test in the crate.

Note selfie-gwhw and selfie-iuhz both edit this file's frontmatter for other reasons; whoever takes this should land after both.
acceptance_criteria: Editing the leak scanner or a leak-regression test loads .claude/rules/secrets.md.
notes:
COORDINATION NOTE (2026-07-30): there are now THREE in-flight changes to .claude/rules/secrets.md's paths: frontmatter, not two.

This bead's description already gates it on selfie-gwhw and selfie-iuhz. Add a third: selfie-cvpm (U4 of the command-execution batch) adds crates/selfie/src/git/**/*.rs and crates/selfie/src/sync_service/**/*.rs -- confirmed by its plan reviewer to be genuinely unmatched by the current paths: list, so the addition is correct rather than cargo-culted.

No glob conflict between them: gwhw/iuhz add crates/test-common/src/secrets.rs and crates/selfie/tests/**, cvpm adds git/** and sync_service/**. But they edit the same frontmatter block, so expect a textual merge conflict and land this one last.

title: Nothing scans stdout or stderr for leaked secrets
description:
selfie's leak-regression tests cover two egress channels: the PackageEvent stream and the tracing subscriber. Direct writes to the process's stdout and stderr are scanned by nothing.

A stray println!, eprintln!, or dbg! on the resolve path would print a credential and fail no test in the repo. dbg! is the likeliest — it is a debugging reflex, it goes to stderr, and it uses {:?}, which on ResolvedContent prints '<N bytes>' but on a raw &[u8] or a String prints the content.

The library is not supposed to write to stdout/stderr at all (.claude/rules/architecture.md), so a lint may fit better than a test: deny println!/eprintln!/dbg! in crates/selfie/src outside #[cfg(test)]. That enforces the existing boundary rule and closes this as a side effect. clippy has print_stdout, print_stderr and dbg_macro lints, all allow-by-default.

Decide whether this is a gap to close or a documented boundary of what the leak tests cover — .claude/rules/secrets.md currently implies the event stream and tracing are the whole net.

Found while implementing selfie-gwhw.
acceptance_criteria: Either direct stdout/stderr writes from the library are prevented, or the leak tests' coverage boundary is documented.

title: No leak test exercises a non-UTF-8 credential end to end
description:
selfie-gwhw unit-tests the leak helper against non-UTF-8 secrets, but no integration fixture drives one through a real apply. Every end-to-end leak test uses an ASCII secret.

That matters because non-UTF-8 is the case where the byte rendering is the ONLY rendering: std::process::Output's Debug prints stdout as text when valid UTF-8 and as a byte array otherwise, so an ASCII credential and a binary one take different paths through the same code. The path that only binary content reaches has no end-to-end coverage.

selfie supports binary dotfile content deliberately — resolve.rs tests provider_output_is_byte_exact_including_non_utf8 (b"\x00\xff\xfe\x0a") and a_non_utf8_binding_survives_into_the_rendered_output (b"k: \xff\xfe").

Fix: one integration fixture in crates/selfie/tests/dotfile_service_tests.rs using a non-UTF-8 provider secret, asserting no leak, with a positive control proving the run produced it. Note selfie-i8qh first — a from_utf8_lossy rendering would escape the scan, so the fixture should be written after that is settled or it may pass for the wrong reason.

Found while implementing selfie-gwhw.
acceptance_criteria: An end-to-end leak test drives a non-UTF-8 credential through apply, with a working positive control.

title: from_utf8_lossy of a non-UTF-8 credential matches neither leak-scan needle
description:
selfie-gwhw's assert_secret_free scans two renderings: the secret as text, and its Debug-of-bytes form. A third rendering escapes both.

String::from_utf8_lossy of non-UTF-8 content replaces each invalid byte with U+FFFD. The result is neither the original text (the bytes are gone) nor the byte-array Debug (it is a string). A leak that formats a binary credential that way matches no needle.

This is the case selfie-gwhw leads with as its urgency argument: std::process::Output's Debug switches to a byte array for non-UTF-8 stdout, and selfie explicitly supports binary dotfile content (resolve.rs tests b"\x00\xff\xfe" and b"k: \xff\xfe"). So the scenario that motivated making the scan byte-aware is the one the byte-awareness does not cover — documented in the helper's limitations list rather than closed.

Closing it means a third needle: the lossy-decoded form of the secret, derived inside the helper alongside the other two so the choice is not re-made per call site.

Worth weighing first: how reachable is it? A leak would have to route binary content through from_utf8_lossy specifically, rather than Display or Debug. resolve.rs:265 does exactly that on the error branch, so it is not hypothetical.

Found while implementing selfie-gwhw.
acceptance_criteria: A leak of a non-UTF-8 secret rendered through from_utf8_lossy fails the leak-regression tests.
notes:
THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION IS WRONG AND OVERSTATES THE HOLE. Retracted by the selfie-gwhw author after its own code review scored this as the round's highest-confidence finding (100/100), and reproduced by probe.

'Matches neither needle' is false. A binary secret with a long readable prefix IS caught, as text — the module's own test demonstrates it.

ACCURATE PROPERTY: a lossy rendering is uncovered by the BYTE needle always, and by the TEXT needle only when the secret's readable prefix does not survive normalization at 12 characters. Where the prefix does survive, the lossy rendering is normally caught.

Two edges narrow it further, both found by probe rather than reasoning:
  - The gate is the SQUEEZED length, not the valid-UTF-8 prefix length. b"a b c d e f g " + [0xff,0xfe,0x00] has valid_up_to = 14, above the 12-character window, and still escapes both needles.
  - squeeze also deletes literal backslash-n / backslash-r / backslash-t PAIRS, so a 13-non-whitespace-character prefix can still produce no needle.

The hole is real but narrower than filed, and selfie-gwhw now documents it and pins BOTH sides with tests — including a_lossy_rendering_escapes_a_whitespace_heavy_readable_prefix, which asserts the escaping case rather than claiming coverage. So this is no longer an undocumented gap; it is a documented, tested boundary.

Downgraded P2 to P3 accordingly. Closing it means a third needle for the lossy-decoded form; weigh that against the fact that the escape now requires a whitespace-heavy readable prefix specifically.

title: Leak tests have no byte-aware positive control (assert_secret_present)
description:
selfie-gwhw makes the NEGATIVE leak assertion byte-aware: assert_secret_free scans for both the text rendering and the Debug-of-bytes rendering of a secret. The POSITIVE controls beside it were left literal-only, deliberately, because converting them would silently invert their meaning.

Two sites:
  crates/selfie/tests/command_output_egress_tests.rs:84   assert ... contains(SECRET)
  crates/selfie/tests/dotfile_service_tests.rs:2656

These are the assertions that prove a leak test is not passing vacuously — that the run genuinely produced the secret through its acknowledged channel. They scan for the literal only. If an acknowledged channel ever renders the secret as bytes rather than text, the control silently stops observing anything and the negative assertion beside it becomes unfalsifiable — which is the exact failure .claude/rules/testing.md warns about, arriving through the control rather than the test.
