Arguments against: YAML's implicit type coercion surprises (the Norway problem); significant whitespace; comments are lost on programmatic rewrite, which matters because selfie edits package files via spec create/update and the MCP server; no schema enforcement without extra tooling.

Alternatives worth weighing: TOML (simpler, no significant whitespace, comment-preserving via toml_edit, weaker for deep nesting); KDL (good ergonomics, small ecosystem); Starlark/Dhall/Nickel (only justified if package files ever need logic, which is contrary to the declarative plus shell-out philosophy).

Cost of switching is broad rather than deep: every command, the MCP server, validation, span reporting, docs, and all existing package files. No backward compatibility is required pre-release.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded as an ADR, either affirming YAML with reasons or selecting a replacement with a migration outline.
notes: Raised while designing selfie-doh, when templating prompted the question of format fit. Deliberately kept separate: nothing in the dotfile templating design depends on the answer, and deciding it as a side effect of a feature would be the wrong way to settle it.

title: dotfiles list/track/remove should reflect per-environment dotfiles
description: The per-environment dotfiles core (34558ef) wired apply + drift to the effective set, but 'dotfiles list' (CLI list.rs, MCP server.rs) and the track/remove readers still use package.dotfiles() (shared only), so environment-specific dotfiles do not appear in listings and are not considered by remove's cleanup/track's display. Decide list semantics (effective set for current env, or list all with an environment label) and update accordingly. Follow-up to per-environment dotfiles core.
close_reason: list (CLI+MCP), track, and remove now use Package::dotfiles_with_scope() to reflect environment-specific dotfiles; CLI Environment column + MCP environment field; TDD.

title: Richer dotfile conflict resolution (backup-then-overwrite, merge) beyond accept/skip
description: On an apply conflict (existing target differs from selfie's source and may be user-authored), selfie currently offers accept (overwrite) or skip, and shows a unified diff. Enhancement: offer safer/richer resolution options, e.g. back up the existing target (.bak) before overwriting, open a merge tool / 3-way merge, or apply per-hunk. The core safety guarantee (never overwrite divergent content without consent) already holds and is recorded in ADR-0001 (Overwrite safety); this is about better ergonomics when a conflict does occur. The diff is already produced; merging is the hard part. Raised 2026-07-23 during ADR-0001 review.

title: selfie requires a config file to exist even when all settings are passed via CLI flags
description: During fresh-machine recovery proof (2026-07-23): running 'selfie apply' with HOME pointed at a clean dir failed with 'No configuration file found in locations: <HOME>/.config/selfie' even though --package-directory, --environment, and --state-directory were all supplied on the CLI. selfie should be able to run fully from CLI flags (and/or env vars) with no config file present — important for fresh-machine bootstrap, scripted/bulk operations, CI, containers, and ephemeral AI-driven runs. Workaround today: create ~/.config/selfie/config.yml first. Consider: treat missing config file as empty-config when required values come from flags, or add a way to point at an explicit config path.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #112

title: CLI: add non-interactive way to attach a dotfile to an existing package (parity with MCP selfie_dotfiles_add)
description: 'selfie track <file>' is fully interactive (prompts existing-package vs standalone) with no flags to bypass it, so it can't be scripted or used in automation/bulk migration. The MCP server already has a non-interactive 'selfie_dotfiles_add' (add file to an existing package's dotfiles section). Add a CLI equivalent, e.g. 'selfie dotfiles add <file> --package <name>' or non-interactive flags on 'track'. Surfaced 2026-07-23 while migrating bat off YADM. Lower priority since the AI/MCP path is the primary driver, but needed for scriptable bulk migration of ~170 dotfiles.

title: Audit selfie for other silent-failure paths; make them warn or error
description: Follow-up to the config-unknown-keys bug. Sweep the codebase for places where selfie swallows errors or degrades silently (e.g. best-effort steps that skip without notice, ignored parse results, dropped fields). Each should surface a warning/error via PackageEvent so the user is never surprised. Establishes 'no silent failures' as a selfie design value. Reference: strategic-direction memory + docs runbook 2026-07-23.

title: Implement environment name completer
description: Create a custom completer for the --environment/-e global flag that suggests known environment names. These can be extracted by scanning package files for their environment keys. This is lower priority than package name completion but still useful — users often forget exact environment labels.

title: Consider suppressing redundant success message on completion
description: After commands like `selfie package status`, the default Completed event handler prints a line like `✓ Package 'foo' status checked successfully (2/2 steps)`. This is redundant when the command already displayed its results (e.g., the status table). Consider suppressing or shortening this message for commands where the output itself implies success.
close_reason: Suppressed redundant success messages in status, info, audit, and check commands

title: Expand SelfieConfig validation
description: Current config validation only checks environment (non-empty) and package_directory (non-empty, absolute). Add validation for dotfiles_directory and state_directory (absolute path when set), and validate that command_timeout is reasonable (warn if >600s). Also consider validating that package_directory and dotfiles_directory exist on disk (as warnings, not errors).
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove custom validation code after garde adoption
description: Once garde handles validation via derive macros, remove: validate.rs hand-written validators, ValidationIssue/ValidationIssues types (replaced by garde's error types), the extra_fields serde(flatten) hack for unknown field detection (serde-saphyr + garde handles this natively). This is cleanup after the garde migration.
close_reason: Superseded — garde not being adopted, so there's no custom validation code to remove after adoption.

title: Improve CI workflow
description:
The CI workflow needs several improvements:
1. (DONE) Double-run fixed — push: now filtered to main only.
2. Add clippy job — it's in the pre-commit checklist but not in CI.
3. The format job auto-commits and pushes on failure, which triggers another CI run. Should just fail instead (let developers fix locally).
4. Consider adding cargo cache for faster builds.
5. Consider adding a Rust toolchain cache.
close_reason: Fixed in c31bf34. Added clippy, rust-cache, removed auto-push, cleaned up job names and deps.

title: Surface drift-check failures in sync status
description: collect_drift_summary() ignores OperationResult::Failure from the drift stream, causing sync status to report empty/zero drift values and overall success when drift checking actually failed. Should surface the failure as a warning event. Copilot PR #35 comment 2978720110.
close_reason: Fixed: collect_drift_summary now captures OperationResult::Failure and emits a warning event

title: Convert fast_forward to native gix ref update + checkout
description: fast_forward currently shells out to git merge --ff-only. Convert to native gix: verify ancestor relationship, update ref, then checkout working tree via gix-worktree-state. Requires adding worktree-state feature to gix dependency. User accepts larger binary for consistency.

title: Convert push/fetch to native gix transport
description: push and fetch currently shell out to git CLI for SSH/credential integration. Convert to gix's blocking-network-client transport. Requires adding the blocking-network-client feature to gix dependency. User accepts larger binary for consistency. May need to handle SSH agent integration via gix-transport.
notes: Assessment (2026-03-24, gix 0.81.0): Push is still incomplete in gix 0.81.0 — thin pack creation works but actual push protocol is not implemented. Fetch works with blocking-network-client feature but adds binary size and complexity for marginal benefit over reliable git CLI shell-out. Recommend revisiting when gix push matures (track gitoxide releases). The gix upgrade from 0.72→0.81 was done separately.

title: Convert remaining run_git calls to native gix
description: stage_files and commit are now pure gix. Remaining run_git calls for local ops that should be converted: discover_repo (branch via rev-parse, remote name), repo_status (ls-files --deleted), diff_commits (diff --name-status), ahead_behind_counts (rev-list). Network ops (push, fetch) and fast_forward (merge --ff-only) are fine as shell-outs.

title: Update docs for sync commands
description: Update README.md status section, docs/configuration.md with sync commands. Add docs/sync.md with usage examples for status/push/pull, flag reference, conventional commit format explanation, and MCP tool descriptions.
close_reason: Added docs/sync.md with complete sync guide. Updated README.md status section and navigation. dprint formatted.

title: Add requires_sudo flag per environment in package specs
description: Allow package specs to declare requires_sudo: true per environment, so selfie can warn or prompt before running commands that need elevated privileges. Nice UX touch for packages that need sudo on some environments but not others. Found in selfie2 old repo.

title: Support multiple package directories in config
description: Allow configuring multiple package_directory paths (e.g., a personal directory and a shared team directory). Packages from all directories would be discovered and available. Current config only supports a single package_directory. Found in selfie-v1, selfie2, and investigation-selfie old repos.

title: Auto-detect installation source from executable path
description: Enhance the audit system with a fallback heuristic that detects how a package was installed by examining its executable path. For example: /opt/homebrew/bin/ → brew, ~/.cargo/bin/ → cargo, /usr/local/bin/ → manual/unknown. This would provide audit info even when no explicit audit command is defined in the package spec. Found in narcissist and investigation-selfie old repos.

title: Add search command to find packages by keyword
description: Add a 'search' or 'spec search' command that searches package files by name, description, tags, or other metadata. Useful once the user has many packages defined. Found in selfie2 spec (was planned but not implemented).
close_reason: Implemented spec search command with case-insensitive substring matching on name and description

title: Add per-environment configs to package specs
description: Currently configs is a top-level field that applies across all environments. Add support for per-environment config entries so users can deploy different config files per environment (e.g. ~/.gitconfig-personal on personal machines, ~/.gitconfig-work on work machines). Design should follow whatever pattern the environment inheritance feature establishes, rather than inventing a separate filtering mechanism. Blocked by environment inheritance design.

title: Remove version field from package YAML schema
description: The version field in package definitions is vestigial — selfie never compares versions, there's no upgrade logic, and git tracks definition history better than a hand-bumped semver. Remove it entirely: drop from Package struct, remove from validation, stop emitting in spec create, update parser to ignore if present (don't break existing files). If we later need schema versioning (post-release), add a schema_version or selfie_min_version field at that point.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #32

title: Investigate flattening CLI command structure
description: Evaluate moving runtime package commands to top-level: 'selfie install X' instead of 'selfie package install X'. Now that groups are off the table (replaced by recommends), the 'package' namespace adds typing without value for the hot-path commands (install, check, audit). Questions to answer: (1) What happens to 'selfie list' ambiguity (specs vs packages)? (2) Should 'selfie package list' and 'selfie spec list' stay namespaced? (3) Keep 'selfie package X' as aliases during transition or break cleanly? (4) How does this affect MCP server tool naming? (5) Does 'selfie apply' already set the precedent for top-level verbs?

title: Investigate flattening CLI command structure (selfie install vs selfie package install)
description:
Now that 'selfie group' commands are off the table (replaced by recommends), the 'selfie package' namespace may be unnecessary overhead for the most common commands. Investigate promoting runtime verbs to top-level:

- selfie install ripgrep (instead of selfie package install ripgrep)
- selfie check ripgrep
- selfie audit ripgrep
- selfie apply ripgrep (already top-level)

Open questions to resolve:
- What happens to 'selfie list'? Ambiguous between spec list and package list. Maybe defaults to package list with status?
- Should 'selfie package install' remain as an alias for backward compat, or break it (pre-1.0)?
- Does the spec subcommand stay as-is? (Probably yes — definition management is less frequent)
- How does this affect the MCP server tool naming?
- Impact on shell completions and help text organization
- Does 'selfie status' make sense as top-level too?

This is an investigation ticket — answer the questions, then decide whether to proceed.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-gyb

title: Rename package config deployment to 'dotfile' terminology
description:
The word 'config' is overloaded in the codebase: SelfieConfig (selfie's settings), ConfigEntry/ConfigService (package file deployment), and the 'selfie config' CLI subcommand. Rename the package config deployment layer to use 'dotfile' instead.

Scope of changes:
- YAML schema: configs: → dotfiles:, configs_directory → dotfiles_directory in selfie config
- Types: ConfigEntry → DotfileEntry, ConfigService → DotfileService, ConfigServiceImpl → DotfileServiceImpl
- Module: config_service/ → dotfile_service/ (or dotfile/)
- Events: ConfigDeploying → DotfileDeploying, ConfigDeployed → DotfileDeployed, etc.
- CLI: apply command internals (the 'selfie apply' command name stays the same)
- MCP server: tool names and descriptions that reference 'config' in the deployment sense
- Docs: package-files.md, configuration.md, README examples
- Tests: all config_service_tests

This is a pure rename refactor with no behavior changes. Should be done as a focused PR separate from feature work.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-ybf

title: Track and display last check/install timestamps
description:
Persist timestamps for when each package was last checked or installed, and display this in info/list output. Helps users identify stale packages that haven't been verified in a while.

This is a larger feature because selfie currently has no persistent state beyond the package YAML files and config. It requires a new storage mechanism for run history.

Implementation considerations:
- Need a state/history store — likely a simple JSON or SQLite file in the selfie config directory (~/.config/selfie/state.db or similar).
- Following hexagonal architecture, the state store should be behind a trait/port (e.g., RunHistoryProvider).
- Record: package name, operation type (check/install/audit), timestamp, result (success/failure).
- Display in info command: 'Last checked: 3 days ago', 'Last installed: 2 weeks ago'.
- Display in list command: optional column or indicator for staleness.
- Consider a --stale flag for list to filter packages not checked within N days.
- The MCP server should also be able to query this data.

title: Detect package manager availability before install
description:
Before running install/check/audit commands, detect whether the package manager binary (e.g., brew, npm, apt) referenced in the command actually exists on the system. Surface this as an early warning in info and list output rather than waiting for a cryptic command-not-found error at install time.

The codebase already has an is_command_available function using the which crate. This feature would parse the first token of install/check/audit commands to identify the binary, then check availability.

Implementation considerations:
- Parse the first token of each command string to extract the binary name. Handle pipes (use the first command), shell wrappers, etc.
- For list command, could show a warning indicator next to packages whose commands reference unavailable binaries.
- For info command, show per-environment binary availability.
- Emit via PackageEvent for frontend-agnostic rendering.
- Performance: which lookups are fast, but cache results since many packages may use the same binary (e.g., dozens of brew packages).

title: Install progress step count is wrong when dependencies are already installed
description: When running 'selfie package install', the total step count is calculated assuming every dependency needs full installation (fetch + env check + check + install command + verify). But dependencies that are already installed skip the install/verify steps, so the final count ends up lower than the total (e.g., '21/29 steps' when the operation is complete). The ProgressTracker total should be adjusted as dependencies are skipped, or the calculation should account for already-installed deps.
close_reason: ProgressTracker::reduce_total_steps(4) called when package already installed, correcting inflated step count

title: config validate checks post-override config, not on-disk file
description: The 'config validate' command validates config.selfie_config() after CLI overrides have been applied. This can mask problems in the on-disk config file (e.g., an invalid package_directory that becomes valid only due to a CLI flag override). Consider loading the raw file config inside this handler and validating that instead of the already-overridden CliConfig.
close_reason: handle_validate re-loads raw config from disk via YamlLoader instead of validating post-override config

title: handle_install returns was_already_installed=false for root package
description: handle_install in service/install.rs always returns OperationSuccess::package_installed(..., was_already_installed = false, executable_path = None) for the root package, even if the root was already installed. This loses information and can cause the CLI to report the wrong final status for no-op installs. Should track the root package's actual install result and use that when returning the final OperationResult.
close_reason: handle_install now returns the actual root package result instead of hardcoded was_already_installed=false

title: Fix verbose mode parity for check command
description: P3: install.rs forwards Progress events to default handler when verbose (returns false), but check.rs always suppresses Progress events (returns true) even in verbose mode. Users who set --verbose expect more output. check should forward Progress events to the default handler when verbose, matching install behavior.
close_reason: Implemented in commit a8ac5ff on feat/cli-display-consistency branch

title: Standardize indentation levels across output
description: P3: Three different indentation levels carry overlapping meanings. print_progress uses 2 spaces, print_field uses 2 spaces, check/validate format_key_fn uses 3 spaces, OperationHandle::add_output_line uses 2 spaces + │. Same visual concept (nested content / key-value pairs) uses different alignment. Pick one indentation for nested content and standardize.
close_reason: INDENT constant standardizes key-value indentation

title: Fix symbol semantic mismatches
description: P3: Two places use symbols with wrong semantics. 1) remove.rs:43 — print_info('✓ Package is not a dependency...') embeds success ✓ inside blue info message; should use print_success. 2) check.rs:106 — '⚠️ Check failed' uses warning symbol for a failure; symbol system says ✗ = failure, ⚠ = warning.
close_reason: Fixed print_info→print_success in remove.rs:48

title: Route static output through MultiProgress when spinners active
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: DisplayManager's static output methods (print_info, print_error, etc.) currently use raw println\!/eprintln\! which will interleave with active spinners. When spinners are wired into more commands, these need to route through self.mp.println()/self.mp.suspend() to avoid visual corruption. Also remove #[allow(dead_code)] from the mp field and EventProcessor::display() accessor when used.
close_reason: Static output routed through MultiProgress

title: Wire ErrorCollector into event processing
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: use DisplayManager::collect_error() and ErrorDetail to accumulate structured errors during multi-package operations, then print a copy-pasteable error summary at the end via DisplayManager::finish(). Currently ErrorDetail, ErrorCollector, collect_error(), and has_errors() exist but are unused (#[allow(dead_code)]). Remove the annotations when wired up. The EventProcessor already calls display.finish() after processing.
close_reason: JoinError metadata fix and ErrorCollector wiring implemented

title: Wire spinners into install/check/validate commands
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: use DisplayManager::start_operation() and OperationHandle for animated spinners in install, check, and validate commands. Currently these commands use static print_progress() calls. The spinner infrastructure (start_operation, finish_success/failure/warning, OperationHandle) exists but is only used by the list command. Remove #[allow(dead_code)] from start_operation(), OperationHandle struct/impl, and the non-in-place finish methods when wired up.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-v5a, resolved in same commit

title: Graceful shutdown with tokio::signal — use existing PackageEvent::Canceled
description:
Implement Ctrl+C (SIGINT) handling using tokio::signal::ctrl_c() (already have tokio as a dependency — no new crate needed).

Current state: No signal handling exists. Ctrl+C during install orphans subprocesses. process::exit() is called in main.rs without cleanup. The PackageEvent::Canceled event type already exists in the event system but is never emitted by service code. The event processor already handles it (sets exit_code=1, prints warning).

Key changes needed:
- main.rs: Wrap dispatch_command in tokio::select! with ctrl_c() signal
- service.rs: Accept a CancellationToken (from tokio_util) or similar mechanism to propagate cancellation to spawned tasks
- shell.rs: On cancellation, kill running subprocess via child.kill().await and emit Canceled event

Note: spawned tasks currently use tokio::spawn() without retaining JoinHandle — this pattern needs adjustment for clean shutdown.

Depends on: Nothing, but this is the largest of the 5 items.
close_reason: Implemented graceful Ctrl+C shutdown with CancellationToken threaded through service and command runner layers

title: Add strum crate — derive Display/FromStr for enums
description:
Replace 10 hand-written impl Display for ... blocks with #[derive(strum::Display)].

Targets:
- event/metadata.rs: OperationType (7 match arms)
- event.rs: StepCount, OperationFailure, CommandFailure, DependencyFailure, OperationSuccess, CheckResult, ValidationStatus
- commands/runner.rs: OutputChunk
- validation.rs: ValidationErrorCategory (6 match arms)

Note: Some Display impls have complex formatting (e.g., CommandFailure includes exit code). strum supports #[strum(to_string = "...")] for simple cases but complex multi-field formatting should stay hand-written. Assess each impl individually.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add semver crate — replace hand-rolled version regex (may drop regex)
description:
Replace regex::Regex::new(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+") in package/validate.rs:164-167 with semver::Version::parse().

Behavior change: Current regex is permissive — 1.2.3xyz passes, pre-release like 1.2.3-beta passes. semver::Version::parse() is stricter (proper semver spec). This is the correct behavior for a version validation warning. Note the validation produces a warning, not an error, so stricter is fine.

Bonus: regex is used nowhere else in the codebase. Adopting semver lets us drop regex entirely (heavy transitive deps: regex-automata, regex-syntax, aho-corasick).

Maintained by dtolnay. Used by Cargo itself.
close_reason: Replaced regex with semver crate for version validation

title: Make selfie crate re-exports consistent
description: Several public types in the selfie crate are not re-exported from their parent modules, forcing consumers to use deep paths like selfie::fs::filesystem::FileSystemError instead of selfie::fs::FileSystemError. Audit all pub mod/pub use in the selfie crate and add re-exports so that commonly-used types are accessible from the module they logically belong to (e.g., fs::FileSystemError, package::event::error::StreamedError). This improves ergonomics for CLI and future consumer crates.
close_reason: Added pub use re-exports in event.rs, config.rs, fs.rs, and package.rs. Updated all CLI imports and doc examples to use shorter paths. Code reviewed and all issues fixed.

title: Fix 3 failing package_list_tests integration tests
description:
Three integration tests in crates/cli/tests/package_list_tests.rs are failing due to assertion mismatches on display formatting:

1. test_package_list_all_flag_not_relevant_status - expects 'No check' but gets 'N/A'
2. test_package_list_default_behavior_filters_by_environment - expects 'No check' but gets 'N/A'
3. test_package_list_environment_mismatch_shows_stats - expects 'No packages found for environment' but output format differs

These are pre-existing failures unrelated to the EventStream unification work.
close_reason: Fixed both bugs: status None vs NoCheckCommand, and environment_stats computed before filtering

title: Dual file-discovery code paths in YamlPackageRepository
description: YamlPackageRepository has two separate code paths for finding .yml/.yaml files: find_package_files (on the trait) uses path_exists twice, while find_package_files_with_context (internal, used by get_package) uses list_directory. The logic for resolving .yml vs .yaml extensions exists twice and should be unified — one should call the other.
close_reason: Unified in commit 1fb4df4: extracted filter_matching_packages as shared pure function, both find_package_files and find_package_files_with_context now use it.

title: Consider 'which' crate for command availability checks
description: ShellCommandRunner::is_command_available spawns a shell process to run 'command -v'. The 'which' crate can do this natively without spawning a process — faster and avoids shell-related edge cases. Would also eliminate the default timeout wait (60s) for simple availability checks.
close_reason: Replaced shell-based is_command_available with which crate for native PATH lookup

title: PackageParseError::FileSystemError erases source error to String
description: PackageParseError::FileSystemError converts the source FileSystemError to a String (source_message: String), losing the error chain. Other error types in the codebase preserve #[source] for proper error chain propagation. This variant should store the original error or at least an Arc<FileSystemError> to maintain the chain.
close_reason: Replaced source_message: String with #[source] source: Arc<FileSystemError> to preserve error chain

title: Package pub(crate) fields accessed inconsistently — direct access vs accessors
description: Package has pub(crate) fields with accessor methods, but internal code inconsistently uses direct field access (e.g., package.name, package.environments) vs the public accessor methods (e.g., package.name(), package.environments()). Should standardize to always use accessors, then tighten field visibility.
close_reason: GetPackage fields are now pub(crate) with consistent accessor methods; CLI uses accessors everywhere

title: Emoji handling inconsistent — install.rs hard-codes emoji outside TerminalProgressReporter
description: Most emoji/styling goes through TerminalProgressReporter, but install.rs hard-codes 📦 and 🔧 directly in InstallationDisplay::add_output_line. All emoji should be handled consistently through TerminalProgressReporter to respect --no-color and terminal capability detection.
close_reason: Routed all emoji in install.rs through TerminalProgressReporter with proper console::Emoji fallbacks and use_colors support

title: Replace unsafe NonZeroU64::new_unchecked with safe const
description: config.rs:50 and config.rs:64 use unsafe { NonZeroU64::new_unchecked(60) } and unsafe { NonZeroUsize::new_unchecked(4) } for compile-time constants. Since Rust 1.83, these can be replaced with safe const blocks: const { NonZeroU64::new(60).unwrap() } which fails at compile time if zero is passed. No reason to use unsafe here.
close_reason: Replaced unsafe NonZero with safe const blocks

title: Fix typos: ApplyToConfg and SUGGESTION_EJOJI
description: Two naming typos in the codebase: (1) ApplyToConfg trait in config/loader.rs is missing an 'i' — should be ApplyToConfig. Used in loader.rs, main.rs, and cli/config.rs. (2) SUGGESTION_EJOJI constant in terminal_progress_reporter.rs should be SUGGESTION_EMOJI.
close_reason: Renamed ApplyToConfg→ApplyToConfig (4 files) and SUGGESTION_EJOJI→SUGGESTION_EMOJI (1 file). All checks pass.

title: Extract handle_missing_environment to steps.rs (DRY)
description: handle_missing_environment is duplicated verbatim in check.rs:123 and install.rs:328. The error construction and event sending are identical; only the return type differs. This should be extracted to steps.rs as a shared function.
close_reason: Extracted handle_missing_environment to steps.rs with generic <T>, removed Box::new+deref anti-pattern in handle_missing_check_command, made function sync instead of needlessly async

title: Address verbose/use_colors in library AppConfig
description: AppConfig contains verbose and use_colors fields which are purely presentation concerns -- the library doesn't use them for any logic. They exist solely so the CLI can read them back out after loading config. Options: (1) split into CoreConfig + UI config, (2) document that these are consumed by UI layers. Either way, clarify the boundary for v1.
close_reason: Split AppConfig into SelfieConfig (library) and CliConfig (CLI). Library no longer contains verbose/use_colors. Config file supports sectioned format with cli: section.

title: Unify PackageService method return types
description: Some service methods return EventStream directly (check, install) while others return Result<EventStream, PackageError> (info, validate, list, create). The Result wrapper on the latter group adds nothing since the inner call never fails -- they all wrap with Ok(self.execute_operation_with_deps(...)). Pick one approach for API consistency before v1.
close_reason: Already implemented — all PackageService methods now uniformly return EventStream directly

title: The apply-path unknown-key warning picks its level a frame away from the keys
description:
`handle_apply` (dotfile_service/service.rs:1278) renders the keys it gets from `Package::shadowing_top_level_keys()` with `describe_unknown_key_in::<PackageField>`, but the level is chosen twice in two places:

- `shadowing_top_level_keys` filters with `shadows_field::<PackageField>` internally, in package.rs.
- the caller names `PackageField` again to build the message.

Nothing ties the two together across the call frame, so changing the level inside `shadowing_top_level_keys` would leave this message explaining those keys against a different level. Same wrong-list class PR #123 closed inside a single walk, one frame up.

PR #123 introduced `unknown_key<F>` so a site names its level once. That does not reach here, because the producing function and the describing call are in different modules.

Candidate fix: have `shadowing_top_level_keys` return keys already carrying their level -- the `UnknownKey` PR #123 added, or an iterator of them -- so the caller has nothing to choose. That changes the function's contract, which is why it was left out of #123 rather than folded in.

Not reachable as a user-visible defect today: both sides say `PackageField`, and they agree. This is about the pairing, not a current miswording.

Found by review of PR #123 (its finding 15), deliberately skipped there as outside that diff.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #134

title: selfie track emits the missing-dotfiles-directory warning twice on the ExistingPackage path
description:
Found by the config-diagnostics unit final reviewer, by tracing rather than by test — the path is interactive and unreachable under piped stdio.

    track.rs:59  -> dotfiles_repository (common.rs:99) -> common.rs:113 print_warning   [emission 1]
    track.rs:84  -> handle_track_for_package (common.rs:274)
                 -> create_dotfile_service (common.rs:281)
                 -> dotfiles_repository (common.rs:170) -> common.rs:113 print_warning  [emission 2]

Same function, same argument, same DisplayManager. print_warning (display_manager.rs:314) holds no state, so nothing suppresses the second.

The NewStandalone branch is fine: require_dotfiles_dir (common.rs:254) refuses and returns before create_dotfile_service, so that path genuinely escalates warning -> refusal, which is intended.

EMISSION 1 MUST STAY. find_existing_tracker can return at track.rs:63 without ever reaching a service, and without the repository it can miss that a file is already tracked — so dropping the early warning would lose it exactly where it matters.

THE FIX IS EMISSION 2. handle_track already holds the repository built at line 59; the second emission exists only because handle_track_for_package rebuilds the service from scratch. Threading the already-built Option<YamlPackageRepository<..>> into a create_dotfile_service variant removes it with no new test machinery. create_dotfile_service has several other callers, so it is a real if modest refactor — which is why it was accepted rather than fixed in a unit that had already grown three times.

WHY IT IS NOT TESTABLE TODAY: the property is "how many times a renderer is called", and the unit-level test that exists constrains "what three pure functions return" — a different property, not a weaker version of the same one. The repo does have emission-counting machinery (dotfiles_directory_tests.rs:265 asserts count() == 1 against the real binary); the obstacle is that FuzzySelect returns Cancelled under piped stdio, so the interactive branch is unreachable without a pty harness this repo has nowhere else.

Cosmetic in effect — the user gets correct information twice, not wrong information once — which is why it is P4.
close_reason:
Filed in error by the team lead. The defect was real when the final reviewer traced it, at a74a75d/95d5fa1, and was already fixed one commit later in 5ea87c3 (now 6ffa511 lineage) — the reviewer was reading a superseded tree and I filed from its report without re-checking the tip.

Verified at the branch tip: missing_dotfiles_dir_warning has exactly ONE production caller, crates/cli/src/commands/common.rs:122, inside dotfiles_repository, guarded by

    let already_reported = MISSING_DOTFILES_DIR_REPORTED.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    if missing_dir_is_worth_reporting(configured_dotfiles_directory(), already_reported) { ... }

Both call sites in the original trace route through that emitter, so the second is silent: track.rs:59 swaps false and warns; track.rs:84 -> handle_track_for_package -> create_dotfile_service -> dotfiles_repository swaps true and stays silent.

The fix is once-per-RUN rather than a targeted refactor of create_dotfile_service, which also covers any future site that builds the service twice. The decision is a pure function so both properties are unit-testable without a filesystem or a terminal; a mutation dropping the already_reported term fails the named test.

Recorded because the reasoning is worth keeping: the correct observation that print_warning holds no state was true of the old tree. The state now lives in the caller rather than the renderer.

title: build_cli_config lets --environment "" override a valid config-file value
description:
Found by the config-diagnostics unit final reviewer. Pre-existing; belongs to the flag-precedence area rather than that unit.

crates/cli/src/config.rs:313 applies the --environment flag unconditionally when it is Some, so an empty string silently overrides a perfectly good value from the config file:

    config.yaml:  environment: macos
    selfie --environment "" package list
    -> runs with environment "", reports every package as not relevant

The asymmetry is the tell: config_from_flags — added by the flags-only bootstrap work — correctly treats an empty flag as missing, because a run with no config file has nothing to fall back to and the emptiness is immediately fatal. build_cli_config does not, because there IS a value to fall back to, and it overrides it anyway.

Only reachable when a config file exists, which is why the flags-only path is unaffected.

Same shape applies to --package-directory "". SelfieConfig::validate catches an empty environment, but it only runs under config validate, which validates the on-disk file and applies no flags — so it cannot see this.

Fix: treat an empty string as absent in build_cli_config, matching config_from_flags. The two functions should agree about what "supplied" means.

title: spec list doubles the package path for a YAML parse failure
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr round-2 code reviewer. Pre-existing on main, untouched by that branch.

crates/cli/src/commands/spec/list.rs:88-96 renders an invalid package as:

    Invalid: {path} — {error}

For PackageParseError::YamlParse, {error} is already "YAML parsing error reading package file `{path}`: ..." (crates/selfie/src/package/port.rs:389). So the path is printed twice:

    Invalid: /pkgs/bad.yml — YAML parsing error reading package file `/pkgs/bad.yml`: ...

"package list" avoids this: crates/cli/src/commands/package/list.rs:214 calls clean_error_message, which strips the self-named prefix. "spec list" has no equivalent.

SAME CLASS as the defect skipped_spec_warning was written to fix in selfie-h2kr — which handled it by matching on the variant rather than string-stripping: YamlParse/IoError/FileSystemError self-name and get no prefix; IrregularFile/RefusedFile do not self-name and get one. That approach is strictly better than clean_error_message, which string-matches one variants #[error] format and silently stops working if that attribute is reworded (see the bead on stringly-typed control flow in package list).

So the fix is not to give spec list its own clean_error_message. It is to decide once, for all render sites, who names the path — and skipped_spec_warning already demonstrates the shape.

Render sites to reconcile: cli/src/commands/spec/list.rs:88, cli/src/commands/package/list.rs:214 (clean_error_message), and the InvalidPackageInfo builders at selfie/src/package/service/list.rs:201 and service/spec_common.rs:124, which are the only verbatim-identical pair in the family.

title: PackageParseError::FileSystemError passes a FileSystemError through verbatim and would double the path
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr unit author, self-auditing work the reviewer had not covered. Unreachable today; filed rather than fixed, deliberately.

PackageParseError::FileSystemError renders as:

    File system error reading package file `{path}`: {source}

and passes the inner FileSystemError through verbatim. If the source is a refusal variant rather than an IO error, the result is:

    Skipping package: File system error reading package file `/x/ghost.yml`: /x/ghost.yml: target resolves to a socket and selfie will not write to it

Path named twice, and a WRITE refusal rendered on a READ path. Identical to the defect fixed on RefusedFile during that unit review; this is the last PackageParseError variant that still forwards a FileSystemError without destructuring it.

WHY IT CANNOT HAPPEN TODAY, verified rather than assumed:
- RealFileSystem::read_file (crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:112) only ever returns FileSystemError::IoError.
- IoError renders as "IO error: {0}" (crates/selfie/src/fs/filesystem.rs:265) and names no path.
- The only production constructor of PackageParseError::FileSystemError is crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:120, wrapping exactly what read_file returned.
- The irregular-file guard routes refusals to PackageParseError::RefusedFile, so a refusal never reaches this variant.

Reproducing the bad output required hand-building a state the code cannot produce.

TWO WAYS IT BECOMES REAL: a future FileSystem::read_file implementation returning a refusal variant, or a mock in a future test doing so. The guard is the same one RefusedFile got — destructure and re-word rather than forwarding the inner error.

WORTH TAKING WITH IT: the unit author wrote a property test that constructs all five PackageParseError variants and asserts the path appears EXACTLY ONCE in the resulting skipped-spec warning — zero would leave a user unable to tell which spec was skipped, two is the duplication the variant matching exists to prevent. It is the only check that would catch a future variant being filed in the wrong half of skipped_spec_warning`s match. That test should land with this fix.

title: A history rewrite can make just check report a compile error that does not exist
description:
Hit by the selfie-h2kr unit author; recorded so the next person does not spend the same time on it.

SYMPTOM: "just check" fails with

    cannot find function skipped_spec_warning in module selfie::package::service

while the function is right there, pub, in an ungated module. "cargo test -p selfie-mcp" passes and "cargo test --workspace" fails on IDENTICAL SOURCE.

CAUSE: a stale build artifact. "git reset --soft <sha>" followed by a recommit leaves file mtimes OLDER than a cached rlib built before the change. Cargos staleness check compares mtimes, sees nothing newer, and links the old rlib. A "touch" on the file clears it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE INCIDENT: this repos rules already say to verify in a "git archive" copy with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, and the stated reason is that another agent may be editing the shared tree. This is the same rule biting from a direction nobody wrote down -- YOUR OWN target directory, after YOUR OWN history rewrite, with nobody else involved.

The unit author nearly reported it as a real defect in the code.

.claude/rules/testing.md already documents the neighbouring case for mutation harnesses: "a batched mutation runner that writes a file and invokes cargo within the same second can hit cargos mtime staleness check and test a stale binary". The history-rewrite variant is the same mechanism and is not mentioned.

CANDIDATE ACTIONS: add a sentence to testing.md covering rewrite-induced staleness; or note it beside the pre-commit checklist in CLAUDE.md, since "just check" is what fails; or have the rebase workflow touch the rewritten paths. Cheapest correct thing is probably documentation, since the fix is one "touch" once you know.

Related: selfie-w4di (no gate keeps Justfile recipes in sync with ci.yml).

title: A tab-indentation parse error reports only 'not valid YAML' when the parser knew exactly what was wrong
description:
Recorded during selfie-flka so the option is not lost. Deliberately NOT fixed there.

selfie-flka's ParseFailure refuses to forward any parser-supplied String into a user-facing message, because in a deploy-state file the mapping keys are dotfile source paths and serde-saphyr interpolates content into several message formatters. Every Location-only variant got its own named kind; everything carrying a String stays in the content-free catch-all.

Tab indentation is one of the String cases. Probe output:

    tab-indent  [ExternalMessage]  tabs disallowed within this context (block indentation)

ExternalMessage.msg is supplied by the parser. So the user is told 'the file is not valid YAML at line 2, column 2' for a condition the parser had already diagnosed precisely. Same for the other ExternalMessage cases and for Message, AliasError and HookError.

THE TRADE, stated so nobody re-litigates it cheaply: recovering that wording means forwarding a parser-controlled String on the egress path, which is the single invariant the selfie-flka design exists to hold. ExternalMessage is also the variant whose text is most likely to churn between serde-saphyr releases, so it is the one whose content is hardest to reason about — a 0.0.x bump could start interpolating something new into it with no signal.

IF THIS IS EVER REVISITED, the prerequisite is a probe over the full set of scanner/parser messages ExternalMessage can carry, establishing that none interpolates input. That probe does not exist; the selfie-flka author declined to recommend the change without it, correctly.

Cheaper alternative worth considering first: match on the specific scanner conditions selfie cares about (tabs, indentation) and emit selfie's OWN static wording for them, rather than forwarding the parser's. That keeps the invariant and recovers the diagnostic for the cases that actually occur.

Related: selfie-eg1s (promote the reachability probe into the repo), which would be the natural home for the scanner-message probe too.

title: cargo doc warns about an output filename collision between the selfie bin and the selfie lib
description:
Noticed by the selfie-h2kr unit author while verifying its doc gate; confirmed pre-existing.

Every run of the CI docs command emits:

    warning: output filename collision.
    ... doc/selfie/index.html

The bin target 'selfie' in selfie-cli and the lib target 'selfie' produce the same output path. This is cargo's warning, not rustdoc's, so RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" does not govern it and the command still exits 0 — CI's docs job passes.

Harmless today. Filing it because it costs every author the same few minutes: it appears in a gate they were told to run, it names the crate they are working in, and deciding whether it is theirs requires knowing that RUSTDOCFLAGS does not cover cargo's own warnings. One author on the specs-and-config batch chased it to rust-lang/cargo#6313 before concluding it was pre-existing.

Options: rename one target, restrict the doc command's targets, or document the warning as expected next to the docs command in CLAUDE.md so nobody investigates it twice.

title: get_package reads every spec file twice on the success path
description:
Found by the selfie-h2kr plan author.

YamlPackageRepository::get_package calls get_file_size (crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:208), which reads the WHOLE file via read_file solely to report file_size_bytes on the error path, and then calls load_package_from_file (:211), which reads it again.

So every successful get_package does two full reads of the same file. get_file_size's result is only consumed when reporting a failure.

Fix by taking the size from the content already read, or from a stat rather than a read. Note selfie-h2kr routes both readers through a single guarded read_spec_file, which makes this cheap to fold in afterwards — the two call sites become one function.

title: A provider command's own stdout notices are deployed as dotfile content on first deploy
description:
Split out of selfie-gwb6 when that bead's premise was found stale. This is the narrow part that survives.

PR #86 fenced the LOGIN PROFILE out of provider stdout (crates/selfie/src/commands/shell/content.rs:43 points stdout at /dev/null before the login shell execs), and capture_warnings (dotfile_service/resolve.rs:362, called on both the Provider and vars branches) reports foreign bytes that reach the content channel anyway.

What remains unguarded is contamination inside the command's OWN stdout — an 'op' update notice, a --verbose echo, a tool's deprecation warning written to stdout rather than stderr. No fence can separate it: by every mechanical test available it IS the command's output.

The damage window is narrow, which is why this is P4:

- Target exists and DIFFERS -> settle_conflict (dotfile_service/service.rs:917) reports and skips; auto_accept is deliberately not consulted. The user sees secret_conflict_summary (service.rs:591), which publishes line counts of both sides.
- Target exists and MATCHES -> in sync, nothing at risk.
- Target ABSENT -> service.rs:923 returns Ok and the write runs with no shape diagnostic at all.

So destroying an existing dotfile already requires a conflict prompt. The uncovered cases are a first deploy to an absent target, and an accepted conflict.

REJECTED APPROACHES (analyzed under selfie-gwb6; do not re-propose without new argument):
- Leading/trailing whitespace as banner evidence — whole files legitimately start and end with blank lines, and 'op read' commonly appends a newline. High false-positive rate.
- Parsing against the target's apparent format — most dotfiles are not machine-parseable, fragments fail, and parser errors quote the input, which is a leak on secret-bearing content.
- A second invocation to detect nondeterminism — doubles side effects on an audit-logged read, doubles the credential in memory, and false-positives on every correct rotating provider (TOTP, short-lived tokens).
- A control command — obsoleted by the #86 fence; would fire on any machine with a chatty profile.

THE ONE CANDIDATE WITH A ZERO-FALSE-POSITIVE STORY is an opt-in declared shape: an enum field (not a String, not a bool) on a whole-file 'command:' entry stating what correct output looks like, refusing on mismatch. Refusing rather than warning is consistent with ResolveError::EmptyOutput and TooLarge, which are both whole-file gates that refuse. A declared shape is the package author's statement of intent, not selfie guessing, so the standing 'proceed but say what you ignored' rule does not apply.

Deferred because it adds a package-schema field, validation, MCP spec-tool plumbing and docs for a check most users will never declare. Revisit if provider-sourced dotfiles see real use and this actually bites. If implemented: a trailing newline MUST be tolerated or every 'op read' entry breaks, and the mismatch error may name the command, the declared shape and a LINE COUNT, never the bytes.

title: save_package canonicalizes the path it just wrote before handing it to dprint
description:
Found by the Unit 4 plan reviewer. VERIFIED at 9fc9f05: save_package canonicalizes the file it has just written and passes the resolved path to a best-effort 'dprint fmt'.

Two things worth separating, because only one is a real concern:

1. THE CANONICALIZE. .claude/rules/secrets.md is emphatic that canonicalization on a write path forfeits the guarantee exactly when it SUCCEEDS -- canonicalize resolves the link and hands the caller the destination, so a writer sees an ordinary file. Here it is not a writer, it is an argument to a subprocess, and it runs AFTER a guarded write, so nothing is currently exploitable. But it is a canonicalize-then-act on a path selfie composed, in a file whose rules forbid the pattern on write paths, and the reasoning for why it is safe here exists nowhere.

2. THE UNSYNCED REWRITE, which is new as of Unit 4. Unit 4 makes save_package use write_file_no_follow, which will fsync the file it writes. dprint then rewrites that file WITHOUT a sync, so the durability the fsync just bought for a package YAML is immediately voided. Not a correctness bug -- a package spec is regenerable from the user's edit -- but it makes the durability claim false for this one caller, and Unit 4's own doc comment has to say so.

Fix directions: pass the un-canonicalized path to dprint if it works (it should -- dprint takes a path argument and does its own resolution), which removes the pattern entirely; or document at the call site why canonicalizing is safe HERE and why the rules-file prohibition does not apply. Prefer the first: a rule with an undocumented exception is a rule people route around.

Check selfie-h6co, which tracks whether save_package should shell out to dprint from inside the library at all -- if that is resolved by removing the call, this bead disappears with it.
acceptance_criteria: save_package either does not canonicalize before invoking dprint, or the exception to secrets.md's canonicalize prohibition is documented at the call site -- and Unit 4's durability doc names the dprint rewrite as voiding it for package YAML.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #127

title: test_known_fields_matches_package_struct checks only one direction
description:
Found by the Unit 3 plan reviewer. VERIFIED at cc8e1f8.

crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:1821-1826 has one loop:

    for key in raw.keys() {
        assert!(KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS.contains(&key.as_str()), ...)
    }

It catches a Package field missing FROM the list. It cannot catch a name IN the list with no matching struct field.

The dotfile equivalent (crates/selfie/src/package.rs:1270-1276) has the second loop:

    for known in KNOWN_DOTFILE_FIELDS {
        assert!(seen.contains(*known), 'KNOWN_DOTFILE_FIELDS lists ... but no fixture emits it; the list or the fixtures are stale')
    }

So the package guard is strictly weaker than the dotfile one, in the same codebase, for the same purpose.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is filed rather than left as tidiness: KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS deliberately EXCLUDES 'target' so that the documented '_target: &target' YAML anchor stays legal at the top level (docs/package-files.md). Adding 'target' to that list would compile, pass every test, and silently kill the anchor.

Unit 3 (selfie-g199) considered adding the reverse loop and DEFERRED it here, because its M2 mutation plus the '_target: &target' control test already enforce the 'target' case specifically in CI. That is enough for g199's acceptance and it is genuinely enforced — but it enforces ONE entry rather than the invariant, so any future name added to KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS with no struct field behind it is still undetected.

Fix: add the mirror loop, matching the dotfile guard's message shape. Small, and it converts one enforced case into an enforced rule.
acceptance_criteria: test_known_fields_matches_package_struct checks both directions, as the dotfile equivalent does.
notes:
CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, PR #92 code reviewer: adding "target" to KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS and running the suite does NOT fail test_known_fields_matches_package_struct. It fails four OTHER tests — including a_top_level_anchor_is_refused_only_when_it_shadows_a_package_field and a_top_level_anchor_that_shadows_nothing_is_left_alone — which are hand-written controls for the '_target: &target' anchor specifically.

So the position after PR #92 is: the 'target' entry is defended, by controls that bite in CI. The LIST is not. A wrongly-added '_source' or '_command' would go undetected, because nothing checks the reverse direction and no control exists for those names.

That is the difference between an enforced case and an enforced rule, and it is why this bead stays open after g199 shipped.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #121

title: write_file_no_follow reports IO failures without naming the path
description:
Found by the Unit 3 plan reviewer. VERIFIED: crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:120's io_err is a bare wrap:

    FileSystemError::IoError(Arc::new(e))

while write_file_private's target_err (real.rs:60-65) re-tags the error with the path it was writing. So every non-refusal write failure on the repository-file path — ENOSPC, EACCES, EROFS — surfaces as an errno naming nothing, where the same failure on the secret path names the file.

Consequence: 'selfie apply' reports 'No space left on device (os error 28)' with no indication of which of N dotfiles it was writing.

Unit 3 fixes the fifo case specifically, by classifying an ENXIO failed-open into FileSystemError::IrregularTarget (which does carry the path). This bead is the general case that classification does not cover.

Same asymmetry-between-two-writers shape as selfie-yezt (whether the two dotfile writers should keep diverging on symlinks) — worth reading that bead before deciding, since the answer may be 'converge the two writers' rather than 'patch one'.
acceptance_criteria: A write failure from write_file_no_follow names the target path, as write_file_private's already does.

title: The deploy-state locate failure names no path and does not say what to fix
description:
Reported by the Unit 2 code reviewer against cb6401a.

load_deploy_state's three warning branches are deliberately worded to distinguish their conditions, but they are not symmetric. The read and parse branches name the file:

  Cannot read deploy state '/path/deploy-state.yml': ...
  Cannot parse deploy state '/path/deploy-state.yml': ...

The locate branch cannot, because it fires precisely when the path could not be resolved:

  Cannot locate the deploy state file: <error>; continuing as though nothing had been deployed

That much is unavoidable. The gap is that the message also does not say what WOULD fix it. The branch is reachable only when state_directory is unset AND the home directory cannot be determined (fs/target.rs:355-381), so the actionable advice is specific and short: set state_directory in the config, or fix HOME. The message gives the user neither.

Minor, and the condition is rare. Filed because the whole point of the selfie-y8ub work was that selfie must say what it ignored -- and this is the one branch where it says what it ignored without saying what to do about it.

Note for whoever takes it: the integration-test helper state_warnings filters on 'deploy-state.yml', so it would not observe this branch. If you add integration coverage, the helper needs widening too.
acceptance_criteria: The locate-failure warning names the actionable fix (set state_directory, or fix HOME) rather than only the failure.

title: save_deploy_state reports a serialization bug as a filesystem IO error
acceptance_criteria: A serialization failure in save_deploy_state is reported as a serialization failure, not as an IO error.
notes:
ADJACENT ASYMMETRY, from the Unit 2 code reviewer (cb6401a): 'Failed to save deploy state: {e}' (service.rs:1468) relies on write_file_private re-tagging the error with the path in order to name the file at all. Its load-side siblings name the file explicitly in the message text.

So the save path has two message defects, not one: the error TYPE is wrong for a serialization failure (this bead), and the message only names its file by borrowing the path from a lower layer's error. Both are cosmetic today. Worth fixing together, since anyone re-typing the error will be editing the same lines.

title: DotfileTracked.source_path carries the target path on the already-tracked branch
description:
Reported by the Unit 1 author during commit c67a986; pre-existing and untouched by that diff.

On the already-tracked branch of handle_track_for_package (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs), OperationSuccess::DotfileTracked is constructed with source_path set to the expanded TARGET path rather than to the repository copy location the field names.

No observable effect today: no consumer reads it. Neither the CLI Display impl nor the MCP server surfaces source_path on this variant, which is why it has gone unnoticed.

Same class as the closed selfie-13bq and selfie-u36f -- a field carrying a value that does not mean what its name says, invisible because nothing reads it. Both of those resolved by DELETING the field rather than correcting it, on the argument that a value nothing reads cannot be trusted to be right when someone finally reads it. That precedent is the first thing to weigh here: either populate it correctly, or drop it from this variant.

selfie-fbr1 (P4, open) is the closely related bead -- 'track's already-tracked short-circuit reports the target as source_path'. CHECK WHETHER THIS IS A DUPLICATE OF selfie-fbr1 BEFORE WORKING IT; if so, close this one against that and carry any detail across.
acceptance_criteria: DotfileTracked.source_path either holds the repository copy location on every branch, or is removed from the variant -- or this is closed as a duplicate of selfie-fbr1.
close_reason:
Duplicate of selfie-fbr1, confirmed on creation. Both describe handle_track_for_package's already-tracked short-circuit emitting OperationSuccess::DotfileTracked with source_path set to the deploy target instead of the repository copy location.

selfie-fbr1 is the better bead and is the one to work: it names the consequence this one missed. The CLI prints source_path as prose so the effect is cosmetic there, but crates/mcp-server serializes OperationSuccess into the JSON an AI assistant reads -- so an assistant that tracks an already-tracked dotfile is told the source is a path that is not the source, and any reasoning it does about where the file lives is wrong.

Nothing to carry across; fbr1 is a superset. Filed independently by the Unit 1 author during c67a986, which is corroboration rather than new information.

title: selfie track scans the package directory twice on every invocation
description:
VERIFIED at 4ef9c05. crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs:183-209, find_existing_tracker, builds a YamlPackageRepository over BOTH the package directory and the dotfiles directory and calls list_packages() on each, walking every package file and parsing it, purely to answer 'is this file already tracked anywhere'.

handle_track then proceeds to create_package_repository(config) (track.rs:48) and the library handler loads the repository again. So an interactive 'selfie track <file>' parses the whole package directory twice.

Cost scales with the number of package specs, and this is the interactive path a user runs one file at a time while converting an existing dotfile setup -- exactly the workload where it is most noticeable.

Not urgent and not a correctness problem. Filed so it is not rediscovered. Note the overlap with selfie-63yd, which proposes changing what find_existing_tracker does with its result: if that bead moves the already-tracked check into the library, this scan disappears as a side effect rather than needing its own fix. Check that bead before working this one.

Found by the Unit 1 plan reviewer (second reviewer).
acceptance_criteria: An interactive 'selfie track' parses the package directory once, or the second scan is documented as deliberate.

title: portable_target re-expands a target the track handlers already expanded
description:
VERIFIED at 4ef9c05. Both track handlers expand the caller's target once, then portable_target (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1594 in handle_track_standalone, :1734 in handle_track_for_package) expands the same string a second time to decide what to record in the spec.

Cheap today -- expand_target_path touches no filesystem beyond HomeDir::home() -- so this is not a performance bead. It is a divergence risk: two independent expansions of the same string, and any rule that lands on one and not the other makes the recorded target disagree with the checked one.

That risk is live rather than hypothetical. Unit 1 (selfie-jlum/q9t3/hkhb/m5dv) introduces deploy_target, a checked expansion that refuses '~user/...' and non-absolute targets, and wires it into the FIRST expansion at both handlers. The second expansion inside portable_target keeps calling plain expand_target_path. Today that is harmless because the first call already refused anything the second would mishandle -- the guard sits ahead of it. It stops being harmless the moment someone reorders the guard, adds a rule to only one site, or lifts portable_target to a path that is not preceded by the guard.

selfie-h15 (PR #89) established what track records: a target relative to home. selfie-u36f (closed 2026-07-31) is the record of what went wrong the LAST time two paths recorded a target in two formats -- apply recorded expanded, track recorded raw, and the field had to be deleted rather than reconciled. This is the same shape one layer down.

Fix direction: thread the already-expanded TargetPath into portable_target instead of re-expanding the &str, so there is one expansion per track call and the recorded target is provably derived from the checked one. Confirm the signature change does not force expand_target_path to become fallible -- Unit 1 deliberately kept it infallible because four call sites expand targets they are not going to write to (service.rs:1396, service.rs:1662, cli/src/commands/track.rs:185 and :203).

Found by the Unit 1 plan reviewer. Deliberately NOT folded into Unit 1: it changes no behavior today, and the unit is already at five call sites.
acceptance_criteria: A track call expands its target once, and the value recorded in the spec is derived from the same expansion the target rule checked -- or the double expansion is documented as deliberate with the reason.

title: track's already-tracked short-circuit reports the target as source_path
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1662 -- handle_track_for_package's idempotent short-circuit emits:

  OperationSuccess::DotfileTracked { source_path: <the expanded TARGET>, ... }

so the already-tracked path reports a different field's value than the real tracking path does. On a fresh track, source_path is the file copied into the dotfiles repository; on a repeat track, it is the deploy target.

Cosmetic in the CLI, which prints it as prose. Not cosmetic for MCP: crates/mcp-server serializes OperationSuccess into the JSON an AI assistant reads, so an assistant that tracks an already-tracked dotfile is told the source is a path that is not the source. An assistant reasoning about where a file lives would be misled.

Pre-existing -- the field held the expanded target before selfie-zv4b's type change and holds the same bytes after (expanded_target.path().to_path_buf()). Not introduced by that unit and deliberately not fixed in it.

Fix direction: report the actual source path, which the short-circuit already knows from the matched entry, or omit the field on the idempotent path if the API allows. Check what the CLI and the MCP tool description each promise the field means before changing it.

Found by the selfie-zv4b author while editing the surrounding lines.

title: Validate-time portability check needs a home-directory port decision
description:
selfie-h15 makes track record '~/...' instead of an expanded absolute path. It deliberately does NOT add a check for hand-written specs that already contain an absolute path under $HOME -- those are non-portable but nothing tells the user.

The maintainer's call (2026-07-31) was to skip that check: the corpus is 8 dotfile entries, all already '~/', so it would fire zero times today, and it would fire on every apply and drift run until a spec were fixed. The failure was in the tooling, which h15 fixes directly.

Filing the blocker in case it is ever wanted, because it is not a small change:

Package::validate(&self, current_env: &str) is a PURE OFFLINE CHECK with no filesystem and no $HOME -- crates/selfie/src/package/service/validate.rs:22-24 says so explicitly -- and PackageServiceImpl holds no FileSystem either. So a validate-time portability check needs either a signature change at ~22 call sites or a new PackageRepository port method to supply the home directory.

That is a port-design question, not a lint. If it is ever taken up, the question to answer first is whether Package::validate should be able to see the filesystem at all -- it is currently pure by design, and the purity is worth something.

The cheap alternative, if the check is wanted without the port change: emit it at the three runtime guards in dotfile_service/service.rs, which already have both the filesystem and the raw and expanded paths in scope. Three lines each, zero plumbing, but it fires on every run rather than on validate.

Raised by the selfie-h15 plan author.

title: Consider command-fds to replace the outer shell wrapper in content capture
description:
selfie-evf9's content capture spawns /bin/sh -c 'exec 8>&1 1>/dev/null; exec $SHELL -l -c $RECIPE'. The outer shell exists only to put the redirect in place before the login shell's profile runs, so anything the profile backgrounds inherits /dev/null instead of the capture pipe.

command-fds (google/command-fds, 0.3.3, released 2026-04-10, ~1.1M recent downloads, edition 2024) passes arbitrary file descriptors to a child. Tokio support is UPSTREAM: Cargo.toml has tokio = ['dep:tokio'] and src/tokio.rs implements CommandFdExt for tokio::process::Command. Do NOT use the tokio-command-fds fork -- single release June 2022, ~6k lifetime downloads, dead.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY: Rust spawns $SHELL -l -c <recipe> directly with .stdout(Stdio::null()) plus fd_mappings(pipe_write -> 8). That deletes content::wrapper(), SHELL_VAR, COMMAND_VAR, and the env-var smuggling of shell and recipe -- roughly 20 of content.rs's 183 non-test lines. The real gain is QUOTING SURFACE: the "$SELFIE_CONTENT_CMD" indirection exists only because the recipe must survive a second shell's parsing.

WHY IT IS NOT AS BIG A WIN AS IT LOOKS, verified against the crate's source rather than its README:
1. It saves NO process. The current wrapper's two execs chain -- /bin/sh BECOMES the login shell. There is no extra process today.
2. The markers and the fish special case both stay. command-fds replaces separation-by-source only; the recipe still does 'exec >&8', so the shell can still write to the capture fd after the command. Separation-by-position is untouched.
3. It costs Rust pipe plumbing. Today the capture channel IS child.stdout, so run_buffered reads it with no new code. With fd_mappings you create the pipe yourself (std::io::pipe(), stable), wrap the read end in tokio::net::unix::pipe::Receiver::from_owned_fd -- WHICH NEEDS TOKIO'S 'net' FEATURE, not currently enabled -- and MUST DROP THE PARENT'S WRITE END AFTER SPAWN OR THE READ NEVER SEES EOF. That last one is the same class of footgun that produced selfie-ql8m; Stdio::piped() handles it for you and a hand-rolled pipe does not. run_buffered also grows a third reader parameter.
4. It introduces the project's first pre_exec. fd_mappings calls Command::pre_exec (inherently unsafe) and map_fds uses nix::dup2_raw. The dep's code is careful and documents the no-allocation-in-pre_exec constraint (src/lib.rs:168), but selfie's path has zero unsafe today, and adding a pre_exec hook moves std off its posix_spawn fast path onto fork+exec.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the env_remove calls for SHELLOPTS and BASH_XTRACEFD could be dropped afterwards. They are documented as protecting the OUTER shell, but both plausibly still affect the inner bash. Needs a real bash test, not doc reading.

RECOMMENDATION: file, do not do now. Weight it UP if the shell-quoting layer ever causes a bug; weight it DOWN because of the pre_exec. This is 'a different factoring with a different cost profile', not 'you reimplemented what the runtime provides'.

Raised by the maintainer asking whether content.rs reinvents a wheel; researched against crate sources.

title: apply and drift name different reasons for the same rejected entry
description:
handle_apply checks is_within before target-absoluteness (service.rs:1227, then :1242). handle_check_drift checks them in the opposite order (service.rs:1538, then :1551).

For an entry that fails BOTH -- a source escaping the package directory and a target that is not absolute -- apply reports 'source path escapes YAML base directory' while drift reports 'target path ... is not absolute'. Same entry, same defect, two different explanations depending on which command the user ran.

Both suppress the entry either way, so nothing is deployed wrongly and no guard is weaker than it looks. Cosmetic, but it costs a user who runs one command, fixes what it named, and then gets a different complaint from the other.

Pre-existing and not symlink-specific; found while verifying drift/apply parity for the symlinked-target unit, which confirmed the symlink refusal itself has no such divergence.

Fix: run the two guards in the same order in both functions, or factor the pair into one helper both call. The second is better -- it is the same 'two sites must agree' shape that produced selfie-6ou1 and the refusal_warning helper.

title: ksh93 reports success on a provider command with an unterminated quote
description:
Of six shells tested, ksh93 (AT&T 93u+) alone recovers from an unterminated quote in a -c string, returns rc=0, and produces the recovered text as output.

Measured with a provider command containing an unbalanced quote:
  sh / dash / bash  -> rc=2, empty content, error path
  zsh               -> parse failure, fails closed
  ksh93             -> rc=0, content 'unbalanced'

So a malformed dotfile provider command deploys garbage as content and reports success, for a user whose $SHELL is ksh. Every other shell fails closed.

Pre-existing and independent of selfie-evf9's fence -- identical behavior unfenced. Found while attacking that fence with malformed commands.

Low priority: it needs a malformed command in the user's own package file, and ksh specifically. Filed because it is the one shell of six where a syntax error in a credential-producing command does not fail closed, and because a reader comparing shells would reasonably assume they all behave alike.

title: track_for_package reports success for a symlinked target that is already tracked
description:
handle_track_for_package's already-tracked short-circuit returns Success(DotfileTracked{was_already_tracked: true}) and writes nothing -- correct, and unit A deliberately leaves it alone rather than refusing an idempotent no-op.

But it means one path stays silent about a symlinked target after that unit lands. The defense offered was 'the right place to tell that user is drift', and that is only true once the repo file moves: in the stow-migrated state where the destination content still matches, drift reports drift_count=0 and is also silent. So a user who runs track and then drift is told nothing by either command.

Benign today -- nothing is actually wrong yet, and both commands speak the moment anything changes. Filing because it is the one remaining silent path in that family, and because 'drift covers it' is not quite true.

Fix direction, if taken at all: the short-circuit could stat the target and warn without refusing, since it is not writing anything. Weigh against noise on a genuine no-op.

Found by the unit-A plan reviewer.

title: Decide whether dated design specs are immutable records or living docs
description:
docs/superpowers/specs/ holds dated design documents, e.g. 2026-03-18-environment-manager-design.md. There is no stated convention for what happens when the code catches up with or diverges from one.

Concretely: that spec's line 245 says 'The MCP server already uses login_shell() ... The CLI should do the same for install/check/audit.' That was already satisfied on main before the current work -- create_package_service has used login_shell all along -- so the spec now reads as an open recommendation for something already done. selfie-w8gd makes it doubly satisfied.

Two coherent positions:
- IMMUTABLE RECORD (recommended by the U3 plan reviewer, and by the lead): a dated spec captures what was believed and intended ON THAT DATE. Editing the body destroys the only thing it is for. If traceability is wanted, add a one-line 'Status:' header at the top pointing at the PR that satisfied it, and never touch the body.
- LIVING DOC: keep it current, in which case the date in the filename is misleading and should go.

Worth deciding once and recording in CLAUDE.md, because the question will recur every time a spec's recommendation lands -- and in the absence of a rule, each agent or contributor guesses, and some will silently rewrite a historical record.

Raised during U3 of the command-execution batch, where an author asked the lead for a ruling and got one ad hoc.

title: The MCP sync tools return two different error JSON shapes for the same concept
bound()'s public doc links to the private BOUNDED_END_BYTES
description:
cargo doc --no-deps -p selfie emits:

  warning: public documentation for `bound` links to private item `BOUNDED_END_BYTES`

Introduced by 2cc584b (PR #78, the head+tail change). BoundedText::bound is public and its doc references BOUNDED_END_BYTES, which is private. Took the crate's private_intra_doc_links warning count from 6 to 7.

Cosmetic: cargo doc is not a CI gate, so nothing fails. But it degrades the rendered docs — the link does not resolve for an external reader, which is exactly the reader the public doc is for.

Three ways out:
  - Drop the link, name the constant in plain text ('half the bound').
  - Make BOUNDED_END_BYTES pub(crate) -> pub. Rejected by the same reasoning that keeps MAX_BOUNDED_BYTES pub(crate): exporting the number pins it as API for no caller that needs it.
  - Restate the doc in terms of MAX_BOUNDED_BYTES, which the reader can already see referenced.

The first is probably right, and cheapest.

Caught by re-deriving the doc-warning baseline against merged main rather than reusing an earlier count. Worth noting the near-miss: comparing counts alone would have shown 7 vs 7 between the base and PR #79's branch and looked clean, because the new warning was already in the base by then.
acceptance_criteria: cargo doc --no-deps -p selfie emits no warning naming BOUNDED_END_BYTES.

title: Streamed chunks can differ from full_output by replacement characters, not only by drops
description:
shell.rs:476 renders each streamed chunk with String::from_utf8_lossy while full_output retains the raw bytes. A multi-byte character split across the 1024-byte read boundary therefore reaches the channel as U+FFFD replacement characters, while the returned CommandOutput holds the correct bytes.

So the streamed view and the buffered view can disagree in two independent ways: dropped chunks (selfie-qd3r) and lossy boundary splits (this). Both are silent.

Pre-existing, not introduced by selfie-3hap -- that branch documents the channel as best-effort and the documentation stays true, since 'the returned CommandOutput holds all of it' is correct in both cases. This is about the streamed side being wrong in a second way nobody has written down.

Low priority: it needs multi-byte output crossing a 1024-byte boundary, and the authoritative copy is unaffected. Worth fixing if the streaming path ever becomes the source of truth for anything.

Consider fixing alongside selfie-qd3r, since both concern the gap between what is streamed and what is returned.

Found by selfie-3hap's independent final reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: Streamed output is not silently lossy at read boundaries, or the difference is documented.

title: resolve.rs justifies a Display-not-Debug rule by citing a variant that never occurs
description:
